title: Gradland: On Phenomenal Experience, Differentiated Across Many Dimensions

title: Valerant: An Automatic Navigable Game Map Generator via Action-Conditioned World Model Exploration

title: XAI-Arena: Can LLMs Assess the Quality of XAI Explanations?

title: Do Agents Know When They Succeed? Calibrating Agent Confidence from Internal Representations
summary: This research investigates methods for calibrating agent confidence from their internal representations, which is crucial for agentic systems deployed in safety-critical applications. It aims to address complex failure modes in agentic workflows.

title: ContractEval: Query-Conditioned Execution Matching for Procedural Instruction Conformance
summary: This paper introduces ContractEval, a method for query-conditioned execution matching to evaluate the procedural instruction conformance of LLM agents. It addresses the challenge of identifying subtle failures in agents performing multi-step procedures.

title: Multi-Agent Agentic Graph Learning via Structural Signatures
summary: This research explores Multi-Agent Agentic Graph Learning, where agents powered by large language models (LLMs) perform graph reasoning tasks by sequentially sampling graph evidence. It discusses methods for orchestrating multiple agents in this context.

title: CityPlanner: A Sandbox Agent for Executable Urban Planning
summary: This paper introduces CityPlanner, a sandbox agent designed for executable urban planning, addressing real-world spatial optimization problems. The agent aims to select feasible actions from large candidate spaces to meet practical objectives like cost and service quality.

title: A Function-Space Approach to the Statistical Mechanics of Learning Dynamics
summary: This research develops a statistical-mechanical description of learning dynamics in deep neural networks, approaching it directly in function space. It aims to explain the macroscopic behavior of neural networks despite their complex parameter dynamics.

title: From State Synchronization to Cognitive Self-Evolution: An Operational Architecture for Cognitive Digital Twins
summary: This paper proposes an operational architecture for Cognitive Digital Twins (CDTs), which extend traditional Digital Twin systems by incorporating cognitive capabilities for task-oriented and knowledge-driven operations. title: Procedural Memory Under Change: Reuse and Interference in Controlled Web Tasks
summary: This study investigates procedural memory in language agents under changing conditions, focusing on the reuse and interference of successful routines in controlled web tasks. It examines how agents adapt when stored routines are no longer applicable.

title: Proof-Carrying Cognition: Closing the Verification Gap with Reality-Settled Reward
summary: This paper proposes 'Proof-Carrying Cognition' to address the 'verification gap' in language-model reasoning, which limits scalable and incorruptible rewards for reasoning outside formal domains. It discusses advancing language model capabilities through reinforcement learning.

title: The Era by Eon Benchmark: A Generated Enterprise Estate with Exact Ground Truth for Benchmarking LLM Agents
summary: This introduces the Era by Eon Benchmark, a generated enterprise estate with exact ground truth designed to evaluate LLM agents that interact with enterprise tools, addressing the challenge of evaluating agents on production data.

summary: This research proposes a method for grounded evaluation and repair of Large Language Models (LLMs) when translating Natural Language planning descriptions into PDDL problem instances, addressing limitations of current evaluation criteria.

title: RAP: Research Attention Prediction Reveals Target-Conditioned Evidence Acquisition Biases
summary: This paper introduces Research Attention Prediction (RAP), a rolling benchmark designed to evaluate how Large Language Models, acting as research agents, track shifts in research attention and reveal target-conditioned evidence acquisition biases.

title: Agent-Based ML-LLM Fusion with Self-Optimizing Prompts for Plateau Weather Alerts

title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
summary: This paper presents kernel-managed shared memory, a system-level abstraction designed for multi-agent AI systems to enable system-wide personalization by allowing specialized agents to share structured, tagged memory.

title: Beyond Surface Imitation: Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment in Multimodal In-Context Learning
summary: This research introduces Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment to improve multimodal in-context learning in MLLMs, moving beyond surface-level imitation to enhance reasoning capabilities.

title: Why Sample What You Can Enumerate? Exact Policy Optimization for Genomic Tool Selection
summary: This paper proposes an exact policy optimization method for genomic tool selection, arguing against sampling when the complete tool-subset space is enumerable in specialist scientific reinforcement learning settings.

title: TRACE: Training Reasoning Agents for Causal Exploration with Synthesized Rewards
summary: TRACE is a method for training reasoning agents for causal exploration using synthesized rewards, aiming to advance diagnostic reasoning over complex data where objective answers are difficult to verify.

title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
summary: This research proposes a framework to guide language models in geometric reasoning by integrating symbolic perception with logical deduction, addressing challenges in plane geometry.

title: Cyber-Financial Contagion: Modeling the Propagation of an AI Vendor Compromise Through the Banking System

title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
summary: This research introduces Fortunate Recall, an ontology-driven memory lifecycle management system for LLMs, designed to maintain persistent coherence by strategically managing which memories persist, are replaced, and at what rate.

title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
summary: Introduces ConvMem, a convolutional memory approach to extend the effective context window for Large Language Models by iteratively updating a fixed-size memory based on text segments. This method aims to improve long-context reasoning for LLMs.

title: Quantifying Logical Consistency in Transformers via Query-Key Alignment
summary: This research paper proposes a method to quantify the logical consistency of Transformer-based Large Language Models using Query-Key Alignment. It aims to address challenges in multi-step logical reasoning within LLMs.

title: Characterizing Text Branch Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Segmentation via Evidence Decoupling

title: Reliability-Aware Hybrid-K Ensemble Selection for Cervical Cytology Classification: Integrating Discrimination, Calibration, and Selective Prediction

title: M3-Former: Multimodal Transformer with Mixture-of-Experts for Long-Term Vessel Trajectory Prediction

title: Halo: Improving forecast accuracy through heteroscedastic estimation

title: Zero-shot rib design: merging training-free generative prior with topology optimization

title: Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for the Detection of Pathologies Related to Lung Cancer through Image Analysis using Convolutional Neural Networks and Data Augmentation: a systematic mapping of the literature

title: GEOSTEER: Geodesic Optimization for Activation Steering in Large Language Models
summary: Introduces GEOSTEER, a method using geodesic optimization for activation steering in Large Language Models to control their behavior. It aims to modify hidden activations during inference without altering the activation norm, reducing representation collapse risk.

title: Adaptive Margin Ordinal Loss: Penalizing Center-Class Hedging in Ordinal Classification

title: Counterfactual Marginalisation: Framework for Evaluating Robustness to Nuisance Variables
summary: This paper proposes Counterfactual Marginalisation, a test-time evaluation procedure for assessing the robustness of classification models to nuisance variables. It aims to identify models that rely on demographic or acquisition-related shortcuts, despite strong test performance.

title: From Connectivity to Rewards: Dense Reward Learning with Directed State Graphs
summary: This paper introduces Dense Reward Learning with Directed State Graphs to enhance Goal-Conditioned Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning. It leverages intrinsic connectivity information in graphs to address challenges in task hierarchies and effective subgoal sampling.

title: RiVaT-Fuse: Reliability-Calibrated Variational Tensor Fusion for Multimodal Prediction under Modality Uncertainty
summary: This paper introduces RiVaT-Fuse, a method for multimodal prediction that fuses heterogeneous evidence by calibrating reliability under modality uncertainty for tasks like image-metadata prediction.

title: Certifying Lower Bounds for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning under Adversarial State Perturbations
summary: This research proposes certification methods to establish lower bounds for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning, enhancing robustness against adversarial state perturbations in safety-critical applications.

title: Story Imprinting: AI Assistants Absorb Traits from Human Characters They Resemble
summary: This study investigates how finetuning AI assistants, such as language models, on synthetic stories can influence their character and behavior in multi-turn conversations with users.

title: Measuring the Value of World-Model Updates: A Counterfactual Utility Protocol for Continual Adaptation
summary: This research proposes a counterfactual utility protocol to measure the true value of individual updates in continual world models, addressing how to determine if new data justifies changing the model.

title: EGGROLL, Unrolled: Understanding and Improving Low-Rank Evolution Strategies at Scale

title: Topological Necessities: Mechanism-Invariant Strategic Subgoals for Cross-Embodiment Goal-Conditioned Control
summary: This research explores topological necessities for mechanism-invariant strategic subgoals in cross-embodiment goal-conditioned control, proposing a novel approach for long-horizon reinforcement learning.

title: T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: This paper introduces T1, a 122B Mixture-of-Experts model trained with reinforcement learning, designed to operate as a terminal agent in a cloud sandbox for long-horizon tasks like coding and scientific discovery.

title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression

title: The information geometry of large language models is shared, learned, and controllable
summary: This paper investigates the information geometry of large language models, using Fisher-Rao geometry to understand shared behaviors, learning processes, and how to controllably modify specific aspects without affecting others.

title: Beyond Solver Verdicts: Generative Reward Models for Autoformalization

title: Phase-Decoupled, Model-Calibrated Power Control for Disaggregated LLM Serving
summary: This paper introduces phase-decoupled, model-calibrated power control to optimize energy efficiency for disaggregated large language model serving, addressing GPU power constraints in datacenters and evaluating NVIDIA's Max-Q profile.

title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes a method using large language models with bidirectional multimodal fusion of sky images and time-series data for improved short-term solar forecasting of photovoltaic power and global horizontal irradiance.

title: LILA: Calibration-Free Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Latent Spectral Geometry
summary: This paper introduces LILA (Latent-Informed Layer Analysis), a calibration-free method for structured pruning of large language models that scores neuron importance via latent spectral geometry to achieve hardware-efficient compression.

title: When does a spectral prior help graph learning? Connectivity-loss estimation under road-network disruptions
summary: This research investigates the utility of spectral priors in graph learning for estimating connectivity loss in road networks after multi-edge deletion, using graph neural networks to learn bounded corrections.

title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving
summary: This paper introduces REVA (Reusable Evidence View Aggregation), a method designed to improve context efficiency in RAG serving by compressing retrieved documents, thereby reducing latency and memory costs for knowledge-intensive LLM applications.

title: Legible Failures: Detecting and Repairing In-Context Binding Errors
summary: This research investigates legible failures in language models, focusing on detecting and repairing in-context binding errors by analyzing whether models fail to use information they hold versus lacking it entirely.

title: Polyhedral Geometry of Time-to-First-Spike Neural Networks
summary: This paper studies the expressivity of spiking neural networks, focusing on the time-to-first-spike model, using polyhedral geometry to understand their asynchronous and event-driven computational capabilities.

title: MUtE: A Dual Framework for Concept Erasure and Counterfactual Interventions
summary: This paper introduces MUtE, a dual framework for concept erasure and counterfactual interventions, designed to remove concept-specific information from representations to mitigate bias and improve model interpretability.

title: A Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model for Traffic Flow Prediction
summary: This research introduces a Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model designed for traffic flow prediction, aiming to improve future traffic dynamics inference and resource allocation efficiency in intelligent transportation systems.

title: Reification as a Transferable Vocabulary: Zero-Shot Link Prediction with Vanilla GNNs
summary: This research proposes a novel method for zero-shot link prediction in knowledge graphs by reifying the input graph, enhancing transferability for vanilla Graph Neural Networks.

title: Prevalence Determines Precision:Silent Contamination in Detector-Defined Datasets
summary: This paper analyzes how dataset precision in machine learning is influenced by true-positive prevalence in detector-defined datasets, highlighting silent contamination via Bayes' theorem.

title: Combining Synthetic and Real Data for Low-Resource Historical OCR: A Manchu Case Study
summary: This research explores combining synthetic and real data to improve Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for low-resource historical Manchu texts, an endangered language.

title: Generalized Score Matching for Parameter Estimation on Convex Domains
summary: This paper introduces generalized score matching as a tractable method for parameter estimation on convex domains, addressing the challenges of maximum likelihood estimation for unnormalized probabilistic models.

title: Particle GFlowNets: Rethinking Generative Marginalization Models
summary: This paper introduces Particle GFlowNets, efficient neural sampling models for any-order autoregressive modeling of discrete distributions, enabling fast posterior evaluation by learning marginal and conditional probabilities.

title: LoaDiff: Conditional Generation of Electricity Consumption Time Series for Energy Analytics
summary: This research presents LoaDiff, a conditional diffusion model for generating electricity consumption time series, aiding energy analytics by understanding evolving residential usage patterns.

title: RDDMPI: Residual Denoising Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Multivariate Time Series Imputation
summary: This research introduces RDDMPI, a Residual Denoising Diffusion Model for probabilistic multivariate time series imputation, crucial for recovering missing values in interdependent temporal data.

title: Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training
summary: This paper proposes Musec (MomentUm SpEctral Clipping), a technique to enhance the stability of Muon optimizers during large language model training, addressing instability caused by spectral flattening.

title: Learnware and AI Model Management System
summary: This paper introduces the concepts of Learnware and AI Model Management Systems, advocating for a transition from simple model storage to managed AI model resources, analogous to database management.

title: Data-Efficient Language Modeling: From Frontier Advancement to Principle-Guided Model Improvement
summary: This research details an autonomous program on data-efficient language modeling, focusing on how models learn from limited text to maintain capabilities and generalize effectively.

title: NCP-ArchPreview Technical Report: Moving towards Latent Space Language Models through Next Concept Prediction
summary: This technical report introduces NCP-ArchPreview, a latent-space language model that advances autoregressive pretraining beyond standard next-token prediction by incorporating Next Concept Prediction (NCP).

title: CMNIE: An Information Extraction Benchmark for Chinese Military News
summary: This paper introduces CMNIE, a new information extraction benchmark specifically designed for structured extraction of events, arguments, entities, and relations from Chinese military news.

title: Think Before You Link: Rarity, Reasoning, and Retrieval in Multilingual Entity Linking
summary: This research investigates challenges in multilingual entity linking, especially for rare entities, proposing new knowledge-graph structural metrics beyond popularity to assess rarity and improve systems.

title: Multilingual in Name Only? Cultural and Linguistic Weaknesses of LLMs in Urdu
summary: This research analyzes the cultural and linguistic weaknesses of multilingual large language models when generating text in low-resource languages, using Urdu as a case study.

title: Analyzing Traditional and Neural Approaches to Multilingual Readability Assessment
summary: This paper analyzes and compares traditional and neural approaches, specifically transformer-based models, for multilingual readability assessment, considering their linguistic properties and performance.

title: Larger Context Window, Fewer Overcorrections: Optimizing Prompts and Batching for Minimal-Edit Grammatical Error Correction
summary: This research investigates optimizing LLM prompts and batching strategies, leveraging larger context windows to reduce overcorrections in minimal-edit Grammatical Error Correction.

title: Detectable Only Where It Is Confounded: What Verified Duplication Counts Say About Membership Evidence in Language Models
summary: This paper explores how prediction cost relates to membership evidence in language models, investigating whether unusually low prediction cost indicates a sentence was part of the training data.

title: Does Linguistic Structure Enrichment Enhance Coherence Assessment? Not With Current Architectures
summary: This research investigates whether enriching linguistic structure enhances coherence assessment in large language models, concluding that current architectures do not benefit from this approach.

title: LLM-Anchored Paralinguistic Enrichment for Alzheimer's Disease Detection
summary: This research explores using LLM-anchored paralinguistic enrichment to enhance speech-based automatic detection of Alzheimer's disease by analyzing atypical pauses and word elongations.

title: SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs
summary: This paper introduces SearchAtlas and Evidential Query Graphs to analyze the strategies of LLM search agents, focusing on how they retrieve and utilize credible evidence.

title: Auto-RecSys: Harnessing Autonomous Research Agents for Industry-Scale Recommender System
summary: This paper introduces Auto-RecSys, which uses autonomous research agents to automate hypothesis generation, experiment execution, and iterative refinement for industry-scale recommender systems, addressing challenges like long feedback loops.

title: Structurally Speaking: Motif-Oriented Graph Captioning through Bidirectional Graph-Text Translation
summary: This research proposes a motif-oriented graph captioning method that translates graph structures into textual descriptions, abstracting connectivity into recognizable patterns like hubs, paths, and cycles.

title: Using Semantic Uncertainty to Estimate Transition Relevance in Turn-taking
summary: This research investigates using semantic uncertainty to estimate transition relevance in turn-taking within Spoken Dialogue Systems, aiming to improve the timing of responses by anticipating appropriate speaking opportunities.

title: Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Modalities via Semantic-aware Completeness based Reconstruction
summary: This paper presents a robust multimodal sentiment analysis method that handles incomplete or noisy modalities by employing semantic-aware completeness-based reconstruction to prevent performance degradation.

title: Distribution-aware Language Neuron Identification in Multilingual Large Language Models
summary: This research focuses on identifying distribution-aware language neurons in multilingual large language models, studying how specific feed-forward neurons are sensitive to particular languages within the model's architecture.

title: Rethinking Verbalized Confidence for LLM-as-a-Judge: A Compatibility Shift on Post-2025 Proprietary Models
summary: This paper rethinks verbalized confidence as a robust soft-scoring mechanism for LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations, demonstrating its effectiveness on top-tier proprietary models across various benchmarks.

title: K/V-Cache Interventions Dissociate Representation Alignment from Persona Expression in Decoder-Only Language Models
summary: This research explores K/V-cache interventions to dissociate representation alignment from persona expression in decoder-only language models, demonstrating a structured surface for persona control in models like Llama-3.1-8B.

title: Rebalancing Token Importance in Language Models with TF-IDF Weighted Cross-Entropy Loss
summary: This paper proposes a TF-IDF weighted cross-entropy loss to rebalance token importance during language model training, aiming to prevent frequent, low-information tokens from dominating learning and reduce memorization.

title: When Noise Fabricates Bias: The Fragility of LLM-as-a-Judge Bias Measurement under Noisy Text
summary: This research investigates the fragility of LLM-as-a-Judge bias measurement, showing that surface noise in text, such as typos or informal spelling, can fabricate and affect the assessment of social bias.

title: ProMediConv: Benchmarking Proactive Conversational Agents in Legal Dispute Mediation
summary: This paper introduces ProMediConv, a benchmark for evaluating proactive conversational agents in legal dispute mediation, addressing limitations of existing LLM-based mediation research in task formulation and evaluation metrics.

title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers
summary: This item provides an overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11, which focuses on agent-based experiment reproduction from scientific papers, challenging LLM agents to automate scientific verification.

title: Rubric-Aligned Disentangled Evaluation of Human Simultaneous Interpreting
summary: This research focuses on developing an automatic, rubric-aligned, disentangled evaluation metric for human simultaneous interpreting, designed to assess meaning transfer, delivery quality, and temporal synchrony.

title: Can LLMs Normalize Databases? A Benchmark and Multi-Agent Framework for Schema Normalization
summary: This research explores whether LLMs can normalize databases, presenting a benchmark and a multi-agent framework to assess their reliability in satisfying database-level constraints for schema normalization.

title: FlexComp: One Model for Every Ratio in Context Compression
summary: FlexComp introduces a soft context compression technique that condenses context into memory tokens, allowing one model to handle various compression ratios dynamically, unlike existing methods that require separately trained models for each ratio.

title: Automated Identification of Competing Narratives in Political Discourse on Social Media
summary: This research focuses on the automated identification and analysis of competing narratives within political discourse on social media platforms, aiming to understand how public opinion is influenced by evolving narratives.

title: OmniHallu: Unified Hallucination Detection for Cross-Modal Comprehension and Generation in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: OmniHallu introduces a unified hallucination detection method for Multimodal Large Language Models, addressing the issue of generated outputs contradicting or misrepresenting input semantics across various tasks and modalities.

title: The Illusion of Balanced Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: Beyond the Limits of Optimization-Based Methods
summary: This paper critically analyzes the limitations of optimization-based methods in addressing modality imbalance in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis, proposing a unified evaluation framework to re-examine balancing strategies.

title: Automatic Lyric Transcription for Greek Songs: Scaling and Task Composition Effects in Whisper Adaptation
summary: This research investigates automatic lyric transcription for Greek songs, a challenging task due to melodic variability and low-resource language status, by adapting and evaluating the Whisper model.

title: MultiHuSE: A Multimodal Dataset for Humour Styles and Emotions
summary: MultiHuSE introduces a new multimodal dataset for studying humor styles and emotions, providing resources for computational recognition of verbal humor which requires understanding language, delivery, emotions, and cultural context.

title: E-CONAN (Entailment, CONtradition And Neutral) Benchmarks: Arabic Textual Entailment and Natural Inference Datasets
summary: E-CONAN introduces new benchmarks and datasets for Arabic Textual Entailment and Natural Language Inference, addressing the lack of resources for semantic relation extraction in Arabic.

title: On the Impact of Anonymization on the Performance of Large Language Models
summary: This paper studies the impact of anonymizing input data on the performance of large language models, a critical practice for privacy in sensitive domains. It presents a systematic empirical analysis of this effect.

title: SEAR: Segment-Evidence-Aware Routing for Weak-to-Strong Multilingual Speech MCQ
summary: This paper describes the SEAR system for the Multilingual Conversational Speech Language Model Challenge, adapting Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct for weak-to-strong multilingual speech Multiple Choice Question Answering. It details a segment-evidence-aware data and post-training pipeline.

title: TransClean: A Benchmark for Detecting and Extracting Clean Translations from Large Language Model Outputs
summary: This paper introduces TransClean, a new benchmark designed to detect and extract clean translations from large language model outputs by addressing common issues like translation noise. It fills a gap in evaluating LLMs for machine translation.

title: SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations
summary: This paper introduces SWRouter, a new method for similarity-contractive window routing in multi-turn large language model conversations. It aims to dispatch queries to the most suitable LLM, improving upon single-turn routing methods for dialogue.

title: Cross-Lingual Clinical Annotation Projection as Constrained Text Generation: A Six-Language Study
summary: This study investigates whether cross-lingual clinical annotation projection can be framed as a text-preserving, document-level generative task for multilingual clinical corpus construction. It characterizes the robustness and computational aspects across six languages.

title: ReGround: Grounding Reviewer Comments in Multimodal Evidence
summary: This paper introduces ReGround, a new benchmark designed to ground reviewer comments in multimodal evidence within research papers. It addresses the challenge of connecting comments to specific content in long, multimodal documents.

title: Structural priors for data-efficient language learning
summary: This research investigates structural priors for data-efficient language learning, aiming to reduce reliance on large data and computational resources. It explores training models on non-language data to induce useful priors for natural language processing.

title: Complex-Text Robustness Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Low-Resource Multilingual Text-to-Speech
summary: This paper addresses the insufficient diagnosis of robustness in low-resource multilingual text-to-speech (TTS) systems when handling complex text inputs. It proposes methods for evaluation and failure diagnosis beyond standard test sentences.

title: A Training-Free, Alignment-Free Approach to Corporate Intelligence: Application to SEC Filings
summary: This paper presents a training-free and alignment-free approach to corporate intelligence, specifically applied to SEC filings. It aims to overcome limitations of high-dimensional dense text embeddings and large language models in financial analysis.

title: Structured Transforms for Low-Overhead Quantization of Language Models
summary: This paper proposes an improved algorithm for Kashin-decomposition-based weight quantization of large language models, featuring stronger convergence properties and structured, efficient orthogonal transforms. This method aims to reduce the overhead of language model deployment.

title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws
summary: This paper introduces Negative Self-Distillation, a new paradigm for large language model self-improvement. It enables models to learn reasoning by actively avoiding identified flaws, contrasting with traditional positive self-distillation.

title: The Eloquence submission for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge
summary: This paper details the Eloquence team's approach for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge, focusing on multilingual Multiple-Choice Question Answering. It describes methods including fine-tuning Voxtral-Mini-3B with LoRA.

title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation
summary: This paper introduces LOCUS, a method for task-aware low-rank post-training that aims to achieve token-efficient language generation in large language models. It investigates how post-training updates can influence output sequence length and serving costs.

title: RAG-Safety-Bench: Reliable Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Safety
summary: This paper introduces RAG-Safety-Bench, a new benchmark designed for reliable evaluation of safety in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) large language models. It aims to assess the unintended side effects of RAG on overall safety.

title: Component-Aware Differential Privacy for Federated Multilingual Speech-LLMs
summary: This paper proposes a component-aware differential privacy method for federated multilingual speech-LLMs, demonstrating that standard per-layer clipping is insufficient for these models. It aims to improve gradient fidelity in privacy-preserving training.

title: Recognizing Is Not Reversing: A Controlled Inversion Test of Fact-Preserving News Framing
summary: This paper investigates large language models' ability to analyze and rewrite news, specifically using a controlled inversion test to see if they can undo news framing while preserving factual content. It assesses their capabilities in complex text manipulation.

title: The widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research 2023 to 2026
summary: This paper highlights a widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research, observing that the rapid evolution of LLMs outpaces the slower development of clinical evidence for their assessment. It analyzes trends in medical AI research from 2023 to 2026.

title: Beyond Word Error Rate: A Switch Aware Evaluation of ASR and Audio Language Models on English Yoruba Code-Switched Speech
summary: This paper proposes a "switch aware evaluation" method for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and audio language models on English-Yoruba code-switched speech. It aims to move beyond traditional Word Error Rate for low-resource and diacritic-rich languages.

title: Target leakage, not model class, explains reported accuracy in survey-based cardiovascular screening: a leakage-tiered audit of glass-box and tabular foundation models
summary: This paper conducts a leakage-tiered audit of cardiovascular screening models, concluding that target leakage, rather than the model class, explains the reported high accuracy in survey-based systems. It assesses glass-box and tabular foundation models.

title: IndicTriMix: Developing Language Identification Datasets and Models for Tri-Language Code-Mixing
summary: This paper introduces IndicTriMix, a project focused on developing new datasets and models for language identification in tri-language code-mixed text. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying languages in utterances that switch between multiple languages.

title: Augustinian BabyLM: What Ostensive Definition Can and Cannot Teach a Small Language Model
summary: This research explores how a small masked language model (DeBERTa) learns word meanings through ostensive definition, simulating St. Augustine's learning picture.

title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
summary: This paper presents a multi-signal detection pipeline, combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification, Monte Carlo Dropout, and temperature-scaled calibration, to detect hallucinations in Large Language Models.

title: Nuha-Speech: Building General-Purpose Arabic Speech-LLMs
summary: Nuha-Speech is introduced as a comprehensive initiative to develop dedicated infrastructure for training and evaluating general-purpose Arabic Speech Large Language Models (speech-LLMs).

title: Distance generalization in transformers: why bother with positional encoding?
summary: This research investigates distance generalization in transformers, specifically focusing on their performance when inter-token distances change between training and inference, and the role of positional encoding.

title: AcFlow: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers via Learned Conditional Activation Flow
summary: AcFlow is introduced as an inference-time controller that manipulates intermediate layer activations to provide enhanced control over style intensity and concept suppression in text-to-image diffusion transformers.

title: MHE-Former: Multi-Hypothesis Transformers via Entropy Maximization for 3D Mesh Recovery
summary: MHE-Former is a new model using multi-hypothesis transformers and entropy maximization to address occlusion and ambiguity in monocular 3D hand and body mesh recovery, providing an exploration-exploitation paradigm.

title: Meta-Learning for Data-Efficient Plant Growth Estimation via Vision Transformers and Fuzzy Clustering
summary: This paper proposes a meta-learning, few-shot regression framework combining Vision Transformer embeddings and fuzzy clustering for data-efficient plant growth estimation in greenhouse monitoring.

title: GRADE: Single-Frame Generative Radar Depth Estimation Under Visual Degradation
summary: GRADE is a new generative model that estimates dense 3D depth from single-frame radar data, providing accurate perception even under visual degradations like smoke or fog where optical sensors fail.

title: Shedding Light: A Benchmark for Evaluating Lighting Understanding in Generative Image Models
summary: This paper introduces a new benchmark to evaluate how accurately generative image models understand and synthesize illumination, addressing the challenge of physical plausibility in image synthesis.

title: Two-Parameter Flow Map Learning for Continuous-Time Diffeomorphic Image Registration
summary: This research proposes a learning-based method using two-parameter flow maps to model autonomous ordinary differential equations for continuous-time diffeomorphic image registration in medical image analysis.

title: TrajFusionNet+: Transformer-Based Prediction of Pedestrian Crossing Intention via Fusion of Trajectory Representations and Scene Graphs
summary: TrajFusionNet+ is a novel transformer-based model that fuses trajectory representations and scene graphs to predict pedestrian crossing intention, specifically for autonomous vehicles.

title: Overpainting: Localized Context-aware Diffusion Image Editing
summary: Overpainting is presented as a new image editing operation for diffusion models that offers localized control over edits while maintaining awareness of the original content within the edited area.

title: BodyCam-VQA: Enhanced Body-Worn Camera Video Captioning via Multimodal Reasoning and Probe Question Generation
summary: This research introduces BodyCam-VQA, an enhanced method for body-worn camera video captioning that uses multimodal reasoning and probe question generation to improve data processing for law enforcement.

title: Evaluation of Vision-Language Models Across Diverse Coastal Environments
summary: This work evaluates the performance of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in diverse coastal environments for robotic perception, introducing a densely labeled coastal dataset for this purpose.

title: HiPerViT: A Hierarchical Perceiver-Vision Transformer Architecture for Multi-Scale Texture Recognition
summary: HiPerViT is a new hierarchical Perceiver-Vision Transformer architecture designed to improve multi-scale texture recognition by effectively capturing higher-order spatial statistics.

title: CamPilot: A Multi-Agent Cinematic Assistant for Camera-Controlled Movie Generation
summary: CamPilot is introduced as a multi-agent cinematic assistant that leverages large language models to provide camera-controlled movie generation, aiming for more professional filmmaking than standard text-to-video.

title: New Evidence, Same Choice: Testing Physical Experiment Selection in Vision Language Models
summary: This study tests how Vision Language Models select information and make choices when presented with new evidence in physical experiment scenarios, assessing their reasoning capabilities.

title: Toward Interpretable Multimodal Fusion: Heat Conduction Modeling for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Joint Classification
summary: This research explores a heat conduction modeling approach for interpretable multimodal fusion of hyperspectral and LiDAR data, aiming to enhance land-cover classification by better handling long-range dependencies.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Using VLMs to Reveal Systematic Classification Failures Under Real World Conditions
summary: This work explores using Vision Language Models to identify systematic classification failures in other models under real-world conditions, moving beyond traditional benchmarks for verification and validation.

title: ReconPlusGen: Injecting Reconstruction Prior into Multi-view 3D Generation through Noise Inversion and Modulation
summary: ReconPlusGen is a new method for multi-view 3D generation that injects reconstruction priors through noise inversion and modulation, improving the quality of generated 3D content from multiple input images.

title: LAION-Mobile: Evaluating Deepfake Detectors On One Million Smartphone Photos
summary: This paper evaluates deepfake detectors on one million smartphone photos, arguing that current benchmarks overlook the impact of modern smartphone photography and on-device AI processing.

title: A Multi-View and Confusion-Guided Ensemble Framework for Robust Synthetic Image Attribution
summary: This research proposes a multi-view and confusion-guided ensemble framework to robustly attribute the source model of generated synthetic images, addressing challenges from the increasing similarity among diffusion-based generators.

title: CEM-TUDASR: Computationally efficient multi-modality transformer based unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution approach
summary: This paper introduces CEM-TUDASR, a computationally efficient multi-modality transformer-based approach for unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution, to enhance low-resolution Wireless Capsule Endoscopy images.

title: HALDETECT at ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks: Answer-First Contrastive Grounding with QLoRA
summary: HALDETECT is presented as a system for the ImageEval 2026 shared task's English hallucination-detection track, employing answer-first contrastive grounding with QLoRA to identify hallucinated visual details in large multimodal models.

title: SCINTILLA-SNN: A Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network for Perineural Invasion Prediction
summary: This paper introduces SCINTILLA-SNN, a Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network designed to predict perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma by identifying subtle cues in MRI images.

title: From Evaluation to Enhancement: Benchmarking and Improving Think-with-Video Reasoning for Video Generative Models
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking and improving the 'think-with-video' reasoning abilities of video generative models, addressing limitations in existing benchmarks for evaluating symbolic rules and physical law adherence.

title: Uncertainty DMD: Restoring Diversity in Few-Step Autoregressive Video Distillation
summary: This paper introduces Uncertainty DMD, a method designed to restore diversity in few-step autoregressive video distillation, which often suffers from diversity collapse and weakened motion dynamics.

title: Improving Faint Object Detection for Space Situational Awareness with Variational Autoencoders
summary: This paper presents a deep-learning pipeline using Variational Autoencoders to improve the detection of faint moving objects in optical space situational awareness imagery by automating star removal and background reconstruction.

title: SAMV-DUSt3R: Instance-Centric 3D Scene Decoupling from Sparse Multi-Views
summary: This paper proposes SAMV-DUSt3R, an end-to-end model that integrates SAM2 2D masks into MV-DUSt3R reconstruction using a Cross Flow Mask Block to improve instance-centric 3D scene decoupling from sparse multi-views.

title: Your Model Already Knows Don't Teach It, Learn to Ask It: Soft Prompting for Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
summary: This research explores soft prompting for few-shot adaptation of Vision-Language Models in out-of-domain object detection, comparing it against existing methods like discrete prompt optimization and LoRA fine-tuning.

title: Mi-Ripple: Restoring Images Degraded by Iterative AI Editing
summary: This paper introduces Mi-Ripple, a diagnosis-guided restoration workflow designed to suppress 'digital ripple' – grid-like and granular textures – that degrade images from iterative AI editing, while preserving image structure.

title: Predictive Multi-Landmark OCT Tracking for Increased Motion Robustness
summary: This research introduces a predictive multi-landmark OCT tracking method aimed at increasing motion robustness, addressing limitations in trackable velocity for markerless motion tracking with optical coherence tomography.

title: R4Tun: LLM-guided adaptive segmental tunnel lining segmentation in point clouds
summary: This paper introduces R4Tun, an LLM-guided adaptation framework that enhances automated, adaptive segmentation of segmental tunnel linings from 3D point clouds for infrastructure inspection.

title: Vision Transformer-Based Multi-Level Feature Fusion for Multi-Label Sewer Defect Classification
summary: This study develops a Vision Transformer-based multi-level feature fusion method to improve the automated multi-label classification of sewer defects for infrastructure condition assessment.

title: Brain-PACE: A Deep Siamese MRI Framework for Modelling Longitudinal Brain Acceleration
summary: This research introduces Brain-PACE, a Deep Siamese MRI Framework designed to model longitudinal brain acceleration, aiming to improve brain age estimation and understanding of brain health trajectories.

title: DINO-Med: A Unified Patch-Based Adaptation Framework for Multi-Modal Medical Image Analysis Applied to Liver Fibrosis Staging
summary: This paper introduces DINO-Med, a unified patch-based framework for adapting natural-image foundation models like DINOv3 to multi-modal medical imaging, demonstrated on liver fibrosis staging.

title: Multi-Modal Controlled Coherent Motion Generation
summary: This research tackles multi-modal controlled coherent motion generation for 3D avatars, aiming to replicate natural human behaviors like walking and talking simultaneously using concurrent text and speech inputs.

title: BruNet: A Cross-Domain Transfer Framework for Bruise Segmentation
summary: This work proposes BruNet, a cross-domain transfer framework for bruise segmentation in medical imaging, combining a ViT-based visual encoder with self-supervised DINOv3 or pretrained LingBot-Vi.

title: BridgeMatch: Conditional Transport Bridges in Matching Matrix Space for 3D Deformable Registration
summary: This paper introduces BridgeMatch, a method using conditional transport bridges in matching matrix space to achieve reliable non-rigid point cloud correspondences for 3D deformable registration.

title: Pre- and Post-Treatment Brain Metastases Segmentation Using nnU-Net with Post-Processing for BraTS 2026
summary: This research presents a pragmatic pipeline for pre- and post-treatment brain metastases segmentation, based on a 5-fold nnU-Net with post-processing, developed for the BraTS 2026 Task 1.

title: FreeFlow: A Bias-free Hierarchical Transformer for Optical Flow Estimation
summary: Introduces "FreeFlow," a hierarchical Transformer model designed for bias-free optical flow estimation, aiming to overcome limitations of traditional methods by avoiding predefined heuristics.

title: UBone3D: Physics-Rectified Conditional Flow Matching for Anatomical 3D Shape Completion from Ultrasound
summary: Presents "UBone3D," a new method using physics-rectified conditional flow matching to complete anatomical 3D shapes from artifact-laden ultrasound point clouds.

title: Harnessing Intrinsic Subject-Aware Attention for Controllable Multi-Subject Video Generation
summary: Addresses challenges in multi-subject video generation by leveraging intrinsic subject-aware attention within Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) to improve control and prevent semantic drift.

title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization
summary: Introduces "LoopVAE," a new hierarchical visual tokenizer that reuses a scale- and loop-conditioned core across different spatial scales to improve computation efficiency.

title: Learning Interaction between Image and Layout Priors for Joint Image-Layout Generation in Design Templates
summary: Addresses graphic design template creation by proposing a method that learns the interaction between image and layout priors for joint image-layout generation from text input.

title: World in World: Explore the World with World Models
summary: Explores enhancing the flexible control of autoregressive video world models to enable interactive, long-horizon exploration from new viewpoints while maintaining synchronization with recorded events.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks for Melanoma Detection
summary: Conducts a comparative evaluation of pre-trained convolutional neural networks for early melanoma detection, addressing the clinical challenge of distinguishing melanoma from similar skin lesions.

title: Learn the Solid, Not the File: Canonical Inputs for Neural Networks on CAD Boundary Representations
summary: Investigates methods for creating canonical inputs for neural networks from CAD Boundary Representations (B-reps) to ensure consistent processing of geometrically identical 3D models despite varying file representations.

title: OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs
summary: Introduces "OmniKVQuant," a KV cache quantization method specifically for Omni-modal Large Language Models (Omni-LLMs) to reduce their high memory cost, adapting techniques previously used for text-only LLMs.

title: HuRo: Robotizing Human Videos for Scalable VLA Pretraining
summary: Introduces "HuRo," a method for robotizing human video datasets to enable scalable Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pretraining, bridging the embodiment gap between human and robot movements.

title: When Information is Worth the Risk: Behavioral Valuation for Hazardous Robotic Exploration
summary: Explores a behavioral valuation framework for hazardous robotic exploration, enabling robots to assess whether the potential information gain outweighs the risks in dangerous environments.

title: Expressive Robotic Pianist: Mastering Complex Piano Repertoire with Graph-Mimic and Musical Dynamics
summary: Focuses on enabling robots to perform complex piano repertoire with human-level expressivity by utilizing a Graph-Mimic approach to master fluid finger transitions and nuanced musical dynamics.

title: ReactHuman: A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Human-Like Reactive Decision-Making in Embodied Multimodal LLMs
summary: Introduces "ReactHuman," a physics-grounded benchmark designed to evaluate human-like reactive decision-making in Embodied Multimodal LLMs for their potential deployment in household robots.

title: IMLE-VLA: Fast Single-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: Proposes "IMLE-VLA," a method for fast single-step action generation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, aiming to improve efficiency over iterative multi-step sampling for robot control.

title: ObstaDiff: Generalizable Diffusion Policy Learning via Obstacle-aware Representations
summary: Introduces "ObstaDiff," a generalizable diffusion policy learning method that uses obstacle-aware representations to improve robotic manipulation in cluttered real-world scenes.
