title: When Connected Does Not Mean Similar: Charting the Homophily Boundary of SNAP-KG for Streaming Entity Integration
summary: SNAP-KG is a framework for assigning newly arriving entities to semantic communities in a growing knowledge graph (KG) using only their raw features, with no graph access and no retraining at inference time. It was evaluated on five multi-view benchmarks and a 2.4M-node OGB-WikiKG2 KG. In each of these datasets, at least one graph view is homophilous, meaning that connected nodes usually belong to the same class, and SNAP-KG performs well on all of them. This paper asks what happens outside that setting. We extend the evaluation to three heterophilous graphs (Texas, Wisconsin, Chameleon) and measure the edge homophily of every view. When no homophilous view is available, clustering quality drops sharply for both SNAP-KG and the transductive baselines used in its original evaluation. What decides this is the homophily of the relation, not the number of relations. Multi-view fusion still helps, but only when at least one homophilous relation provides a reliable foundation. The homophily assumption is therefore shared by the whole method family, not specific to SNAP-KG. We argue that heterophilous multi-view clustering is a separate research problem, outside the scope of this work. As future work, we outline how a heterophily-aware teacher could be distilled into SNAP-KG's projector to serve both homophilous and heterophilous KGs.

title: LatentVerse: A Framework for Understanding Shared and Modality-Specific Information in Multimodal Latent Representations
summary: Latent embeddings have become a central data abstraction in modern machine learning, especially in biomedicine, where foundation models are increasingly used to encode multimodal data like clinical text, medical images, omics, and physiological signals. However, the utility and value of these representations depends on understanding their quality, structure, and the information they encode. Existing analysis workflows for evaluating representations remain fragmented across custom scripts, isolated metrics, and most importantly lack multimodal analysis, limiting accessibility and reproducibility. We present LatentVerse, a representation analysis resource that combines a web-based visual analytics platform for accessible, report-driven exploration with a command-line interface for scalable technical workflows. LatentVerse unifies diagnostics for various representation quality metrics and extends to multimodal settings by decomposing embeddings into shared and modality-specific components. We evaluate LatentVerse through controlled unimodal and multimodal simulations, discovery-oriented analyses on real biomedical embeddings, and a user study across diverse use cases. By supporting thorough and interpretable evaluation of latent spaces, LatentVerse makes foundation model representations more understandable in biomedical and data science applications.

title: Certified AI Triage of ICU Alarms
summary: In the VTaC benchmark 71% of ventricular-tachycardia alarms are false, but silencing a real one can delay recognition of a dangerous arrhythmia. We reframe alarm reduction as three-way triage (retain, suppress, or defer) and bound the decision this analysis treats as harmful: among suppressed alarms, the fraction that were genuine stays below a user-set budget with 95% confidence, under i.i.d. event sampling. Alarms sharing a waveform record are dependent, so the clustered analysis is a sensitivity check. On the official split a 5% budget certifies in all three seeds, suppressing 74.8% of false alarms while silencing 1.5% of genuine ones, at AUROC 0.953 and Challenge Score 83.33, numerically comparable to the strongest of the eleven published systems. Our central finding measures what multiplicity costs: the correction charges for every candidate, so a finer grid can certify strictly less. Under held-out calibration the 885-cell grid we declared certifies 1 of 15 fold-runs, while choosing the grid on a separate selection partition certifies 8. We project the calibration volume each budget needs, making an uncertifiable budget a design parameter. Finally, adding a learned reliability dimension to the policy grid did not sharpen the certified frontier.

title: MInTRL: Off-policy Intervention can boost On-policy RL
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is typically performed on-policy, keeping training data close to the current policy but limiting learning to trajectories that the policy can discover itself. Off-policy methods such as supervised fine-tuning, on the other hand, can leverage external knowledge beyond the base model's capabilities, but may suffer from large distribution shift. The key challenge is thus to expand exploration without sacrificing learnability. In this work, we introduce Minimal Intervention Reinforcement Learning (MInTRL), which expands the exploration frontier through sparse, local interventions in otherwise on-policy rollouts. During generation, a judge-intervention policy periodically reviews the current policy's output, replaces erroneous suffixes with short corrections, and immediately returns control to the policy. During training, MInTRL adopts a sequence-level advantage-regression objective that eliminates the need for importance sampling. We show that sparse, local interventions can substantially improve coverage beyond finite-budget on-policy sampling while preserving the overall on-policy nature of the resulting trajectories. Across math and code benchmarks, MInTRL consistently outperforms standard on-policy and off-policy baselines. Ablations show that MInTRL remains effective with self-intervention and across different judge policies, while performance peaks at moderate intervention intensity, highlighting the importance of intervening minimally. These results establish minimal intervention as an effective paradigm for enhancing on-policy RL.

title: Granularity-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning is now the standard way to train large language model agents on long-horizon tasks, where dozens of interdependent actions precede a single sparse reward. Critic-free, group-relative methods such as GRPO suit this regime, but they broadcast one trajectory-level scalar to every step and cannot say which decision drove the outcome. GiGPO recovers a step-level signal by grouping time steps that share an anchor state, yet it merges the step- and episode-level estimates under one fixed weight, spending the same resolution on a pivotal branching decision as on a routine, near-deterministic transition. We argue that the right resolution is state-dependent, and propose GACA, a critic-free estimator whose granularity follows an uncertainty-based criticality proxy. GACA scores every step by the negative log-likelihood its own rollout already records, then blends the two advantages with a per-step weight that grows with that score, so the gradient places more weight on the fine-grained signal at above-average NLL and on the episode-level signal below it. We derive an exact risk decomposition for the implemented mixture and show that sufficiently small modulation improves on fixed mixing under positive directional alignment. A separate conditional result bounds local action-value variation using expected NLL, while an error-projection analysis characterizes when mixing adds value beyond scalar uncertainty reweighting. On ALFWorld and WebShop, GACA improves task success over GRPO and GiGPO at both 1.5B and 7B scales.

title: Observation-Anchored Selective Assimilation for Longitudinal Tumor-State Proxy Forecasting in Post-Treatment Glioma
summary: Post-treatment MRI in patients with glioma provides serial observations for updating patient-specific tumor-state proxy estimates, but variable appearances and trajectories complicate forecasting. We formulate forecasting as an observation-aware digital-twin update in which an intermediate observation anchors the patient-specific state. Among 203 patients and 594 follow-up time points, a predefined no-new-treatment criterion retained 120 of 236 candidate triplets, split into 81/24/15 training/validation/test triplets at the patient level. Each time point was represented by a continuous voxel-wise tumor-state proxy map in [0,1] derived from MRI lesion labels. A SegMamba-based single-step forecaster predicted update proposals from multimodal source-state tensors. Observation-Anchored Selective Assimilation (OASA) retained the observed intermediate proxy as the state anchor and selectively applied updates through a validation-selected tiered case-level rule and voxel-wise soft gate. We compared initial-scan forecasting, rollout without assimilation, latest-observation persistence, direct prediction, OASA, OASA + calibration, and morphological dilation. Checkpoints, OASA rules, and calibration thresholds were selected using validation data only. Across three seeds on 15 held-out test triplets, OASA maintained Dice at $\tau$ = 0.2 comparable to persistence (0.6071 $\pm$ 0.0025 vs. 0.6070) while yielding numerically higher Dice at $\tau$ = 0.5 (0.4269 $\pm$ 0.0079 vs. 0.3981), with a small RMSE increase. Calibration increased Dice at $\tau$ = 0.2 to 0.6178 $\pm$ 0.0025, increased false-positive (FP) support (11,836$\rightarrow$18,663), and reduced false-negative (FN) support (22,107$\rightarrow$17,536). This reflects near-threshold support calibration rather than improved biological predictive capability. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/jsudg436/longitudinal-proxy-forecasting.

title: Beyond the Query: Do Retrieval Signals Improve Adaptive Multimodal RAG Routing?
summary: Adaptive RAG often uses retrieval-time signals to decide whether another retrieval, reranking, or multimodal step should run. We ask whether these signals add routing value once the query itself is already known. Across document, audio, and video RAG, we compare matched query-only and query+retrieval routers while holding the optional actions, router family, training procedure, and evaluation fixed. On the held-out final evaluation, adding the tested retrieval signals does not produce a reliable routing improvement over the query-only baseline. Some retrieval signals are associated with whether a later step will help, but that predictability does not consistently lead to bet- ter RUN/SKIP decisions. The main lesson is therefore methodological: retrieval-state features should not be credited with routing value unless they improve over a matched query-only control. Our results do not show that routing or retrieval state is generally useless; they show that the incremental value of retrieval signals must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

title: SAGE-Loop: Reliable Closed-Loop LLM-Driven AutoML with Trial-and-Correction and Adaptive Ensembling
summary: Automated machine learning (AutoML) is reshaping data-driven science and industrial practice, and as large language models are introduced into AutoML, pipeline reliability becomes as important as automation efficiency. However, existing AutoML still struggles to realize instant feedback and adaptive optimization during execution, so once a run drifts into a suboptimal or failed state, it lacks a process-level correction mechanism. The fundamental pathology lies in its one-way pipeline: intermediate failures are typically terminated or bypassed, while fixed paradigms often strengthen model generation but leave ensemble decisions static, weakening both execution reliability and the controlled use of structural diversity. This indicates that LLM-driven AutoML needs a closed-loop ability for trial-correction-improvement together with evidence-based use of model diversity. To this end, we propose SAGE-Loop, a reliable closed-loop, self-adaptive, LLM-driven AutoML framework that performs multi-round generation and validation for trial-and-repair, and adaptively selects ensemble strategies in both supervised and unsupervised tasks, thereby unifying how to generate with how to use models. Across 20 public datasets, SAGE-Loop consistently improves performance and stability on classification, regression, and clustering tasks. Additional results further show its ability to recover from execution failures and maintain robust pipeline behavior.

title: A Differentially Private Federated Proximal Optimization Framework for Customer Churn Prediction in Heterogeneous Federated Telecom Networks
summary: Customer churn is one of the major issues in the telecommunication industry. To predict customer churn, conventional centralized machine learning approaches have been widely used. This centralized approach requires customer data to be stored in a central repository, which raises privacy concerns and may violate data protection regulations. Federated learning addresses this problem by allowing multiple telecom operators to collaboratively train a global model without transferring their raw customer data. However, real-world customer data are often heterogeneous (non-IID), which may negatively affect the performance of standard federated learning. Trained models can also suffer from privacy attacks. To address those issues, we propose a Differentially Private (DP) based Federated Proximal optimization (FedProx) framework. All experiments were performed on two publicly available telecom churn datasets. We trained Federated Averaging (FedAvg), DP-FedAvg, FedProx, and the proposed DP-FedProx framework. For baseline comparison, we also used several centralized and local models. To evaluate the models, we employed seven widely used evaluation metrics. The experimental results show that the FedProx based models consistently outperform the FedAvg based models. Compared with the best centralized model, the proposed DP-FedProx framework achieves competitive prediction performance with only a small reduction in accuracy while providing privacy guarantees. To explain our model, we conducted SHAP analysis which shows that DP-FedProx method priorities revenue group features. These results indicate that the proposed DP-FedProx framework provides a practical balance between prediction performance and data privacy protection.

title: Temporal Recurrence Favors Fewer Layers
summary: In streaming tasks, recurrent models can carry latent computation across time, allowing each update to build on representations produced earlier. This raises a basic question: once temporal recurrence provides sequential computation across steps, how much depth is still needed within each step? Prior work has shown that recurrence can make shallow models competitive. We instead study this question as a compute-allocation problem, varying within-step depth, expert width, and the number of parallel experts per layer across several compute budgets. For each budget, we compare the best observed recurrent and non-recurrent allocations and the performance they achieve under approximately matched per-step computation. Across Sokoban and autoregressive FineWeb language modeling, we find that temporal recurrence shifts the best observed compute allocation toward substantially fewer layers, with comparable or better performance.

title: $\text{GSF-}\chi$: Global Stereochemical Fields for Chiral Graph Transformers
summary: Enantiomers share atoms, bonds, and pairwise distances yet can behave differently in chiral environments, so molecular encoders must respect atom relabelings and proper rotations without becoming blind to reflection. We introduce GSF-$\chi$, a graph transformer in which stereogenic units modulate all pairwise interactions rather than single out one atom as special. Each central or axial stereogenic unit creates a reflection-even phase field over all atoms, a handedness pseudoscalar $\chi$ sets the direction of a relative rotation on latent query--key blocks, giving a \textbf{Chiral-RoPE} that reflection inverts rather than leaves fixed. A $C_2$ projection separates mirror-even ECD peak counts and positions from mirror-odd peak signs. We prove the operator's even--odd decomposition and its annotation-inversion, permutation, and unit-order identities under explicit canonical-role conditions; property tests and a coordinate-reflection audit verify the laws end to end. GSF-$\chi$ leads every central-ECD output and improves axial Rotation and Symbol by $12.6\%$ and $7.9\%$ over the strongest baseline. Equal-budget controls attribute the Rotation advantage to global signed support rather than parameter or edge count; the $C_2$ projection yields exact enantiomer-pair consistency at a small raw-accuracy cost under complete supervision and becomes predictive when mirror supervision is scarce.

title: Quality-Constrained Routing over a Fixed Pool of Quantized Mixture-of-Experts Instances
summary: Quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) services can hold several pre-materialized instances of one base model, but quantization damage varies sharply across requests and bitwidths. Because instance materialization and replica counts consume memory and require slow reconfiguration, we treat them as upstream provisioning decisions and study routing within a fixed resident pool. Within this fixed-pool boundary, we route each request to maximize modeled throughput under a class-level expected quality-degradation budget and measured instance capacities. To predict this request-specific risk, we introduce FWP (Fragility-Weighted Perplexity), computed from prompt tokens on a reference-instance prefill and calibrated to candidate-instance degradation. Underlying FWP is an exact two-expert affinity--fragility decomposition and a conditional multi-layer top-$k$ expansion whose bias, interaction, route-change, separability, and higher-order terms remain explicit. Using these calibrated risks, a window-level linear program yields a signed reduced-reward score that is KKT-consistent with the LP optimum under optimal prices and primal-feasible tie allocation. On 88 extended Qwen prompts, complete W2, W3, and W4 instances quantizing all 6,144 expert blocks incur mean $\Delta$NLL of $0.9437$, $0.1832$, and $0.0513$. Under the same population and $\tau=0.1513$, FWP allocation reaches a $1.284\times$ offline model-based multiplier versus $1.253\times$ for request-agnostic mixing and $1.000\times$ for static W4, an incremental $2.5\%$ relative FWP gain.

title: SCOPE-OPSD: Fisher-Conditioned Privileged Subspaces for On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) scores student-generated prefixes with a solution-conditioned self-teacher, yet transfers supervision only through next-token probabilities. We ask whether the aligned final-layer discrepancy offers a useful second channel, and how to test that channel without confusing its geometry with auxiliary strength. SCOPE-OPSD projects the privileged teacher-student residual onto a frozen rank-64 factor estimated from residual covariance and language-model-head Fisher sensitivity. It reuses the forwards already required by OPSD and adds neither rollouts nor inference-time modules. A matched Random control preserves the structured factor's rank and nonzero spectrum and uses per-arm gradient-RMS calibration, isolating the effect of the data-dependent orientation. Across the complete 25/50/75/100-step trajectories for Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B, Structured is never below Pure OPSD, with strict gains in 11 of the 12 model-checkpoint combinations and an exact tie at 4B step 25. Structured also exceeds matched Random in 10 of the 12 combinations. At step 75 on Qwen3-1.7B, Structured exceeds matched Random by 1.39 Macro Avg@12 points in each of two independent training reruns. A cross-fitted diagnostic also shows 4.40 times greater held-out privileged-gap capture than the matched random orientation. The results support a compact, Fisher-conditioned privileged subspace for short-budget OPSD.

title: Clustering-Based Balanced Sampling and Allocation with Data Parallelism for High-Performance Fine-Tuning
summary: Instruction-tuning datasets for large language models (LLMs) are often large, redundant, and imbalanced, limiting efficient adaptation. Naive large-batch fine-tuning repeatedly includes overrepresented sample groups while weakly covering underrepresented but informative ones, especially under data parallelism (DP) across multiple GPUs. We propose CluSTER, a Cluster-aware balanced Sampling framework for Training Efficient data Reduction in DP instruction tuning. CluSTER curates a representative reduced dataset through gradient-space clustering and DP-aware balanced allocation, ensuring dual-level coverage across clusters and workers, while preserving the original data distribution by weighted update. As a result, CluSTER reduces redundant computation and improves training stability without compromising model quality. Across multiple instruction-tuning datasets, CluSTER reduces training time by up to 69.6% with almost no accuracy loss compared to prior sampling and data reduction methods. Code is available at https://github.com/kaist-dmlab/CluSTER.

title: Where Decoder Cosine Similarity Fails for SAE Feature Flow Discovery
summary: Foundation models are increasingly adapted through fine-tuning, model editing, and alignment procedures while retaining previously acquired capabilities. Understanding the internal computations that support these adaptations is therefore becoming increasingly important for continual model evolution. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide interpretable feature dictionaries for residual-stream activations and sublayer outputs, but it remains unclear how state features and update features interact to produce downstream residual features. In this work, we focus on MLP updates as a first test case. We construct a transition atlas of triples $s_k + u_j \rightarrow t_\ell$, where a residual-state feature and an MLP-update feature jointly predict a target residual feature, and validate candidate triples by ablating the decoded update feature. In a 20M-token Pythia-160M $L_7 \rightarrow L_8$ run, we find 38,125 strong ablation-effect transitions, but 88.0% have both state-target and update-target decoder cosine similarity below 0.7. As a preliminary cross-model check, a run of 20M-token Gemma-3-4B $L_{21} \rightarrow L_{22}$ causally validates only the top 30,000 ranked candidate triples by ablating the decoded update feature, and 53.6% of strong-effect triples have both state-target and update-target decoder cosine similarity below 0.7. The Gemma result is directionally consistent with Pythia, but weaker, since update-target cosine recovers many of the strongest Gemma effects and the run is not a full-atlas causal validation. Ultimately, our results suggest that feature flow atlases can serve as diagnostics of representation-update mechanisms and thereby inform tools for steering model updates. Future work will validate more complex patterns across layers, models, and SAE families.

title: New method enables AI for safety-critical situations
summary: The “HardFlow” algorithm could help generative AI models produce high-quality outputs that obey strict requirements when “pretty close” doesn’t cut it.

title: R2VC: Modular Fact-Checking with Retrieval, Verification, and Confidence Calibration
summary: Large language models are increasingly used for automated fact checking, but end-to-end prompting often entangles evidence retrieval, reasoning, and uncertainty estimation, making failures difficult to diagnose and confidence difficult to trust. We present R2VC, a modular retrieve, reason, verify, calibrate architecture for evidence-grounded fact checking with citations and abstention. R2VC combines hybrid sparse+dense retrieval over Wikipedia, a supervised fine-tuned and DPO-aligned generator that produces diverse structured verdict candidates, an external NLI cross-encoder for evidence-based candidate selection, and a lightweight sequence-level calibrator for confidence estimation and selective abstention. On FEVER, an 8B backbone with R2VC achieves 13.74% higher accuracy than baseline. Ablation studies show that verifier-based candidate selection and confidence calibration are the largest contributors to performance. Removing candidate selection drops FEVER accuracy to 76.24%, while removing calibration nearly doubles the Brier score to 0.161. A manual analysis of 250 errors further shows that retrieval failures, especially wrong-entity evidence, remain the dominant bottleneck. Together, these results show that modular fact-checking pipelines can substantially improve both predictive accuracy and confidence reliability in open-domain verification.

title: What Counts as a Mistake? Annotating Recitation Events in Quran Memorization Transcripts
summary: Checking Quran recitation from an ASR transcript requires distinguishing unresolved mistakes from repetitions, repairs, opening formulas and accepted spelling differences. We report a completed human annotation of 100 production recording cases: 348 scored units and 162 localized events across ten combined labels. An executable evaluator scores labels and word positions together. A plain diff reaches label-aware F1 0.525 and localization F1 0.826; adapted production cleaner/alignment components reach 0.518 and 0.786, with exact-span F1 0.505 for both. Correcting the adapter's word coordinates recovers all five annotated repetition events, showing why annotation interfaces must be checked before interpreting baseline failures. In a preliminary pilot, eight single 20-minute runs across three coding agents and eight models span label-aware F1 0.143 to 0.892: seven land far above every baseline, and one collapses below the naive diff from a missing normalization step. Across the six, 970 of 972 gold-event instances draw an overlapping prediction, so what remains is not detection but convention: span extent, and the labels whose boundary is stipulated by adjudication rather than visible in the text. Seven of 162 events defeat all six same-day runs, five of them one orthographic rule, and the strongest run still misses the same ones. No run annotated before building, so the pilot measures the algorithm half of the task only.

title: Extracting Dataset Mentions in Forced Displacement and FCV Documents: A Weakly Supervised Framework with LLM-Based Label Refinement
summary: Development and humanitarian organizations produce and support surveys, administrative registries, and other data resources to inform research, policy, and operations, yet systematically identifying where these datasets are referenced remains difficult. Such references are dispersed across research papers, project documents, humanitarian reports, and other unstructured text, limiting both the ability to trace data use and to identify potential gaps in data availability or dissemination. We present a weakly supervised framework for adapting dataset extraction to forced displacement and Fragile, Conflict, and Violence (FCV) documents without first constructing a large manually labeled training corpus. A lightweight model trained on general research literature generates candidate dataset mentions from unlabeled domain documents, which a frontier large language model (LLM) reviews in context, validating or rejecting candidates and correcting their extraction boundaries. The resulting annotations are supplemented with targeted synthetic and contrastive examples and used to fine-tune the lightweight model for large-scale extraction. We evaluate the resulting model on an independent gold-standard benchmark of 1,706 text passages spanning research, humanitarian, and operational documents. Across the full benchmark, the model achieves 74.1\% precision and 70.5\% recall at the mention level; among passages containing dataset references, precision reaches 89.5\%. At the passage level, the model achieves 88.2\% accuracy and 88.6\% specificity in distinguishing passages with dataset references from those without them. These results demonstrate a practical approach for constructing domain-specific supervision when labeled data are limited, and provide a technical foundation for larger-scale analysis of data use and potential gaps in the displacement data landscape.

title: The Cost of Compression: A Rate-Distortion Limit on Factual Hallucination
summary: Factual hallucination in closed-book question answering is often treated as a coverage problem: a model fails because the relevant fact is absent from its internal memory. This view misses a second source of error. Even when a fact has been observed, finite memory may force it to be stored only approximately. We study this effect through a simple coverage--compression model of factual recall. We consider an unstructured question-answering task with $N$ possible queries and $K$ possible answers. A learner observes $M$ training facts, compresses them into at most $B$ bits, and answers uniformly drawn test queries without retrieval. For a uniformly random ground-truth mapping, we prove $\mathcal{E} \geq \frac{M}{N}\delta^\star\!\left(\frac{B}{M}\right) + \left(1-\frac{M}{N}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{K}\right)$, where $\delta^\star(r)$ is the inverse rate-distortion function of a uniform $K$-ary source under zero-one loss. The two terms separate compression distortion on observed facts from missing coverage on unobserved facts. The bound gives a compact way to reason about selective memory, forced compression, structure, retrieval, abstention, and long-context organization. We study the predicted signatures with theory-implied simulations and controlled fact-injection probes in modern language models that vary fact load and effective trainable memory. The result is not a complete theory of hallucination, but an information-theoretic account of a separable failure mode: lossy recall of observed facts under finite memory.

title: GAUGE: When Not to Trust LLM-as-a-Judge in User-Simulated Evaluation of Task-Oriented Agents
summary: Introduces GAUGE, a reusable offline protocol for evaluating task-oriented LLM agents by assessing when to trust LLM-as-a-judge user-simulations.

title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering
summary: Presents a method to improve multi-hop question answering by repairing and reinforcing context-augmented knowledge graph reasoning for large language models.

title: Chopthin-Consensus Power Sampling: A Diversity-Preserving Approach to LLM Decoding
summary: Introduces Chopthin-Consensus Power Sampling, a diversity-preserving approach for large language model decoding that improves reasoning by addressing aggressive pruning in sequential Monte Carlo methods.

title: Automated Detection and Structuring of Social Tipping Point Evidence in Climate related Documents: A Modular AI Framework
summary: Proposes a modular AI framework for the automated detection and structuring of social tipping point evidence within climate-related documents.

title: HypoKG: Evidence-Disciplined Biomedical Hypothesis Generation Beyond Endpoint Knowledge
summary: Introduces HypoKG, a system combining biological databases to enable evidence-disciplined biomedical hypothesis generation by large language models, addressing their reasoning capabilities.

title: EAR: Entity-Aware Partitioning Approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Development
summary: Presents EAR, an entity-aware partitioning approach designed to improve Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) development by optimizing how source corpora are divided into retrievable units.

title: Breaking the Token Ceiling: Distilling Smaller, Stronger Byte Models
summary: Explores breaking the token ceiling by distilling smaller, stronger byte models from larger ones, investigating scaling trends between distilled byte and token models.

title: ESTS at WMT26: Routing-Informed Expert Pruning for Model Compression
summary: Details six submissions to the WMT26 Model Compression Shared Task, employing routing-informed expert pruning to compress GPT-OSS-20B for English-Chinese and English-Egyptian Arabic translation.

title: I Am No One: Style-Aware Paraphrasing for Text Anonymization
summary: Proposes style-aware paraphrasing for text anonymization to counter authorship attribution models that re-identify users, addressing growing privacy risks in text publishing.

title: SynthSentry: Detecting Synthetic Data Contamination in Language Model Training Data
summary: Introduces SynthSentry, a method for detecting synthetic data contamination in language model training data to prevent model collapse and preserve factual accuracy.

title: CueMem: Cue-Guided Context Reconstruction for Long-Term Conversational Memory
summary: Presents CueMem, a cue-guided context reconstruction method designed to enhance long-term conversational memory for agents by efficiently recalling information from extended dialogue histories.

title: ORQA: An Occupation-Realistic Question and Answer Framework for LLM Professional Knowledge
summary: Introduces ORQA, an occupation-realistic question and answer framework designed for testing and evaluating the professional knowledge of large language models.

title: Representation-based Masked Diffusion Model
summary: Discusses a representation-based Masked Diffusion Model aimed at improving language modeling by addressing independent token updates in parallel text generation.

title: GraphProfiler: Source-Linked Sensitive Attribute Inference via Personal Knowledge Graphs
summary: Introduces GraphProfiler, an LLM-based system that infers sensitive personal attributes from user-generated content via personal knowledge graphs, raising privacy concerns.

title: Not All Speech Is Intent: Adaptive Self-Correcting Inference Layer for Post-ASR False Wake-Up
summary: Proposes an adaptive self-correcting inference layer to mitigate post-ASR false wake-up activations in conversational AI by refining intent decisions from speech input.

title: AMDKernelVault: Large-Scale Datasets and Agentic Training for AMD GPU Kernel Optimization
summary: Introduces AMDKernelVault, an open kernel corpus and training framework for AMD CDNA GPUs, designed for agentic training to optimize GPU kernels and support LLM-based kernel agents.

title: Zipbench: Low-Cost Framework for Compressing Comprehensive Benchmarks of Large Language Models
summary: Presents Zipbench, a low-cost framework for compressing comprehensive benchmark suites of large language models to make evaluation more efficient.

title: The House with a Million Windows: Interactive Fiction for Narrative Restorying
summary: Introduces "The House with a Million Windows," an LLM-based interactive fiction system designed to enhance narrative restorying and address challenges in AI-assisted writing.

title: Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Introduces "Agent as Policy" (AGP), demonstrating how a general-purpose agent can directly control a physical robot for task execution and manipulation without specific training.

title: Calibrated Ambiguity in Multimodal Language Models: Humans reach for cultural references, while models describe the picture
summary: This paper investigates how multimodal language models handle ambiguity compared to human communication, where ambiguity can be a generative resource rather than a bug.

title: SWARM: A Multilingual Human-Annotated Dataset for Russian Propaganda Detection in Search Engine Results
summary: This work introduces SWARM, a multilingual human-annotated dataset designed for detecting Russian propaganda in search engine results, expanding beyond typical social media analysis.

title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents
summary: This research introduces LifeMem, a framework to improve large language model agents' ability to reuse past experiences and overcome catastrophic forgetting for lifelong adaptation.

title: Doc2FRC: Length-Consistent Document-Level Machine Translation via Fixed-Range Chunking
summary: Doc2FRC proposes a Fixed-Range Chunking method to achieve length-consistent document-level machine translation using LLMs, addressing issues like n-gram repetition and quality degradation.

title: Cognition on Graph: Navigating Massive Knowledge Space via Cognitive Cycles and Bidirectional Graph-Text Synergy
summary: This paper explores 'Cognition on Graph' to enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for LLMs, enabling better navigation and reasoning over massive, heterogeneous knowledge bases.

title: DuplexDrama: A Synthesized Dialogue Dataset with Scenarios, Full-Duplex Behaviors, Expressive Speech, and Sound Events
summary: This presents DuplexDrama, the first synthesized spoken dialogue dataset that includes complete persona settings, full-duplex behaviors, expressive speech, and sound events.

title: Parameter-Efficient Retrievers for Polish and European Languages
summary: This work proposes a three-stage training pipeline for developing compact and efficient dense retrieval systems, focusing on parameter-efficient models for Polish and other European languages.

title: LLM-Enhanced Dual-Branch Learning for Large-Scale Multi-Label Text Classification
summary: This paper introduces an LLM-enhanced dual-branch learning approach for large-scale multi-label text classification, improving performance for documents with many candidate labels.

title: Judging by the Cover: Cleaning LLM Truthfulness Benchmarks to Avoid Surface-Level Feature Leakage
summary: This study identifies and addresses surface-level feature leakage in LLM truthfulness benchmarks, showing how models can appear to perform well without actual reasoning.

title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models
summary: This research reveals gaps in large language models' long-horizon procedural reasoning by testing them on tasks derived from application manuals, highlighting limitations of current benchmarks.

title: Kraken: LLM-based Speech-to-Speech Translation via Low-bitrate VQ and Dual-path Source Conditioning
summary: Kraken is introduced as an LLM-based Speech-to-Speech Translation system that uses low-bitrate VQ and dual-path source conditioning to optimize performance and preserve non-linguistic information.

title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper investigates Expert-Space Exploration in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Reinforcement Learning, focusing on improving expert selection beyond fixed components for post-training LLMs.

title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking
summary: SAS (Simple Attention Sparsification) is presented as a method for optimizing context ranking via end-to-end training to reduce the quadratic attention cost in pretrained Transformers.

title: Type Diversity Enables Transformers to Generalise Compositionally
summary: This research suggests that type diversity, rather than inherent limitations, enables Transformers to achieve compositional generalization, particularly in structural generalization.

title: PRISMA-LLM: An Empirical Reporting Framework for AI-Assisted Systematic Reviews
summary: PRISMA-LLM is introduced as an empirical reporting framework to standardize the auditing and reporting of workflows in AI-assisted systematic reviews, addressing inconsistent information.

title: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding with a Contamination-Controlled Private Suite
summary: This study measures the 'harness effect' in agentic coding systems, distinguishing the impact of tools, prompts, and control flow from the language model's capabilities in autonomous software engineering.

title: Is Bash All You Need? An Empirical Study of Tool Interfaces for Enterprise Digital Worker Agents
summary: This empirical study investigates whether a general shell interface can outperform specialized tools for enterprise digital worker agents performing complex organizational tasks.

title: Creating an Atomic User Model for Personality-Aware Large Language Model Interaction
summary: This research proposes creating an Atomic User Model to enable more sophisticated personality-aware interactions for large language model assistants, moving beyond simple preference summaries.

title: Can LLMs in Draft-Verify-Revise Pipelines Resolve Deictic Ambiguity?
summary: This paper examines whether LLMs employing the 'draft-verify-revise' orchestration pattern can effectively resolve deictic ambiguity by passing context between different stages.

title: Beyond ID Embeddings: Process-Grounded Language Modeling for Cognitive Diagnosis
summary: This work introduces Process-Grounded Language Modeling as an alternative to ID-based embeddings for Cognitive Diagnosis Models, aiming for a more natural representation of learner cognition in personalized learning.

title: Diverse Minds, Divided Networks? Personality Composition, Polarization, and Collective Intelligence in LLM-Based Social Simulations
summary: This paper uses LLM-based social simulations to study online polarization and collective intelligence by analyzing the impact of personality composition.

title: Do LLMs Trust the Accuser or the Accusation? Measuring Belief Shifts in Werewolf
summary: This research proposes a belief-shift evaluation benchmark for LLM agents in Werewolf to analyze their communication skills and belief updating, moving beyond final game outcomes.

title: Confidence-Gated Transductive Test Generation for Code Reranking
summary: This paper introduces Confidence-Gated Transductive Test Generation, a method for synthesizing high-quality test cases to evaluate and rank programs generated by LLMs.

title: Information Specialization and Constrained Synthesis in Multi-Agent LLM Forecasting: A Prospective Live-Study of the 2026 FIFA World Cup
summary: This study conducts a live evaluation of multi-agent LLM systems with specialized roles for forecasting, specifically for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, to assess the impact of information specialization.

title: Earth-Agent-Pro: Towards Real-World Full-Chain Earth Observation with Agents
summary: Earth-Agent-Pro is an agent system designed for real-world Earth observation, capable of translating scientific questions into executable workflows for data acquisition, processing, and conclusion derivation.

title: SteerDuplex: Steerable Duplex Speech Dialogue Models
summary: SteerDuplex introduces steerable full-duplex speech dialogue models that allow reliable shifting of conversational behaviors like tone, persona, speaking rate, and voice style.

title: Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as Long-Context Recall Regardless of Context Window Size
summary: This research proposes Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as a method for achieving long-context recall in LLMs, aiming to overcome limitations related to context window size.

title: What Drives Recovery in Agentic Text-to-Cypher? LAST-CQ: An LLM Agent Self-Refinement Framework
summary: This paper introduces LAST-CQ, a five-agent self-refinement framework for Text-to-Cypher generation, and analyzes the mechanisms driving recovery in agentic structured-query pipelines.

title: Feature Recovery for Object Understanding After Irreversible Fire Damage
summary: This work focuses on a method for feature recovery to understand objects after irreversible fire damage, critical for hazard detection and content reconstruction.

title: Beyond Argmax: A Mechanistic Study of Semantic Retention in Frozen Foundation-Model Composition for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Segmentation
summary: This study mechanically investigates semantic retention when composing independently pretrained, frozen foundation models for generalized few-shot 3D segmentation tasks.

title: Single-Query Person-Centric Bimanual Hand-Object Interaction Detection
summary: This research presents a method for single-query person-centric bimanual hand-object interaction detection, aiming to identify interactions specific to an individual with both hands.

title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation
summary: USPLIT-VQA proposes a U-shaped split learning framework with contribution-aware weighted aggregation for Visual Question Answering, addressing privacy concerns in VQA systems.

title: When Ground-Truth Fidelity Matters: An Orchestrated UAS Framework for Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus Detection Using Vision Transformers and Machine Learning
summary: This research details an orchestrated UAS framework utilizing Vision Transformers and Machine Learning for the early detection of Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus in sweet corn production.

title: Physics as the label for measuring and correcting materials reasoning in multimodal models
summary: This paper explores using physics as a label to measure and correct materials reasoning in multimodal models, aiming to identify and mitigate hallucinations regarding physical properties.

title: QuPAINT: Physics-Aware Multimodal Reasoning for Quantum Material Characterization
summary: QuPAINT is introduced as a physics-aware multimodal reasoning system for characterizing 2D quantum materials, assisting in localizing flakes and determining layer thickness from optical microscopy.

title: UniMo: Unifying Human and Animal Motion Generation
summary: UniMo is a system designed for unifying human and animal 3D motion generation, addressing challenges in extending text-driven human motion generation to animal domains.

title: UFO: Chain-of-Evaluation for Omni-Condition Alignment in Multi-Modal Image Generation
summary: UFO proposes a Chain-of-Evaluation method for multi-modal image generation, focusing on omni-condition alignment to improve the assessment of generative models.

title: GSO-Net: Visual State Machines for Hazardous Freight Transfer Compliance at Petrochemical Logistics Nodes
summary: GSO-Net describes a visual state machine network for ensuring compliance during hazardous freight transfer operations at petrochemical logistics nodes, addressing safety-critical procedural adherence.

title: OphBiWSSD: Scaling Temporal Action Localization in Ophthalmic Surgeries with Bidirectional Weight-tied State Space Duality
summary: OphBiWSSD presents a novel approach for scaling temporal action localization in ophthalmic surgeries using bidirectional weight-tied state space duality to model high-frequency surgical maneuvers.

title: A Multimodal Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis using 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Clinical Data
summary: This research proposes a multimodal explainable deep learning framework for Alzheimer's Disease diagnosis, integrating 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging and clinical data.

title: An End-to-End Automated Pipeline for Controllable Crack Data Synthesis
summary: This paper presents an automated pipeline for synthesizing controllable crack data, crucial for deep learning-based crack inspection where real data is scarce. It addresses limitations of generic image-generation methods by offering better control over crack morphology.

title: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
summary: This research improves few-shot medical anomaly detection by combining Vision Foundation Models with CLIP, overcoming CLIP's lack of explicit spatial supervision for precise lesion localization.

title: Partition-Invariant Tuning for 3D Scene Understanding
summary: This paper introduces Partition-Invariant Tuning, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for pre-trained 3D point cloud foundation models. It addresses the substantial computational and storage costs associated with full fine-tuning for 3D scene understanding.

title: PhysioAI: Clinical Knowledge-Guided Semantic Supervision for Skeleton-Based Physiotherapy Action Recognition
summary: This research introduces PhysioAI, a method using clinical knowledge to guide semantic supervision for skeleton-based physiotherapy action recognition. It aims to support automated tracking of exercises in remote rehabilitation settings.

title: RoES: Rotational Equivariant Selective-frequency Fusion for Multimodal Images
summary: This paper proposes RoES, a method for rotational equivariant selective-frequency fusion of infrared-visible images. It aims to enhance robust multimodal perception by integrating complementary textural and thermal information.

title: LettuceVisSim: A Simulator That Generates Lettuce Image Time-series for Vision-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces LettuceVisSim, a simulator designed to generate labelled lettuce image time-series data for vision-based reinforcement learning. It addresses the scarcity of labelled crop images hindering AI development in controlled environment agriculture.

title: ChitraMiti: Benchmarking Visual Grounding and Modality Reliance in Bengali Geometric Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces ChitraMiti-12.8k, a new synthetic benchmark for evaluating vision-language models in Bengali geometric reasoning. It focuses on low-resource languages and problems requiring diagram and text interpretation.

title: One Skill Does Not Fit All: Automatic Discovery and Taxonomy-Guided Routing of Frame-Selection Skills for Long-Video Question Answering
summary: This research proposes a method for automatically discovering and routing frame-selection strategies for Long-Video Question Answering. It addresses the limitation of applying a single strategy to varied question types in hour-scale videos.

title: RelateAnything: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Relation Prediction From Any Inputs
summary: This paper introduces a new approach to open-vocabulary relation prediction that moves beyond fixed predicate taxonomies. It allows for real-time relation prediction from diverse inputs, similar to open-vocabulary detection and promptable segmentation.

title: DRS-VPT: Directly Relocalizing in a Scan with Vision Point Transformers
summary: This paper presents DRS-VPT, a feed-forward transformer architecture for foundational image-to-scan registration. It predicts scan pose and point maps from query images and a 3D point cloud.

title: An Ultra-Widefield Swept-Source OCTA Dataset and a Polar-Gated Mamba Network for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces WOIVES, a new ultra-widefield swept-source OCTA dataset, and a Polar-Gated Mamba Network for retinal vessel segmentation. It aims to address the lack of public benchmarks and comprehensive evaluation for this task.

title: Detecting and Explaining Fake News Short Videos with Multimodal Content and Real-World Evidence
summary: This research focuses on developing methods for detecting and explaining fake news in short videos, using multimodal content and real-world evidence. It addresses the challenge of widespread misinformation on video platforms.

title: NOVA-GS: Noise-Aware View-Consistent Gaussian Splatting for Low-Light Novel View Synthesis
summary: This paper introduces NOVA-GS, a technique for 3D scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis under low-light conditions using Gaussian Splatting. It aims to mitigate issues caused by severe sensor noise and low signal-to-noise ratios.

title: Semantically Aligned Gradient-Driven Context-Preserving Image Editing
summary: This paper describes a method for instruction-guided image editing that ensures semantic verification and context preservation. It addresses issues of incomplete edits and spatial spillage in generative editors.

title: ExpertHTR: Unified Handwritten Text Recognition with Multi-Task Learning and Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
summary: This paper proposes ExpertHTR, a unified vision-language framework for handwritten text recognition using multi-task learning and sparse Mixture-of-Experts. It tackles challenges posed by diverse and distributed datasets across languages and scripts.

title: Multimodal Floorplan Encoding: Learning Dense Modality-Invariant Representations
summary: This paper introduces a method for multimodal floorplan encoding to learn dense modality-invariant representations. It aims to enable learning systems to transfer across different floorplan formats for geometry-centric tasks.

title: GRACE: Adaptive Concept Erasure with Geometry-Guided Retention in Diffusion Models
summary: This paper presents GRACE, a method for adaptive concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models while retaining desired geometry. It aims to remove sensitive concepts from models without excessive intervention.

title: AquaCubeAI-Powered Monitoring Turbidity on-board {\Phi}sat-2
summary: This paper proposes AquaCubeAI, an AI-powered system for on-board, real-time monitoring of coastal water quality from satellites. It aims to reduce latency in responding to rapidly evolving turbidity events.

title: Same Encoder, Different Winner: A Paired-View Framework for Cell Painting Encoder Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces CP-BG-Bench, a new paired-view framework for evaluating vision encoders in Cell Painting, moving beyond single-metric rankings. It provides a more comprehensive assessment by holding the central cell fixed across multiple views.

title: LG-PF: Lightweight Confidence-Guided Polarization Image Fusion
summary: This paper describes LG-PF, a lightweight confidence-guided method for polarization image fusion. It aims to combine stable luminance and structural information with material-sensitive details from DoLP images effectively.

title: LGFN: Lightweight Gated RGB-Polarization Fusion with Modality-Availability Conditioning for Camouflaged Object Detection
summary: This paper introduces LGFN, a lightweight gated RGB-polarization fusion method with modality-availability conditioning for camouflaged object detection, addressing challenges in intelligent optical perception.

title: Online Video Agent Harness for Long Video Understanding
summary: This research proposes an online video agent harness designed to improve long video understanding by addressing context rot and cost issues in processing query-relevant evidence across extended temporal spans.

title: SCDM: Spatial-Contextual Disentanglement Mamba via Differential Inference for Efficient Image Classification
summary: This paper presents SCDM, a Spatial-Contextual Disentanglement Mamba via Differential Inference for efficient image classification, particularly for medical image analysis where distinguishing subtle pathological features is critical.

title: CoralscapesV2: Panoptic and Fine-Grained Visual Scene Understanding in Coral Reefs
summary: This paper introduces CoralscapesV2, a method for panoptic and fine-grained visual scene understanding in coral reefs, aimed at scaling up ecological monitoring for conservation strategies using computer vision.

title: A Dual Cross-Attention Framework for Colposcopic CIN Grading and Swede Score Prediction Using a New Multi-Center Dataset
summary: This research proposes a novel deep learning dual cross-attention framework for colposcopic CIN grading and Swede score prediction, using a new multi-center dataset to improve cervical cancer screening in LMICs.

title: Balancing Emotional Alignment and Semantic Consistency in Image Generation via Reinforcement Learning with Valence-Arousal Anchoring
summary: This paper explores balancing emotional alignment and semantic consistency in image generation using reinforcement learning with Valence-Arousal Anchoring to improve continuous emotion control in text-to-image models.

title: Self-supervised Pre-training Helps Retinal Disease Progression Modelling Most When Data Is Scarce
summary: This research investigates how self-supervised pre-training can effectively model retinal disease progression, especially when longitudinal imaging data is scarce, by leveraging abundant cross-sectional data.

title: HemaHier: Chain-Conditioned Ordinal Hierarchies for Lineage-Aware Bone-Marrow Cytology
summary: This paper introduces HemaHier, a method utilizing chain-conditioned ordinal hierarchies for lineage-aware bone-marrow cytology, which improves classification by incorporating the inherent structured nature of cell types.

title: 3D CT-to-PET Translation via Latent Brownian Bridge Diffusion
summary: This research proposes a method for 3D CT-to-PET translation via Latent Brownian Bridge Diffusion to provide complementary anatomical and functional information for cancer diagnosis, addressing limitations of PET scans.

title: VideoTok4D: A 4D-Aware Video Tokenizer for Compact World Representation
summary: This paper presents VideoTok4D, a 4D-aware video tokenizer designed for compact world representation in video modeling, improving compression, reconstruction, and generation capabilities.

title: Scenario-Independent Criticality Assessment and Prediction for Vulnerable Road Users in Autonomous Driving
summary: This research focuses on developing scenario-independent criticality assessment and prediction methods for vulnerable road users in autonomous driving, aiming to enhance the safety of automated vehicles.

title: Pelican-Sim 1.0: A General World Model Simulator for Embodied Intelligence
summary: This technical report introduces Pelican-Sim 1.0, a general world model simulator designed for embodied intelligence, which predicts future observations from visual context and robot actions.

title: MoPA: Coordinated Mobile Manipulation via Subsystem-Specific Perception Alignment
summary: This paper introduces MoPA, a system for coordinated mobile manipulation that aligns subsystem-specific perception for base motion and arm control, addressing challenges in kinematically coupled robotic systems.

title: RodForesight: A World Model Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Slender and Material Agnostic Rod Insertion
summary: This paper presents RodForesight, a world model enhanced diffusion policy for slender and material agnostic rod insertion, designed for precision manufacturing tasks requiring accurate robotic perception and control.

title: A Data-Driven Distributed Control Scheme: Learning Multi-Objective Agent-Based MPC for Path-Tracking
summary: This research proposes a data-driven distributed control scheme, learning multi-objective agent-based model predictive control (MPC) for path-tracking in vehicle systems using distributed agents.

title: A Physics-Based Closed-Loop Robotic Bioprinting Framework Towards Volumetric Muscle Loss Treatment
summary: This paper proposes a physics-based closed-loop robotic bioprinting framework aimed at treating Volumetric Muscle Loss (VML) by optimizing print outcomes.

title: An Automated Thickness Evaluation Procedure Using an Integrated Structured Light 3D Camera in a Robotic Bioprinting Framework
summary: This research presents an automated thickness evaluation procedure using an integrated structured light 3D camera within a robotic bioprinting framework to improve the quality of bioprinted constructs.

title: Chain-SLAM: Globally Consistent Backend for Multi-Session LiDAR SLAM via Chained Loop Closure
summary: This paper introduces Chain-SLAM, a LiDAR SLAM backend that enables globally consistent, online multi-session map alignment and reuse for large-scale autonomous navigation systems.

title: DIA: Denoising Intermediate Advantage for Diffusion Policy Optimization
summary: This research proposes DIA (Denoising Intermediate Advantage), a method to improve diffusion policy optimization for robotic manipulation by integrating reinforcement learning with behavior cloning.

title: Pneumatic neurons for soft robots enable inflate-and-fire networks for rhythmic motion
summary: This research explores using pneumatic neurons to enable inflate-and-fire networks for soft robots, allowing them to achieve rhythmic motion without external centralized electronic controllers.

title: AnchorVLN: Geometry-Anchored Vision-Language Grounding Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Navigation
summary: AnchorVLN is a system that uses geometry-anchored vision-language grounding reasoning to enable robots to navigate unseen indoor environments and follow natural language instructions.

title: DATAFARM: Distribution-Aligned Task and Motion Planning for Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: DATAFARM proposes a method to generate high-quality robot data using distribution-aligned task and motion planning for fine-tuning vision-language-action models, addressing a key challenge in training robot foundation models.

title: DWMP: Leveraging Dual World Models for Humanoid Obstacle Traversal
summary: DWMP introduces a method leveraging dual world models to enable humanoid robots to traverse cluttered obstacle fields using onboard proprioceptive and visual observations effectively.

title: READ: Learning Risk-Informed Fields for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: READ focuses on learning risk-informed fields for end-to-end autonomous driving, allowing planners to determine future maneuvers based on road structure, surrounding agents, and their motion states.

title: FoldNet++: a Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for Robotic T-Shirt Folding and Unfolding
summary: FoldNet++ is a large-scale synthetic dataset created for training generalizable policies for robotic T-shirt folding and unfolding, featuring diverse robotic embodiments and garments.

title: PATH: Continuous Target Sensing among Autonomous Cooperative Drones
summary: PATH investigates continuous target sensing among autonomous cooperative drones (UAVs), addressing the challenge of limited flight endurance by facilitating tracking responsibility transfer.

title: ArtManip: Category-Level Articulated In-Hand Manipulation
summary: ArtManip addresses the challenge of category-level in-hand manipulation of articulated objects by dexterous robotic hands, focusing on controlling internal degrees of freedom while maintaining grasp stability.

title: Quantifying Spectral Differences in Vehicle Between Production Autonomous and Human-Driven Vehicles Across Driving Scenarios
summary: This research quantifies spectral differences in vehicle kinematic characteristics between production autonomous vehicles and human-driven vehicles across various driving scenarios through empirical study.

title: Online Material Estimation for Conditioned Diffusion Policy in Shaping Deformable Linear Objects
summary: This paper explores online material estimation for a conditioned diffusion policy to improve shape control of deformable linear objects, accounting for varying material properties in robotic manipulation.

title: Breaking the Vision-Action Shortcut: Latent Interface Training for Generalizable Robotics Foundation Models
summary: This research proposes latent interface training to enhance the generalizability of robotics foundation models, aiming to prevent performance degradation under visual distribution shifts.

title: Size Doesn't Matter: Material-State Reinforcement Learning for Excavator Transferable Soil Manipulation
summary: This work introduces material-state reinforcement learning for excavators to achieve more transferable soil manipulation, addressing limitations of current autonomous systems in earthmoving tasks.

title: Improving Imitation Learning Efficiency for Manipulation through Geometric Prior Pretraining
summary: This research aims to improve the efficiency of imitation learning for robotic manipulation tasks by utilizing geometric prior pretraining, addressing sample efficiency concerns.

title: High-Fidelity Multi-Body Simulator for Autonomous Racing
summary: This paper presents a custom high-fidelity multi-body simulation environment for testing and validating autonomous racing software and autonomous vehicle dynamics.

title: VertexCBF: Improving Neural Control Barrier Functions via Vertex-Restricted Control Search
summary: VertexCBF introduces an improved method for neural control barrier functions using a vertex-restricted control search to enhance safety and effectiveness for autonomous robots.

title: Parameter Sensitivity Analysis for Aerial LiDAR-Inertial Odometries in low-altitude flights
summary: This study performs a parameter sensitivity analysis for aerial LiDAR-inertial odometry algorithms used for precise navigation of unmanned aerial vehicles in low-altitude flights.

title: A Multi-Vehicle Dataset with Camera, LiDAR, and Radar Sensors and Scanned 3D Models for Custom Auto-Annotation using RTK-GNSS
summary: This paper introduces a multi-vehicle dataset featuring camera, LiDAR, and radar sensors, along with scanned 3D models and RTK-GNSS, for custom auto-annotation in autonomous driving perception algorithm development.

title: From Transportation to Manipulation: Enabling Grasping in Magnetic Robotics
summary: This research focuses on enabling grasping and advanced manipulation capabilities in magnetic robotics, extending the utility of magnetic levitation systems beyond transportation.

title: Before the Tipping Point: Force-Guided Active Perception for Shape-Agnostic Estimation of 3D Centers of Mass
summary: This paper presents a force-based active perception method for robot manipulators to estimate the 3D center of mass of unknown objects from a single sub-critical tipping experiment.

title: Robust Underwater Grasping of Sloped Objects with a Waterproof Passive Adaptive Gripper
summary: This research addresses robust underwater grasping of sloped objects using a waterproof passive adaptive gripper, improving performance compared to traditional parallel-jaw grippers.

title: ARC: Autonomous Robotics Compliance A Three-Layer Governance Architecture for Deployed Autonomous Systems
summary: ARC proposes a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous robotic systems, outlining a framework for compliance through model safety validation, cognitive certification, and operational authorization standards.

title: A Robot Among People:From Social Imitation to the Social Becoming of Human Groups
summary: This article discusses a different way of understanding robots as situated elements within human groups, rather than discrete agents, focusing on their role in mediating social interactions.

title: Distributed Stochastic Optimal Control for Pattern-Oriented Swarms
summary: This paper introduces a GRF-based stochastic optimal control framework designed to address challenges in geometric control, self-organization, and safe navigation for pattern-oriented swarms.

title: Tuning ROS 2 for Energy-Efficient Navigation: Empirical Insights from Costmap 2D Configurations
summary: This paper presents empirical insights into tuning ROS 2 Costmap 2D configurations to improve the energy efficiency of autonomous navigation in robots.

title: Comfort by Construction: Adaptive, Comfort-Bounded Action Spaces for Learned Driving Policies
summary: This research proposes adaptive, comfort-bounded action spaces for learned driving policies to prevent reinforcement learning from generating abrupt maneuvers in data-driven driving simulators.

title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model
summary: Dynin-Robotics introduces an omnimodal unified diffusion Vision-Language-Action model that provides language-conditioned robot policies with visual goal and dynamics prediction for action generation and selection.

title: ASTRIL-MPC: Autonomous Traversal Framework of Articulated Tracked Robots with Language-Guided Neural-Kinematic MPC
summary: ASTRIL-MPC presents an autonomous traversal framework for articulated tracked robots, utilizing language-guided neural-kinematic model predictive control for reliable navigation in complex urban search and rescue environments.

title: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Management and Serving for Robot Factories
summary: This research focuses on efficient management and serving of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation, addressing the need for strict Service-Level Objectives in robot factories.

title: Decentralized Evolution of Hexapod Gaits with Independent Leg Controllers
summary: This paper proposes a novel approach for hexapod robot locomotion, using a decentralized evolutionary algorithm to independently evolve gaits for each leg through a simulator and a physical robot.

title: UniPart: Towards Zero-shot Language-Grounded 3D Part Segmentation for Embodied Interaction
summary: This paper introduces UniPart, a research approach towards zero-shot language-grounded 3D part segmentation to enhance fine-grained robotic manipulation and embodied interaction.

title: RoMu4o: A Robotic Manipulation Unit For Orchard Operations Automating Proximal Hyperspectral Leaf Sensing
summary: RoMu4o is a robotic manipulation unit designed for orchard operations, automating proximal hyperspectral leaf sensing to support precision agriculture.
