summary: This paper introduces FirmCORe, a new benchmark designed for structured reasoning about inter-firm collaboration opportunities. It aims to address the scarcity of comprehensive data on inter-firm relationships for evaluation purposes.

title: MOCC-R1: Reinforcing Reasoning-Response Consistency for Multimodal Counselor Response Generation
summary: This research introduces MOCC-R1, a method for reinforcing reasoning-response consistency in multimodal counselor response generation. It aims to improve the generation of appropriate counselor responses from multimodal dialogue histories by addressing dataset limitations.

title: End-to-End Latency-Minimizing and Load-Balanced Request Scheduling for Edge LLM Inference in Agentic AI Services
summary: This research focuses on end-to-end latency-minimizing and load-balanced request scheduling for Large Language Model (LLM) inference on distributed edge servers. It aims to optimize agentic AI services by addressing heterogeneous communication and computing capabilities in edge deployments.

title: Extracting ontology-compliant knowledge from scientific text describing irradiated materials using large language models
summary: This research applies large language models to extract ontology-compliant knowledge from scientific texts describing irradiated materials. It aims to make essential data from scientific literature more accessible for predictive models and simulations in materials science.

title: Causal neural set filtering for online multi-target tracking
summary: This research proposes Causal Neural Set Filtering (CNSF) for online multi-target tracking, addressing redundant computation in transformer-based trackers. The method aims to jointly learn data association and state estimation more efficiently.

title: Managing Action Preconditions in Neuro-Symbolic RL: Three Placement Strategies for Embodied Agents
summary: This research explores three placement strategies for managing action preconditions within Neuro-Symbolic Reinforcement Learning for embodied agents. It aims to enable agents to leverage prior behavioral knowledge for more efficient learning in new tasks.

title: OmniHarness: Harnessing Generalizable Visual Generation via Symbolic Policy Learning
summary: This paper introduces OmniHarness, a novel methodology for generalizable visual generation using unified multimodal large language models and multi-agent systems, addressing limitations in existing task-specific methods.

title: Driver Behavior Estimation at Signalized Intersections Using a Physics-Constrained Decision-Conditioned Autoregressive Transformer
summary: This paper presents a physics-constrained decision-conditioned autoregressive transformer to estimate and predict human driver decision-making and trajectory behavior at signalized intersections, aiming to mitigate traffic accidents.

title: HintMiner: Automatic Question Hints Mining From Q&A Web Posts with Language Model via Self-Supervised Learning
summary: This paper proposes HintMiner, a novel tool using language models and self-supervised learning to automatically mine question hints from Q&A web posts, helping users find answers more effectively.

title: POSPAN: Position-Constrained Span Masking for Language Model Pre-training
summary: This paper introduces POSPAN, a new position-constrained span masking technique for language model pre-training, enhancing the benefits of span-level masked language modeling by addressing previous limitations in span length considerations.

title: You Don't Need To Train: Agentic Heuristic Learning Studio for Executable Human Activity Recognition
summary: This paper introduces the Agentic Heuristic Learning (AHL) Studio, which uses an agentic approach inspired by human cognitive learning for executable human activity recognition, focusing on forming rules and repairing mistakes rather than gradient-based training.

title: A panoramic aerodynamic performance prediction method for turbomachinery cascades using transformer-enhanced neural operator
summary: This paper proposes a panoramic aerodynamic performance prediction method for turbomachinery cascades, utilizing a transformer-enhanced neural operator to enable flexible and rapid evaluation in design.

title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Semantics-Consistent Tabular Diffusion with Weak Semantic Priors
summary: This paper presents Semantics-Consistent Tabular Diffusion, a new method for generating synthetic tabular data that explicitly models weak semantic priors to ensure consistency, moving beyond mere distribution matching.

title: Schema-Adaptive Action-Conditioned JEPA for Cross-Machine CNC Transfer under Partial Sensor Overlap
summary: This paper studies Schema-Adaptive Action-Conditioned JEPA (SAAC-JEPA) for cross-machine CNC transfer, addressing challenges in deploying industrial world models across varying dynamics, sensing interfaces, and control units.

title: Distilling Foundation Models for Agentic What-If Reasoning:Cost, Latency, and Governance in a Hybrid LLM+SLM Architecture
summary: This paper explores distilling foundation models into compact student models to enable practical, low-latency 'Agentic What-If Reasoning' within interactive agentic loops, addressing performance limitations of large models.

title: LLMs as Master Forgers: Generating Synthetic Time Series Data for Manufacturing
summary: This paper introduces a novel framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate synthetic time series data for manufacturing processes, addressing the scarcity of labeled data in real-world industrial settings.

title: LLM Inference in a Flash!
summary: This article discusses the increasing demands and challenges associated with serving Large Language Model (LLM) inference as a critical workload for various downstream applications.

title: Z-Loss Backward Geometry in Dense Output Heads and Sparse Routers
summary: This paper analyzes the application of Z-loss in language-model output heads and sparse mixture-of-experts routers, detailing how it constrains softmax log-normalizers to improve training stability and reduce roundoff exposure.

title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration
summary: This paper proposes Decoy Direction Optimization, a post-hoc defense mechanism against LLM abliteration techniques like Refusal Feature Ablation (RFA) that can bypass safety guardrails in open-weight language models.

title: How I learned to stop worrying and love StopGrads: Stationarity, Convergence, and a case study on Flow Map Learning
summary: This paper introduces a stopgrad regression principle to theoretically ground the use of stopgrads in training machine learning models, investigating their impact on gradients, stationary points, and convergence guarantees.

title: Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder
summary: This paper proposes a new method, "Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder," to remove specific knowledge from trained Large Language Models (LLMs) without complete retraining, addressing limitations of existing weight-based approaches.

title: Efficient Reasoning Distillation: Small Video-Language Models via Synthetic CoT and Difficulty-Aware Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper presents an efficient method for 'Reasoning Distillation' to instill reasoning capabilities into compact video-language models (VLMs) for video question answering, using synthetic chain-of-thought and difficulty-aware fine-tuning.

title: Differentially Private Semantic Plans for Aggregate Insight Generation
summary: This paper describes a method for generating Differentially Private Semantic Plans to provide end-to-end differential privacy for aggregate insights derived from data-dependent clusters, focusing on privacy-preserving data analysis.

title: Drift Field Net: Learning Ocean Lagrangian advection fields from in-situ and satellite observations
summary: This paper introduces Drift Field Net (DFN), a method for learning ocean Lagrangian advection fields from observational data to improve forecasts of particle drift, particularly relevant for plastic debris accumulation zones.

title: Agentic Search Spaces for Tabular Machine Learning
summary: This paper investigates the practical value of LLM-based agentic AI systems in designing extended hyperparameter optimization (HPO) search spaces for tabular machine learning, exploring their capabilities beyond traditional applications.

title: Robust Fault Detection in Mechanical Multimodal Time Series via Self-Supervised Cross-Modal Reconstruction
summary: This paper presents a method for robust fault detection in industrial systems by using self-supervised cross-modal reconstruction on mechanical multimodal time series data, aiming for early identification of abnormal behavior.

title: Generative models for simulation based filtering: Formulations and Empirical Comparisons
summary: This paper presents a unified formulation and numerical comparison of generative-model approaches for the nonlinear filtering problem. It analyzes how different approaches realize the analysis step by transporting the forecast distribution to the posterior.

title: Channel-Informed Neural Network for Physical Layer Key Generation
summary: This research proposes a channel-informed neural network for physical-layer key generation, enabling wireless devices to establish shared keys from reciprocal channel observations. This method is attractive for lightweight key establishment in resource-constrained edge networks.

title: Multi-Label Proportion Learning for Sea-Ice Type Prediction
summary: This paper addresses sea-ice type prediction, crucial for climate monitoring and maritime navigation, using multi-label proportion learning on manually produced ice charts from satellite imagery. It aims to improve prediction despite challenges from sparse and ambiguous label data.

title: Federated stochastic bilevel optimization with fully first-order gradients
summary: This paper investigates federated stochastic bilevel optimization, a method widely applied in machine learning, focusing on an approach that uses fully first-order gradients. It aims to address the computational burden of existing algorithms that often require second-order Hessian and Jacobian matrices.

title: Autonomous Droplet Navigation via Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research explores autonomous droplet navigation in lab-on-a-chip platforms using model-based reinforcement learning. The goal is to achieve precise manipulation of liquid droplets through complex geometries, which is challenging due to their physical properties.

title: Certified Uncertainty Propagation in One-Shot Federated Bayesian Models via Posterior Event Transport
summary: This paper addresses the probabilistic certification of Bayesian neural networks by lower-bounding the posterior probability of a model satisfying a verifier-defined safety property. It applies posterior event transport to one-shot federated Bayesian learning, where aggregated parameters form the deployed model.

title: Bounded Adjustment with Reliability-Guided Embedding for Imbalanced Learning with Noisy Labels
summary: This paper introduces BARGE (Bounded Adjustment with Reliability-Guided Embeddings), a single-stage approach for imbalanced learning with noisy labels. It aims to prevent frequency correction from amplifying incorrectly labeled minority examples, a common failure mode in class-balanced learning.

title: Attention Mean Fields Predict Average Representation Dynamics and Reveal Context-Specific Computation
summary: This paper introduces a mean-field analysis of attention to predict average representation dynamics in language models. It aims to faithfully account for the evolving representation geometry of models as they run, revealing context-specific computation.

title: How Good Are Time-Series Foundation Models for Pedestrian Crowd Count Forecasting? A Cross-Dataset Comparative Study
summary: This paper presents a cross-dataset comparative study to evaluate the effectiveness of time-series foundation models for pedestrian crowd count forecasting. It assesses their zero-shot accuracy and overall performance in supporting Intelligent Transportation Systems.

title: Interpreting and Steering LLM Agents for Social Simulations
summary: This paper explores the use of large language model (LLM) agents for social simulations, highlighting their power in understanding human behavior. It focuses on the challenge of interpreting and steering these black-box LLM agents to enhance their value for social science.

title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper introduces OPD-Aha, a method for multimodal on-policy distillation that enhances multimodal reasoning by allowing a teacher model to evaluate student trajectories using rich visual evidence. The approach focuses on how student models misinterpret images early in their processing.

title: Decoder Design Matters for ECG Delineation
summary: This paper investigates the importance of decoder design for accurate Electrocardiogram (ECG) delineation, which identifies boundaries of P waves, QRS complexes, and T waves. It aims to improve AI models' ability to learn and interpret ECGs despite the scarcity of manual annotations.

title: FlowATC: Aircraft Trajectory Prediction via Flow Matching
summary: This paper presents FlowATC, a flow-matching architecture designed for robust aircraft trajectory prediction to support next-generation air traffic control. The model is trained exclusively on historical aircraft trajectories, without route labels or chart supervision.

title: What Does Layer-Importance Reveal About Transformers and State-Space Models?
summary: This paper investigates what layer-importance reveals about Transformers and state-space models (SSMs), the two dominant families of sequence models. It explores the transferability of analytical knowledge from Transformers to SSMs through the lens of layer importance, which underpins compression and selective fine-tuning.

title: On the Importance of Gating: Memorization vs. In-Context Learning in State Space Models
summary: This paper examines the importance of gating mechanisms in State Space Models (SSMs) to understand their role in memorization versus in-context learning. It compares SSMs to Transformers, noting SSMs' favorable computational characteristics despite lagging in performance on some tasks.

title: Divergence Timing and Cumulative Disagreement under KV-Cache Eviction
summary: This paper investigates the effects of KV-cache eviction on autoregressive generation by analyzing divergence timing and cumulative token mismatch. It derives an exact decomposition to understand how perturbations to conditional token distributions lead to cumulative disagreement.

title: Stable by Construction: Variational Latent Markov Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
summary: This paper develops a variational approach using latent Markov operators to improve neural PDE solvers for long-horizon prediction of time-dependent physical systems. It aims to address the accumulation of local errors and distribution shift inherent in autoregressive prediction.

title: GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?
summary: This paper introduces GrowMTP, exploring whether reinforcement learning (RL) can dynamically generate its own draft head for speculative decoding during post-training of large language models. It aims to address the bottleneck of autoregressive rollout generation, which dominates wall-clock time.

title: Right Direction, Wrong Step: Geometric Analysis of Finite-Step Failure in Looped Transformers
summary: This paper provides a geometric analysis of finite-step failure in Looped Transformers, which reuse shared layers for iterative latent reasoning. It investigates why additional iterations can reduce support for a reference answer, clarifying whether an update's direction is locally unhelpful or its displacement is too large.

title: Continuous-Time Machine Learning: A Unified Mathematical Perspective
summary: This paper introduces continuous-time machine learning as a unified mathematical framework for modeling temporal dynamics, particularly for arbitrarily sampled or long-range observations. It addresses the fragmentation of existing CT machine learning branches.

title: A Systematic Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Fault Detection and Line Identification in Electrical Power Grids
summary: This study evaluates machine learning methods for fault detection and line identification in electrical power grids, aiming to improve upon traditional relay protection systems for grids with renewable energy sources. It addresses the challenges of complex fault scenarios in modern power infrastructure.

title: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment
summary: This research introduces TAME, a method for token attribution and masking, to localize emergent misalignment in fine-tuned language models. It investigates how narrow, flawed data can induce harmful behavior beyond the training domain.

title: Lidé možná přestanou chodit na e-shopy. Shoptet se připravuje na svět, v němž bude nakupovat AI
summary: Shoptet, a Czech e-commerce platform, is preparing for a future where AI will handle online shopping, as discussed by its Product and Technology Director. The article also covers the platform's European expansion and the changing landscape for online retailers due to AI.

title: Few-Shot Degradation Is Not What It Seems: Behavioral Evidence, Representation Analysis, and a Random-Text Control Across 12 Models, 2 Tasks, and 2 Architectures
summary: This study investigates "few-shot degradation," where few-shot prompting can degrade language model performance, across 12 open-weight models and two tasks. It analyzes this effect through behavioral evidence and representation analysis, finding it to be strongly task-dependent.

title: The Functionalizer: Lossless Functional Decomposition for Subword Tokenization
summary: This paper introduces "The Functionalizer," a new lossless pre-tokenization method designed to overcome the limitations of standard subword tokenizers. It aims to prevent fragmented embedding spaces and lossy normalization of orthographic variations.

title: Optimal Model Activation Policies for Inference Networks of Large Language Models
summary: This research explores optimal model activation policies for inference networks composed of multiple expert large language models. The goal is to manage cost-performance trade-offs in NLP tasks by synergistically using LLMs.

title: Single Document Extractive Summarization using Domination in Hypergraph
summary: This study proposes a novel method for single document extractive text summarization by leveraging the concept of domination in hypergraphs. It aims to extract relevant and important information from documents more effectively.

title: Latent Undertow: How Ordinary Typos Break Probes
summary: This research reveals how ordinary typos, while not affecting an LLM's substantive response, significantly disrupt probes designed to detect malicious prompts by reading hidden states. It highlights a robustness issue in model interpretability.

title: Bias Audits Detect Bias but Disagree on Ranking: Evidence from Ten Instruments and Ten Frontier Models
summary: This study evaluates ten bias audit instruments across ten frontier models, finding that while these tools detect bias, they often disagree on model rankings. It raises concerns about the reliability of current AI regulation and audit practices.

title: Comment on arXiv:2607.01233: Survivorship Bias in Published-Paper Baselines for Research-Idea Distributions
summary: This comment critiques a prior paper's methodology, highlighting a survivorship bias issue when using published papers as a human baseline to evaluate LLM-generated research ideas. It points out a potential flaw in the distributional evaluation.

title: Crash Narrative-Guided Countermeasure Recommendation Using Large Language Models: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Intersection Safety
summary: This paper introduces a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework that uses Large Language Models to recommend traffic safety countermeasures based on crash narratives. This approach aims to make identifying crash mechanisms and recommending solutions more scalable than traditional expert judgment.

title: Self-reported archetypes and behavioral failures in Large Language Models
summary: This research explores self-reported archetypes and behavioral failures in Large Language Models to understand their inherent traits and moral preferences. It investigates the persistent dispositions that shape how LLMs interact, comply, and err.

title: NepKANUN: A RAG-Based Nepali Legal Assistant
summary: NepKANUN is introduced as an AI-powered, RAG-based legal assistant tailored for Nepali legal texts, built on a fine-tuned large language model. It aims to improve access to legal information in Nepal by providing precise and streamlined answers.

title: Nepali Legal Expertise through Generative and Extractive Pre-trained Transformers (NepLEGiT)
summary: NepLEGiT leverages generative and extractive pre-trained transformers to provide Nepali legal expertise, addressing challenges in accessing legal information and the shortage of legal experts in Nepal. It aims to overcome language barriers and information fragmentation.

title: ViCo: Visual-oriented Coding with Self-Reflection for Chart Replication
summary: ViCo is a new method that enhances AI agents' ability to generate high-quality academic charts by integrating visual-oriented coding with self-reflection. This approach aims to achieve stylistic and semantic fidelity comparable to human-authored designs.

title: Are We Grading Properly? Understanding Failure Modes in Medical Benchmarks
summary: This paper critically examines the reliability and failure modes of rubric-based grading in medical benchmarks, especially for open-ended outputs. It questions the effectiveness of current scalable evaluation methods in medical assessment.

title: Retrieval-Driven Memory Reconsolidation for Long-Term LLM Agents
summary: This research introduces a novel memory system for long-term LLM agents that employs retrieval-driven memory reconsolidation. It aims to improve memory evolution by treating retrieval as a driver of updates, rather than just an endpoint of access.

title: State of Thought Enables Endogenous Reasoning
summary: This paper presents "State of Thought" (SoT), a new test-time compute approach for Large Language Models that enables endogenous reasoning. It aims to improve LLM capabilities by reducing reliance on external control or costly search space expansion.

title: Towards Scalable RLVR: Multimodal Instruction Following Data Synthesis and Distillation
summary: This research explores data synthesis and distillation for Multimodal Instruction Following to enable scalable Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). It aims to improve training paradigms for building more capable generalist agents.

title: Efficient Multimodal Generative Recommendation with Latent Narrative Reasoning
summary: This research paper introduces a new method for efficient multimodal generative recommendation that reformulates item prediction as semantic identifier generation, using latent narrative reasoning.

title: The Immutable Past: Formalizing State Mutability and Conflict Resolution in Mutable RAG
summary: This paper formalizes state mutability and conflict resolution in mutable Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, which serve as primary memory architectures for autonomous agents, to address 'Semantic Shadowing' issues.

title: The Imitation Game: When LLMs Learn to Reason Like Programs via Code-Centric Reasoning Data Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes MIMIC, a framework that uses executable code to synthesize reasoning data, enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve deterministic, fine-grained reasoning capabilities.

title: RAG-CT: Mitigating Privacy Risks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Scanning Prompt Distribution
summary: This paper introduces RAG-CT, a method designed to mitigate privacy risks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems by scanning prompt distribution, aiming to prevent information leakage.

title: Spurious Tool Use: When RL Agents Learn the Wrong Reason to Act
summary: This research investigates how reinforcement learning (RL) agents, particularly those using Large Language Models (LLMs), can develop spurious tool use by learning incorrect reasons to act.

title: Efficient One-to-Many Translation with Joint Multi-Stream Diffusion
summary: This research explores how a joint multi-stream diffusion framework can enable efficient one-to-many multilingual machine translation, addressing computational expenses of autoregressive systems.

title: StalePO: Anchored Token-Level Preference Optimization using Legacy Post-Edits in Machine Translation
summary: This paper introduces StalePO, a method for anchored token-level preference optimization in machine translation, using legacy human post-edits to update newer models efficiently.

title: How Humans and LLMs Read Gender into Gender-Neutral Physical Descriptions
summary: This research examines how both humans and Large Language Models (LLMs) infer gender from supposedly gender-neutral physical descriptions, highlighting potential biases in descriptive language.

title: Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper proposes using 'Register Tokens' to enable bounded-state reasoning in diffusion language models (dLLMs), allowing them to continue reasoning without keeping all generated text in context.

title: ParsHate: A Benchmark Dataset for Hate and Target Detection in Persian
summary: This paper introduces ParsHate, a new manually annotated dataset of 10,000 Persian tweets, serving as the first decade-long benchmark for hate speech and target detection in Persian.

title: Negation Beyond the Verbal Channel: Temporal Multimodal Correlates in Dialogue
summary: This research investigates multimodal behavioral information, beyond linguistic realization, that correlates with negation cues in spoken dialogue.

title: ReMova: Fine-tuning LLMs for English to Belarusian translation
summary: This paper presents ReMova, a Belarusian-specific data-cleaning pipeline and fine-tuning methodology for English-Belarusian machine translation, addressing orthography and noise challenges.

title: Early-Bird Decoding: Accelerating Diffusion LLMs with Learnable Block Sizes and Parallel Sampling
summary: This paper introduces Early-Bird Decoding, a method to accelerate diffusion Large Language Models (LLMs) by using learnable block sizes and parallel sampling for more efficient inference.

title: Beyond the Name: Demographic Leakage in De-Identified R\'esum\'es and Evaluation Artifacts in LLM Bias Audits
summary: This research reveals 'demographic leakage' in de-identified resumes, showing that Large Language Models (LLMs) can still infer ethnocultural information during bias audits despite redaction.

title: Competence-Preserving Resume Perturbations Expose Presentation Sensitivity in LLM Screening
summary: This study demonstrates that Large Language Model (LLM) resume screeners exhibit sensitivity to superficial presentation changes, even when underlying candidate competence remains identical.

title: Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data
summary: This paper proposes Style-Debiased DPO, a method for updating Large Language Model (LLM) knowledge by using factuality-aware synthetic preference data to improve recall and accuracy.

title: PunGraph: Retrieval-Enhanced Phonetic-Semantic Graph Reasoning for Pun Understanding
summary: This paper introduces PunGraph, a novel method utilizing retrieval-enhanced phonetic-semantic graph reasoning to improve Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to understand puns.

title: Challenges of Auditing: Variability in Outputs of Large Language Models for Health
summary: This research highlights systematic variability in outputs of Large Language Models (LLMs) used for health advice across different access modes, posing significant challenges for auditing and safety.

title: RoleBreak: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Role-Playing Robustness in Spoken Dialogue
summary: This paper introduces RoleBreak, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the long-horizon robustness of speech-to-speech dialogue models in role-playing scenarios.

title: Quantifying Organizational Environmental Action from Web Data and Large Language Models
summary: This research presents a scalable computational framework using Large Language Models (LLMs) to quantify organizational environmental actions from public web data, addressing challenges in environmental data science.

title: Rewarding Reasoning, Not Answers: Fixing and Bounding Test-Time Reinforcement Learning on Medical QA
summary: This research investigates test-time reinforcement learning on medical multiple-choice QA, revealing that while effective in mathematics, it causes accuracy stagnation and reduced output diversity in a medical context. It analyzes the limitations and behavior of the method in this specific application.

title: DiaWhisper-DPO: Role-Attributed Transcription of Clinical Interviews via Failure-Mined Preference Optimization
summary: This paper introduces DiaWhisper-DPO, a method utilizing failure-mined preference optimization for role-attributed transcription of clinical interviews, specifically for automated depression screening. It focuses on accurately attributing utterances to clinicians or patients.

title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes the 'Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation,' a new conversational benchmark designed to assess the capabilities of large language models for safe stroke care in Japanese. It evaluates clinical history taking, urgency assessment, and safety aspects of LLM performance.

title: TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization
summary: This research introduces TIAO (Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization), a novel reinforcement learning method aimed at improving large language models' performance in text summarization. It focuses on condensing content while preserving consistency and coherence by being aware of token importance.

title: Benchmarking Factual Robustness of LLMs via Multi-conversation Persuasion
summary: This paper presents a new methodology for benchmarking the factual robustness of large language models against 'persuasion attacks,' which involve injecting misinformation or enforcing counterfactuals through multi-conversation interactions. This addresses a critical safety concern as LLMs become primary knowledge retrieval interfaces.

title: Smarter by the Moment: Environment-Driven Dynamic Policies for Continual LLM Improvement
summary: This research explores environment-driven dynamic policies for continual improvement of large language models, aiming to enable them to adapt to evolving tasks and environments. It addresses the limitations of existing memory-augmented approaches that retrieve individual examples.

title: A Data-free Universal Prior over Syntactic Structures
summary: This paper investigates the existence of a data-free universal prior over syntactic structures, exploring whether parts of language's probabilistic structure can arise independently of language-specific data. This has fundamental implications for theories of language and large language models.

title: Reduplicative constructions in Mandarin: Socio-emotional profiling through distributional semantics
summary: This study uses distributional semantics for socio-emotional profiling of reduplicative constructions in Mandarin Chinese, analyzing how the repetition of words or their constituents conveys varied meanings. It explores aspects like plurality, valence coloring, and pragmatic functions.

title: Cascade: Hierarchical Recoverability Control for Large Language Model Unlearning
summary: This research proposes 'Cascade,' a hierarchical recoverability control method for large language model unlearning, designed to remove sensitive or copyrighted knowledge. It aims to prevent residual knowledge from being recovered from intermediate representations, ensuring utility preservation.

title: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
summary: This paper introduces RiskChainBench, a new benchmark for evaluating the ability of AI systems to restore obfuscated platform messages and conduct evidence-grounded web investigations. It addresses challenges posed by platform abuse campaigns that use disguised links and symbols.

title: Deconstructing Stereotypes: Scope-Conditioned Generation for Effective Multilingual Counterspeech
summary: This research introduces 'Scope-Conditioned Generation,' a method for generating more effective multilingual counterspeech to combat online hate speech. It aims to produce targeted and nuanced responses that deconstruct stereotypes, moving beyond generic replies.

title: Lit3R: Retrieve-Relate-Read for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Scientific Literature
summary: This paper describes Lit3R (Retrieve-Relate-Read), a system for evidence-grounded question answering over scientific literature, developed for the LitTraceQA shared task. Lit3R combines off-the-shelf retrieval, reranking, and large language models to identify evidence and generate answers.

title: HUMAID-NER: A Disaster Tweet Dataset for Joint Named Entity Recognition and Event Classification via Uncertainty-Weighted Multitask Learning
summary: This paper introduces HUMAID-NER, the first named entity recognition dataset built on disaster tweets, designed for joint named entity recognition and event classification via uncertainty-weighted multitask learning. It provides span-level entity annotations important for humanitarian response.

title: Target-Language Generation in Multilingual Models: Activation Steering and Optimal Control
summary: This research develops an optimal control method, including activation steering, to enhance target-language text generation in multilingual models. It also proposes a framework for evaluating the quality of the generated text in specific target languages.

title: Nameless Tokenization: A Lossless Tokenizer-Level Defense Against Control-Token Forgery in Open-Weight LLMs
summary: This research proposes 'Nameless Tokenization,' a lossless tokenizer-level defense mechanism against control-token forgery in open-weight large language models. This defense aims to prevent manipulation of chat templates and reserved identifiers through prompt text.

title: Autoformalizing Argumentative Material Inferences
summary: This paper explores methods for 'autoformalizing argumentative material inferences' to make natural language arguments machine-checkable. It addresses the challenge of making implicit premises, warrants, and exceptions explicit for formal verification.

title: The Role of Implicit and Explicit Demographic Signals in Large Language Model-based Student Assessment
summary: This research investigates the impact of implicit and explicit demographic signals in large language model-based student assessment. It discusses the ethical dilemma between potentially improving readability for diverse users and the risk of introducing bias.

title: PaperDoctor: Evidence-Grounded and Actionable Feedback for Scientific Papers in Progress
summary: This paper introduces 'PaperDoctor,' a system designed to provide evidence-grounded and actionable feedback for scientific papers in progress. It aims to scale the process of identifying flaws and offering traceable suggestions, similar to human advisors.

title: Can LLMs Follow the Pulse of a Crisis? Evaluating Crisis Sentiment in Bangladesh's July Uprising
summary: This research evaluates the capability of large language models to perform crisis sentiment analysis in Bangla, a low-resource language, using the newly introduced UNRESTSENT200K dataset. The dataset comprises approximately 200,000 social media comments related to Bangladesh's July-August 2024 uprising.

title: EviScope: Paired Counterfactual Evidence Diagnostics for Faithful and Efficient Grounded Language Models
summary: This paper introduces 'EviScope,' a new paired counterfactual benchmark designed for evidence diagnostics to evaluate the faithfulness and efficiency of grounded language models. It addresses issues where correct answers might be unsupported or drawn from incorrect sources.

title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
summary: This paper studies counterfactual self-explanations in large language models to assess the faithfulness of their generated explanations to their actual behavior. It investigates how models minimally edit inputs to change their own predictions.

title: MechReason: Benchmarking Multi-Image Multi-Hop Reasoning in Mechanical Engineering
summary: This paper introduces MechReason, a new benchmark for evaluating multi-image, multi-hop reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models in the mechanical engineering domain. It aims to address gaps in current evaluation methods for complex reasoning tasks.

title: DenseFace: Bias Mitigation in Face Recognition via Density-Aware Probabilistic Matching
summary: This research proposes DenseFace, a method to mitigate demographic biases in face recognition models using density-aware probabilistic matching. It aims to improve fairness without degrading recognition accuracy or imposing training constraints.

title: Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment for Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: This paper explores Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment as an AI method to improve the accessibility and scalability of Spatial Transcriptomics in biomedical research. It addresses challenges like high operational costs and experimental noise in gene expression mapping.

title: SceneBench: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Vision-Language Understanding of 3D Scenes
summary: This paper introduces SceneBench, a hierarchical benchmark designed to improve the evaluation of vision-language models' 3D spatial reasoning capabilities. It addresses limitations in existing 3D datasets by incorporating richer visual features.

title: ProtoLIP: From Sentence-Level to Object-Level Evidence Disentanglement
summary: This research introduces ProtoLIP, a method for disentangling evidence in query-conditioned vision-language models to achieve more fine-grained, object-specific interpretations. It aims to improve how models reveal visual evidence in response to textual queries.

title: Sequence Recognition in Bharatnatyam dance
summary: This paper investigates sequence recognition in Bharatanatyam dance, focusing on identifying "Adavu" variations which comprise specific motions and postures. It applies AI techniques to analyze this traditional Indian classical dance form.

title: Reasoning with Image Generation
summary: This research explores integrating image generation with chain-of-thought reasoning to overcome limitations of text-only reasoning for tasks requiring visual manipulation. It aims to enable large language models to decompose problems using visual representations.

title: Decentralized Gossip Learning and Federated Averaging for Histopathology Image Classification
summary: This study compares decentralized gossip learning and server-based Federated Averaging for breast histopathology image classification, addressing privacy and governance constraints in distributed medical data analysis. It explores distributed learning techniques for healthcare applications.

title: A multimodal large language model for evidence-based autism spectrum disorder screening
summary: This paper introduces ASDchat, a specific multimodal large language model designed for evidence-based autism spectrum disorder (ASD) screening. It aims to address the bottleneck in early ASD diagnosis caused by specialist scarcity and subjective assessment tools.

title: MDN-Control: Mask-Depth-Noise Guided Region Control for Multi-Subject Video Editing
summary: This research introduces MDN-Control, a mask-depth-noise guided region control method for multi-subject video editing. It aims to improve subject modification, prevent attribute leakage, and handle occlusion ambiguity in generative video tasks.

title: VPRef: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces VPRef, a cross-domain benchmark for Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation (RRSIS). It aims to evaluate and address performance degradation issues in practical deployments of vision-language models for Earth observation.

title: Which Pretext Task Transfers? Self-Supervised Pretraining Objectives for Lung Ultrasound
summary: This study investigates which self-supervised pretraining objectives, such as contrastive learning or masked reconstruction, are most effective for lung ultrasound image analysis. It aims to reduce the reliance on labeled medical images by optimizing pretext tasks for self-supervised learning.

title: Vision And Text Transformer For Predicting Answerability On Visual Question Answering
summary: This research proposes a Vision and Text Transformer for predicting answerability in Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks. It aims to provide more nuanced answerable scores between images and questions than traditional binary mapping approaches.

title: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation: An Adaptive Step Schedule Controller for Diffusion Models
summary: This paper proposes an adaptive step schedule controller for diffusion models to enhance the efficiency of text-to-image generation. It dynamically adjusts the number of denoising steps based on input prompt complexity, optimizing for both speed and image quality.

title: GraLoD: Graphics-Inspired Continuous Level-of-Detail Learning for Image Restoration
summary: This research introduces GraLoD (Graphics-Inspired Continuous Level-of-Detail Learning) as a novel method for image restoration. It addresses the varying spatial support required by different degradation types by learning representation scales dynamically, moving beyond fixed multi-scale hierarchies.

title: FLAT: Resampling Image and Text into 1D Flexible-Length Aligned Transmodal Tokens for Retrieval and Generation
summary: This paper introduces FLAT, a method for multimodal representation learning that resamples image and text into 1D flexible-length aligned transmodal tokens. It aims to improve generative performance by bridging the gap between traditional two-stage multimodal learning and generation.

title: FRPSS: Feature Rearrangement in Pre-Shape Space for Single-Image Generation
summary: This research introduces FRPSS (Feature Rearrangement in Pre-Shape Space), a novel method for single-image generation. It aims to improve the balance between global structural integrity and local diversity in generated images by providing explicit structural constraints.

title: A Vision-Language Foundation Model for Precise and Comprehensive Brain Tumor Diagnosis from Preoperative Multimodal Data
summary: This paper presents the development of a vision-language foundation model designed for precise and comprehensive brain tumor diagnosis using preoperative multimodal MRI data. It aims to address challenges in non-invasive presurgical diagnosis.

title: SAVOR: Self-Aware Visual Grounding via Confidence-Calibrated Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Hallucination Mitigation
summary: This research introduces SAVOR, a method for mitigating multimodal hallucinations in large language models using self-aware visual grounding and confidence-calibrated reinforcement learning. It aims to improve the trustworthiness of MLLMs by preventing ungrounded claims.

title: G3AR: Graph-Guided Neural Visual Geometry for Scalable Multi-Sequence Aerial Registration
summary: This paper introduces G3AR, a graph-guided neural visual geometry framework designed for scalable multi-sequence aerial image registration, addressing challenges in processing thousands of images. It improves how irregular non-local overlap is handled in aerial collections.

title: EgoPathBench: Evaluating Zero-Shot Egocentric Waypoint Decision-Making in Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces EgoPathBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the zero-shot egocentric waypoint decision-making capabilities and integrated spatial intelligence of vision-language models.

title: JewelTry: Mask-Free Scale Aware Jewelry Virtual Try-On
summary: This paper presents JewelTry, a mask-free and scale-aware virtual try-on method specifically developed for jewelry, aiming to improve online shopping visualization despite challenges like small item size.

title: Can Knowledge Transfer Parameters Be Learned? LePoKet for Efficient Robotic Vision
summary: This paper proposes LePoKet, a method that learns knowledge transfer parameters from larger pretrained models to achieve efficient perception for robotic systems operating under computational constraints.

title: What Do Hallucinations Reveal About Multimodal Reasoning? Diagnosing Visual Grounding Failures via Contrastive Decoding Probes
summary: This research investigates what hallucinations reveal about multimodal reasoning in large vision-language models, using contrastive decoding probes to diagnose visual grounding failures.

title: ViD: Vision-Dominant Gender Bias Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces ViD, a novel method for mitigating gender bias in large vision-language models by focusing on dynamic visual bias mitigation, addressing limitations of current training or post-hoc calibration approaches.

title: SAVTrack: Selective Vote Aggregation for Reliability-Aware Point Cloud Tracking
summary: This paper proposes SAVTrack, a method for selective vote aggregation to improve reliability-aware 3D single object tracking in LiDAR point clouds, especially under sparse and incomplete observations.

title: Bridging the Perceptual Gap: Residual-Enhanced Downscaling and Manifold-Aware Perception Alignment Adaptation for NR-IQA
summary: This paper proposes a method to enhance No-Reference Image Quality Assessment by using residual-enhanced downscaling and manifold-aware perception alignment adaptation to bridge the perceptual gap in models like CLIP.

title: Lesion-centered 3D mapping of colonoscopy procedures: validation of a hierarchical ensemble pipeline on public benchmark videos
summary: This paper validates a hierarchical ensemble pipeline for lesion-centered 3D mapping of colonoscopy procedures, aiming to preserve spatial information from recorded videos that is typically discarded.

title: Efficient Quantization-Aware Distillation with Cross-Modal Alignment for Edge Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper proposes an efficient quantization-aware distillation method with cross-modal alignment to enable the deployment of large vision-language models like CLIP on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: Efficient 3D Whole-Body PET Image Denoising via Conditional Rectified Flow With Optimized Sampling Strategy
summary: This paper proposes an efficient method for 3D whole-body PET image denoising using conditional rectified flow with an optimized sampling strategy to address noise in ultra-low-dose imaging.

title: MAETrack: Unleashing the Potential of Pretrained Geometric Priors for 3D Single Object Tracking
summary: This paper introduces MAETrack, a method that leverages pretrained geometric priors from self-supervised 3D encoders to improve 3D single object tracking, addressing limitations in direct fine-tuning.

title: PriorPose: Reference-Guided Joint Deformation and Alignment for Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
summary: This paper proposes PriorPose, a method for category-level object pose estimation that employs reference-guided joint deformation and alignment to accurately recover similarity transforms for unseen instances.

title: De-GAN - Dynamic Parameter Tuned GAN for 3D Medical Image Segmentation: A Step Towards Generalisation
summary: This paper introduces DE-GAN, a dynamic parameter-tuned conditional GAN that combines input-adaptive dynamic convolutions for improved 3D medical image segmentation, specifically for brain tumors.

title: FSANet: Frequency-Spatial Aware Network for Image Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces FSANet, a Frequency-Spatial Aware Network designed for image segmentation that aims to improve performance under challenging conditions while being computationally efficient.

title: IMVS: Interactive Medical Volume Segmentation with Test-Time Adaptation - A New Method for Annotating Radiology Datasets
summary: This paper introduces IMVS, an interactive method for medical volume segmentation that uses test-time adaptation to make the annotation of large radiology datasets more efficient.

title: Unifying Semantic Priors and High-Frequency Traces: Enhancing V-JEPA with Mixture-of-Experts for Robust Synthetic Image Forensics
summary: This paper enhances V-JEPA with a Mixture-of-Experts approach to develop robust synthetic image forensics, aiming to improve the detection of manipulated images and combat misinformation.

title: TEDi: Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer for Surgical Instrument Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces TEDi, a Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer designed for surgical instrument segmentation, which improves upon existing query-based methods by incorporating temporal information.

title: Hyper-RED: Scalable Event Pre-training via Semantic Hypergraph Distillation
summary: This paper proposes Hyper-RED, a method for scalable event representation pre-training that utilizes semantic hypergraph distillation to overcome the scarcity of large-scale annotated event data.

title: What Breaks Local Watermarks? A Robustness Benchmark for Local Invisible Image Watermarking
summary: This paper introduces a new robustness benchmark for local invisible image watermarking, designed to evaluate the effectiveness of payload recovery and locality in selected image regions.

title: StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection
summary: This paper introduces StackTok, a method to accelerate VLM inference by using budget-adaptive visual token selection, reducing overhead without retraining.

title: FAHCD-Net: Frequency-Adaptive Heatmap-Conditional Diffusion Networks for Robust Facial Landmark Detection
summary: This paper proposes FAHCD-Net, a method using frequency-adaptive heatmap-conditional diffusion networks for robust facial landmark detection, particularly in challenging conditions.

title: RegRet: Enhancing Region-Level Retrieval in Large Multimodal Models
summary: This research introduces RegRet, a method to enhance region-level retrieval in Large Multimodal Models by aligning image regions with textual descriptions.

title: TecoPrompt: Temporal-Conservative Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper proposes TecoPrompt, a temporal-conservative prompt-learning framework that addresses label noise during few-shot supervision for Vision-Language Models like CLIP.

title: Measuring Annotation Efficiency for Handwritten Devanagari Recognition: Sample-Complexity Curves for Four Pretraining Regimes
summary: This research measures annotation efficiency for handwritten Devanagari recognition using sample-complexity curves across four pretraining regimes.

title: tcnerv:dual-domain temporal context modeling for implicit neural video compression
summary: This paper introduces tcnerv, a dual-domain temporal context modeling method for implicit neural video compression, aiming to minimize reconstruction distortion.

title: SPEAR NeXT Causal Latent Forecasting Across Multiple Horizons for Spectral Temporal Earth Representation Learning
summary: SPEAR NeXT is introduced as a pixel-wise multimodal spectral temporal foundation model for Earth representation learning, focusing on causal latent forecasting.

title: NeuroTS-Net: Multi-Class Semantic Segmentation of Pediatric Brain Tumors in Multi-Modal MRI
summary: This paper presents NeuroTS-Net, a method for multi-class semantic segmentation of pediatric brain tumors using multi-modal MRI, to support diagnosis and treatment planning.

title: Accelerated Decoding of Centroid Positional Encoding for Instance Segmentation
summary: This research focuses on accelerating the decoding of centroid positional encoding for instance segmentation, aiming to reduce the significant execution cost of this stage.

title: Multi-modal Knowledge Preserving Adapter for Embedding Backward Compatibility
summary: This paper introduces a multi-modal knowledge preserving adapter to ensure embedding backward compatibility, addressing the issue of costly database re-indexing when upgrading embedding models.

title: VOR-Bench: A Human Perception-Driven Benchmark for Video Object Removal
summary: VOR-Bench is a new human perception-driven benchmark for evaluating video object removal, addressing limitations in existing evaluation paradigms and aligning metrics with human preference.

title: PiPS: Post-Hoc Prototypical Explanations for Interpretable Semantic Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces PiPS, a method for post-hoc prototypical explanations to achieve interpretable semantic segmentation, enhancing trust in deep neural networks.

title: NeuroSymbEAD: A Large Scale Neuro-Symbolic Caption Dataset for Omni-Directional Embodied Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper introduces NeuroSymbEAD, a large-scale neuro-symbolic caption dataset featuring an ego-centric knowledge graph, designed for omni-directional embodied autonomous driving.

title: Bi-MoDe: Bilateral Control-based Imitation Learning via Modifier-Conditioned Decoding for Modulation of Execution Speed and Contact Intensity
summary: This paper presents Bi-MoDe, a bilateral control-based imitation learning method that uses modifier-conditioned decoding for robotic manipulation tasks.

title: World-Action Models for Robot Learning and Control: A Survey
summary: This paper is a survey of World-Action Models for robot learning and control, exploring how robots anticipate the effects of actions in complex, dynamic environments.

title: AssemblyGrid v1: A Benchmark for Multi-Robot Production with Temporary Coalitions, Local Information, and Geometric Constraints
summary: AssemblyGrid v1 is presented as a benchmark for multi-robot production, focusing on challenges like temporary coalitions and decentralized control scenarios.

title: Occupancy Network-Guided Autonomous Robotic Partial Nephrectomy
summary: This paper introduces an occupancy network-guided autonomous system for robotic partial nephrectomy, enabling complete tumor resections in soft-tissue cancer surgery.

title: Tendon-Driven Continuum Robot with Modular Stiffness and In-Situ Self Pose Estimation
summary: This paper presents a self-contained modular tendon-driven continuum robot featuring modular stiffness and in-situ self pose estimation for adaptability in confined environments.

title: ManiSkillFormer: Demonstration-Free Compositional Manipulation via Task-Conditioned Geometric Contracts
summary: ManiSkillFormer is a neuro-symbolic framework for demonstration-free and compositional robotic manipulation, which uses task-conditioned geometric contracts to structure perception and action.

title: Auto-HSI: Personalized human control of a robot swarm on demand by using LLMs for online automatic code generation
summary: Auto-HSI is a method that uses LLMs for online automatic code generation to enable personalized human control of a robot swarm on demand.

title: UDAV: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive VLM Waypoint Planner
summary: This paper introduces UDAV, an Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive VLM Waypoint Planner, enabling vision-language models to generate reliable routes from aerial imagery for UAV-guided UGV off-road navigation.

title: Geometry vs Structure: Graph-Based Diagnostics for LiDAR Point-Cloud Simulation Fidelity
summary: This research proposes graph-based diagnostics to quantify the fidelity of LiDAR point-cloud simulations, which are used to validate autonomous-driving and advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) sensor pipelines.

title: Collision-Aware Humanoid Whole-Body Control under Imperfect Tracking Targets
summary: This paper presents a collision-aware whole-body control method for humanoid robots that tracks motion targets while considering scene geometry to prevent collisions from imperfect target motions.

title: Dense to MoE Adaptation for Compact Vision Language Action Policies
summary: This work explores adapting dense vision-language-action (VLA) policies to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained robot platforms, while maintaining performance.

title: UniDex-ViTac: Learning Unified Visuo-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation Policy from Human Video Data
summary: UniDex-ViTac is a framework that uses human video demonstrations to generate robot-executable data, including fingertip contact observations, for training visuo-tactile dexterous manipulation policies.

title: ProxiDex: Learning Dynamics-Guided Proximity Policy for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: ProxiDex is introduced as a method for learning dynamics-guided proximity policies to improve multi-finger dexterous manipulation, addressing challenges like occluded visual observations and tactile sensor calibration.

title: SAVLA: Symmetry-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
summary: SAVLA (Symmetry-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models) is presented to enhance language-conditioned robot manipulation by inherently encoding geometric information, improving spatial competence beyond pure demonstrations.

title: WholeBodyWAM: Generalizing Pre-trained World-Action Priors to Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via WBC-Grounded Coordination
summary: WholeBodyWAM extends World Action Models (WAMs) to humanoid loco-manipulation by generalizing pre-trained world-action priors through Whole-Body Control (WBC)-grounded coordination, addressing a less explored area in robot manipulation.

title: Weave: Learning Whole-Body Dexterous Loco-Manipulation from Human-Object Interactions
summary: Weave proposes a framework for learning whole-body dexterous loco-manipulation for humanoid robots from human-object interactions, coordinating balance, locomotion, and hand contact to control both robot and object motion.

title: Differentiable Mesh State Estimation via Factor Graph Inference for Deformable Object Reconstruction
summary: This paper proposes a novel factor graph-based framework for differentiable mesh state estimation, enabling probabilistic reconstruction of deformable objects, a fundamental challenge in robotics and simulation.

title: IL-ACT: Imitation Learning with Adaptive Cartesian Tracking Control for a 30-ton Excavator
summary: IL-ACT (Imitation Learning with Adaptive Cartesian Tracking) is a new motion control framework for autonomous excavators, utilizing imitation learning from operator demonstrations to manage complex kinematics and uncertainty.

title: World Models for Embodied Intelligence: From Plausible to Controllable to Actionable
summary: This paper discusses the role of world models in embodied intelligence, highlighting their function in connecting perception and decision-making by anticipating consequences and adapting to improve behavioral capabilities.

title: The Robot Data Factory
summary: This article argues that 'robot experience' derived from continuous physical interaction, rather than just large datasets, is the crucial scientific resource for advancing Physical AI.

title: CorrRisk-WM: Corridor-Conditioned Risk World Modeling for Safety-Critical Trajectory Planning
summary: CorrRisk-WM introduces a Corridor-Conditioned Risk World Model for safety-critical trajectory planning, which forecasts surrounding-agent motion and evaluates trajectory-specific risks for safe local planning.

title: The Latent That Never Was: A Forensic Re-run of the CVAE Ablation in Action Chunking Transformer
summary: This paper provides a forensic re-evaluation of the CVAE ablation in Action Chunking Transformers (ACT), a widely used method for robot manipulation, questioning previous findings regarding the encoder's impact.

title: TEMPO: Learning Temporal Context for Dynamic Robot Manipulation
summary: TEMPO addresses the challenge of dynamic robot manipulation by enabling Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to learn temporal context, overcoming limitations of single-observation inference in dynamic tasks.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Space Robot Operations: Technologies, Challenges and Prospects
summary: This paper surveys the technologies, challenges, and prospects of AI-enabled space robot operations, focusing on improving autonomy and adaptability for long-duration, contact-rich tasks with limited human intervention.

title: Overcoming technical adoption barriers for mobile service robots in rehabilitation
summary: This paper discusses strategies for overcoming technical adoption barriers for mobile service robots in rehabilitation, focusing on advancing their technology readiness levels beyond early-stage development.

title: SWIM: Vision-Language-Grounded Soft Whole-Body Interactive Manipulation
summary: SWIM (Vision-Language-Grounded Soft Whole-Body Interactive Manipulation) is a framework presented for soft and continuum robots, translating language and visual context into executable whole-body actuation for manipulation.

title: BRAVE-6D: Benchmark for Robotic Active Vision in 6DOF Pose Estimation
summary: BRAVE-6D is introduced as a benchmark for Robotic Active Vision in 6DOF Pose Estimation, providing a standardized way to compare approaches for detecting and grasping small objects in robotics.

title: Intrinsic Robot Rewarding: Reusing VLA Representations for Autonomous Evaluation and Policy Improvement
summary: This research introduces Intrinsic Robot Rewarding (IRR), a method that reuses Vision-Language-Action (VLA) representations to autonomously evaluate and improve robot policies.

title: LiLi: Lie Theory Based 3D LiDAR Scan Alignment Degeneracy Detection
summary: This paper presents LiLi, a method for detecting degeneracies in 3D LiDAR scan alignment, which is critical for maintaining localization and mapping accuracy in challenging autonomous navigation scenarios.

title: Fingers as Legs: Learning Self-Supported Locomotion and Manipulation with an Anthropomorphic Hand
summary: This work demonstrates how an anthropomorphic robotic hand can learn self-supported locomotion and manipulation, using its fingers for movement and interaction while being self-contained.

title: Fleet-To-Lab: A Transfer Learning Framework For Lunar Rover Slippage Estimation Via Model Fusion
summary: This paper introduces Fleet-To-Lab, a transfer learning framework that uses model fusion to estimate slippage for autonomous lunar rovers, addressing challenges with limited lunar data.

title: TIO-Former: Ultra-Lightweight 6-Directional ToF-Inertial Odometry for Nano-UAVs via a Streaming Causal Transformer
summary: This research presents TIO-Former, an ultra-lightweight ToF-Inertial Odometry system utilizing a streaming causal Transformer for accurate ego-motion estimation in nano-UAVs, essential for autonomous navigation under strict SWaP-C constraints.

title: FluxVLA Engine: A One-Stop VLA Engineering Platform for Embodied Intelligence
summary: FluxVLA Engine is presented as a comprehensive platform designed for engineering embodied intelligence systems, enabling the development of reliable robot systems from VLA models and other AI methods.

title: DriveMCP: An Agentic AI framework for Advanced Driver Assistance System
summary: DriveMCP is introduced as an agentic AI framework for advanced driver assistance systems, integrating perception, compliance reasoning, and safety arbitration into a modular pipeline.

title: Port-Hamiltonian Koopman Operator Synthesis for Mechanical Systems
summary: This paper explores Port-Hamiltonian Koopman Operator Synthesis to create efficient linear prediction and control models for nonlinear robotic systems, ensuring they respect the underlying energetic structure.

title: CAD-Based Relation Learning and Geometric-Symbolic Planning for Robotic Assembly
summary: This research focuses on using CAD-based relation learning and geometric-symbolic planning to address the combinatorial challenges and data limitations in robotic assembly sequence planning.

title: Online Geometric Change Detection via Scene Decomposition
summary: This framework proposes online geometric change detection via scene decomposition, enabling autonomous robots to identify environmental alterations for improved online planning in dynamic missions.

title: XPACE: Joint World and Action Modeling from Heterogeneous Experience
summary: XPACE is introduced as a unified embodied world model that allows general-purpose robots to learn from diverse experiences, predict actions, and anticipate their effects on the environment.

title: Exact Fusion and Coordinated Exploration in Multi-Robot Active Inference
summary: This work investigates exact fusion and coordinated exploration strategies for multi-robot teams using active inference, allowing them to learn a common environment model and plan actions for information gain.

title: Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability for Hybrid Systems: Unified Goal-Driven Control with Safety Guarantees
summary: This paper discusses Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability for hybrid systems to achieve unified goal-driven control with safety guarantees for robotic systems operating in contact-rich environments.

title: Show HN: A Stateful LLM API that works across providers
summary: For the last year we've been building AI workspaces. With every new product, we found ourselves rebuilding the same context layer and infrastructure. We tried existing solutions, but we'd either have to lock into one provider or have to manage the storage infrastructure. What we wanted was an API that's stateful and isn't tied to a specific provider. So that we didn't have to think about compaction, differing schemas, or running the infrastructure ourselves. Since we'd already built most of the constituent parts, we’ve decided to release Twigg. The API is deliberately simple. You create a chat and get back an ID. When you have a new prompt or tool result, you send that plus the ID. There's no need to store or manage context yourself. It appends the new prompt and assembles the history for you. To switch models, you change one field in the next request. The dashboard covers most of what you'd want to configure: tool schemas, system prompts, context window limits and retention settings. We'd like to hear from anyone who has run into the same problems. How are you hosting your context right now, and what would make you not want to hand it to a third party?
