summary: This paper introduces RideWay, an efficiency-centered benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of tool-using language agents in completing tasks without frustrating users.

title: Multimodal Conditioning of Fine-Tuned Stable Diffusion XL for Controllable and Culturally Faithful Ulos Motif Generation
summary: This study proposes a multimodal generative framework using a fine-tuned Stable Diffusion XL model for controllable and culturally faithful generation of Batak Ulos weaving motifs.

title: Missing Bridges: Composition-Aware Active Imitation Learning
summary: This research explores composition-aware active imitation learning, a method to reduce expert effort by allowing a learner to request specific demonstrations in structured multi-task domains.

title: Anchoring What Matters: A Dual-Level Learning Framework for Visually-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning
summary: This paper presents a dual-level learning framework to improve visually-grounded multimodal reasoning in large vision-language models, addressing optimization bottlenecks in reinforcement learning.

title: The Other Half of the Memory Wall: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD with Trained Routing Prediction
summary: This research addresses the memory wall for serving 35B Mixture-of-Experts models on consumer hardware by proposing a system that leverages SSDs with trained routing prediction.

title: Teaching AI, Robotics, & Community: A Hubs-Based K-12 Education Framework for Reaching Rural Schools
summary: This paper introduces a Hubs-Based K-12 education framework for teaching AI and robotics, aiming to scale learning opportunities, especially for rural schools.

title: Decodability is Not Causality: Dissociating Probe Readouts from Behavioral Drivers via SAE Decomposition
summary: This research argues that linear probes only demonstrate decodability, not causality, regarding safety-relevant concepts in language models, impacting AI interpretability and safety evaluations.

title: When Is Graph Structure Worth Its Cost? The Case for Structure Pricing in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This paper investigates the cost-benefit of graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), proposing 'structure pricing' to assess whether quality gains justify the ingestion cost.

title: AutoTuneBench: Trustworthy Measurement for Agent Auto-Tuning of LLM Serving Engines
summary: This paper introduces AutoTuneBench, a benchmark designed for trustworthy measurement and evaluation of agent auto-tuning processes for LLM serving engines.

title: Designing Agentic AI Workflow Portfolios under Imperfect Selection and Compute Cost
summary: This research focuses on designing agentic AI workflow portfolios, considering multiple reasoning strategies, verification structures, and compute costs under imperfect selection.

title: Symbolic Temporal Supervision of LLM Agents Using Contracts
summary: This paper proposes symbolic temporal supervision using contracts to enhance the reliability and control of LLM agents, especially when performing complex tasks with external tools.

title: WFM: Wiki Foundation Model for Complex Agentic Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces the Wiki Foundation Model (WFM) to provide persistent non-parametric knowledge and long-term memory, which are crucial for complex agentic reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation.

title: Re2A: Situated Conversational Recommendation via Rubric-based Preference Reasoning and Alignment
summary: This paper introduces Re2A, a method for situated conversational recommendation that reasons over dialogue history and co-observed scenes to provide personalized recommendations. It focuses on how recommender assistants can integrate environmental context into dialogue.

title: REPAIR: Resolving Long-Tail Confusion in Scientific Retrievers via Fact-Verified Iterative Refinement
summary: REPAIR is a new method designed to improve the precision of scientific information retrieval by addressing long-tail concepts and fact-sensitivity. It uses fact-verified iterative refinement to enhance dense retrievers and LLM augmentation.

title: BENCHCOMPASS: From Scores to Signals for Training and Harness Decisions in Payment-Domain LLMs
summary: BENCHCOMPASS is a new benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models in the payment domain, providing insights beyond mere scores. It aims to offer signals for training and deployment decisions given the dynamic nature of payment rules.

title: Who Audits Whom, on What Substrate, with What Evidence? An Independence-Graded Audit Protocol for Agentic AI
summary: This paper proposes an independence-graded audit protocol for agentic AI systems, addressing challenges in auditing these autonomous systems. It examines who audits whom, on what substrate, and with what evidence, considering independence as a graded concept.

title: Building Trust in Artificial Intelligence: A Necessity for Railway Applications
summary: This paper discusses the necessity of building trust in AI for railway applications, which are currently restricted to non-safety critical uses due to strict industry standards. It proposes reviewing robustness, interpretability, and privacy to increase compliance and adoption.

title: Where Should Agents Live? Energy-Memory Characterization of Agentic AI for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
summary: This research investigates the energy and memory characteristics of agentic AI workflows, particularly those involving LLMs, within the edge-cloud continuum. It aims to determine optimal deployment strategies for these systems in evolving telecommunication networks.

title: What Counts as Strategic Reasoning? A Systematic Mapping of Chess Research on Humans, Engines, and Language Models
summary: This paper systematically maps chess research to understand strategic reasoning in humans, AI engines, and Large Language Models. It uses chess as a controlled environment to investigate and compare strategic thinking across these entities.

title: Visual Compliance via Executable Safety Rule Entailment
summary: This research proposes a method for achieving visual compliance in LLMs and VLMs by using executable safety rule entailment to manage complex and evolving safety guidelines. It aims to enhance safety systems beyond simple risk pattern recognition.

title: Faithful yet Collusive: Why Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Cannot Detect Collusion in LLM Pricing Agents under Oligopolistic Competition
summary: This paper investigates how LLM pricing agents can engage in tacit collusion to sustain supracompetitive prices, showing that chain-of-thought monitoring cannot detect this behavior. It introduces a causal graph divergence framework to measure faithfulness in these agents.

title: Market Signal Injection: Adversarial Context Manipulation of LLM Pricing Agents
summary: This research introduces "market signal injection" (MSI), an attack that manipulates LLM pricing agents by altering market data presentation without changing numerical values. It shows how such adversarial context manipulation can influence agent behavior.

title: Cultural Competence in Context: A Large Language Model Passes the Turing Test in Finland
summary: This paper reports on a Turing Test conducted in Finland using the Finnish language, where ChatGPT 5.2 demonstrated cultural competence. The study examines how LLMs perform in languages and cultural contexts underrepresented in their training data.

title: WetRobo: A Reproducible Robot Kit for Coding Agents in Biological Laboratories
summary: WetRobo is a reproducible robot kit designed for biological laboratories, enabling researchers to code agents for automating tasks. It provides a general-purpose system for delegating robot tasks without requiring teleoperation or complex neural network training.

title: The Mirage of Calibrated Confidence: Trajectory-Independence of Verbalized Confidence in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research investigates Vision-Language Models' verbalized confidence, discovering it to be largely trajectory-independent. It reveals that VLMs can report high confidence even after self-correction and arriving at an incorrect answer.

title: Collective Loss of Control in LLM Agent Systems: An Epidemic Account of Mutation, Contagion, and Recovery
summary: This paper proposes an epidemic model to explain how a local deviation can lead to collective loss of control in LLM multi-agent systems. It describes the mechanisms of accidental mutation, contagion, and recovery within these systems.

title: Disentangling Long-Term Memory via Latent Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
summary: This research introduces a method for disentangling long-term memory in personalized agents using latent neuro-symbolic reasoning. It aims to improve memory systems by reasoning over long-term history interactions to infer both explicit and implicit preferences.

title: First Token Matters: Understanding Safety Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
summary: This research explores the phenomenon of "safety collapse" in Large Reasoning Models when handling harmful queries, emphasizing the impact of the first token. It seeks to understand the internal mechanisms behind safety alignment degradation.

title: Hyperbolic Graph Representation Learning for Differential Diagnosis on Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
summary: This paper explores hyperbolic graph representation learning for differential diagnosis on biomedical knowledge graphs, leveraging their ability to capture hierarchical and transversal relationships. It investigates whether hyperbolic embeddings can improve diagnostic accuracy.

title: Beyond Routine Compliance: Cunning Data Cultivates Safety Vigilance in Large Language Models
summary: This research explores how "cunning data" can cultivate safety vigilance in Large Language Models, enhancing their ability to detect harmful intent beyond routine compliance. It aims to improve safety alignment even when intent is concealed.

title: Pay Only for Disagreement: Certified No-Regression Verdicts for Model Updates with Matching Label-Complexity Bounds
summary: This paper proposes "certified no-regression verdicts" for model updates, allowing for efficient auditing of changes in production models. It introduces a support identity for auditing risk differences to ensure that updates do not degrade performance.

title: Beyond Static RAG: An Adaptive, Tri-Metric Routing Framework for Efficient Long-Context Inference on Commodity GPUs
summary: This paper introduces an adaptive, tri-metric routing framework to optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for efficient long-context inference on commodity GPUs. It addresses the "Compression Paradox" by managing neural prompt compression, KV cache contention, and preprocessing latency.

title: Where Grokking Happens: Distributed Utility and Fourier Recoding Without a Module Switch
summary: This paper investigates 'grokking' in Transformers, examining where the shift from memorization to generalization occurs and identifying distributed utility gain with a block-0 attention bias.

title: Disentangling Algorithmic Bias from Archival Artifacts: A Controlled Audit of Vision-Language Model Valuation in Metropolitan Museum Archives
summary: This study audits Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP for societal bias using historical artwork metadata from the Metropolitan Museum, aiming to distinguish algorithmic bias from archival artifacts.

title: Temperon: Full-Time SAM Quality at a Third Less Wall-Clock
summary: This paper introduces Temperon, a method that reduces the computational cost of Sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) training by using plain-SGD for the initial training phase.

title: Lecture notes on Physics Informed Neural Networks, Neural Operators, and their applications
summary: This item comprises lecture notes for a PhD course on Physics Informed Neural Networks and Neural Operators, detailing their principles and applications.

title: Fathom: Per-Query Read Depth for Sparse Decoding over Offloaded KV Caches
summary: This paper presents Fathom, a key scan method that optimizes sparse decoding over offloaded KV caches by allowing each query to decide its read depth, addressing traffic bounds in agentic sessions.

title: Regularized Least Squares Training of Quadratic Neural Networks with Applications to System Identification
summary: This paper proposes a regularized least squares approach for training quadratic neural networks, providing a lower bound for the optimization problem with applications in system identification.

title: DSD: Learning Diverse and Reusable Motor Skills via Diffusion Skill Discovery
summary: This paper introduces DSD (Diffusion Skill Discovery), a method for learning diverse and reusable motor skills for simulated characters, enabling efficient task performance across various goals and contexts.

title: The Missing "I Don't Know": Why Three Reasoning-Reliability Findings Converge on Calibrated Abstention
summary: This paper explores why Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle with 'I Don't Know' responses, linking findings on reasoning reliability, tool-reliability, and safety-constrained generation to the concept of calibrated abstention.

title: Accelerating Diffusion Sampling via Speculative Draft Trees
summary: This paper describes a method to accelerate diffusion model sampling using speculative draft trees, which speeds up generation by drafting candidate states and correcting them to preserve the target distribution.

title: Composite-Gradient Learning for Shared Control Authority Between Deep Reinforcement Learning and Model Predictive Control
summary: This paper proposes a composite-gradient learning approach that combines Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) to achieve shared control authority in autonomous systems.

title: REVERSAL-BENCH: A Reversibility Axis and Reset Oracle for Measuring the Reset-Free RL Cliff
summary: This paper introduces REVERSAL-BENCH, a new benchmark with a reversibility axis and reset oracle designed to measure the 'reset-free RL cliff' for continuous policy training in autonomous reinforcement learning.

title: SAM-on-the-Curve: Sharpness-Aware Mode Connectivity for Robust Weight-Space Interpolation
summary: This paper explores SAM-on-the-Curve, a method leveraging sharpness-aware mode connectivity to achieve robust weight-space interpolation in deep neural networks, underpinning techniques like model ensembling.

title: Modular Deep Learning Mechanisms for Auditable Next-Day Wildfire Spread Prediction
summary: This paper proposes modular deep learning mechanisms for auditable next-day wildfire spread prediction, aiming for forecasts that can be evaluated alongside their assumptions and physical fidelity.

title: Principled Koopman Representations with Kalman Inference for Efficient Time-Series Prediction
summary: This paper presents a method for efficient time-series prediction using principled Koopman representations combined with Kalman Inference, addressing mathematical consistency issues in latent Koopman spaces.

title: The Free Inference Dimension: Complexity Measure for Zero-Collision Navigation under Hypothesis Mixtures
summary: This paper introduces 'The Free Inference Dimension,' a complexity measure for zero-collision navigation under hypothesis mixtures, expanding on Solomonoff induction in meta-reinforcement learning.

title: NObSP: Functional Decomposition of Neural Networks via Oblique Subspace Projections
summary: This paper introduces NObSP (Nonlinear Oblique Subspace Projections), a framework for functionally decomposing neural networks to provide explicit per-feature contribution functions and an interaction residual, aiding interpretability.

title: Procedural Pretraining for Molecular Property Prediction
summary: This paper investigates procedural pretraining for molecular property prediction, demonstrating how inductive biases can be learned from abstract, procedurally generated data to overcome small dataset limitations.

title: Adaptive hybrid coupling with operator inference, the overlapping Schwarz alternating method and reinforcement learning
summary: This paper proposes an adaptive hybrid coupling method that combines operator inference, the overlapping Schwarz alternating method, and reinforcement learning for flexible subdomain modeling in transient problems.

title: Hybrid coupling with numerics-informed neural networks and the overlapping Schwarz alternating method
summary: This paper develops a hybrid modeling framework that couples pre-trained numerics-informed neural networks (NINNs) with classical full order models (FOMs) using the overlapping Schwarz alternating method for solving PDEs.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Continual Learning for Open-World Intent Discovery Under an evolving Label Space
summary: This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware probabilistic framework for continual learning and open-world intent discovery in intelligent systems, addressing evolving user intents in dynamic label spaces.

title: Dataset-Dependent Effects of Cross-Depth Aggregation and Soft-Routed Experts in EEG Foundation Model Fine-Tuning
summary: This research explores improving EEG foundation models by augmenting CBraMod with cross-depth Attention Residuals and soft-routed expert banks for better decoding tasks.

title: Long-Context Demonstration Selection Using State Space Models
summary: This paper studies demonstration selection using state space models to optimize example subsets for in-context learning and language model inference, addressing transformer inference costs.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
summary: TabPFN-3.5 is introduced as a new flagship Tabular Foundation Model that significantly outperforms its predecessor and existing baselines, setting a new state of the art in tabular prediction.

title: Walking the Score Manifold: Continuous-time Generative Dynamics on Learned Data Manifolds
summary: This research proposes a new approach to generative modeling for time-dependent data, framing generation as continuous-time evolution on a learned data manifold using pretrained score-based models.

title: EdgeReMIND: A Scalable, Top-Ranked Memorization Baseline for Temporal Multi-Relational Link Prediction
summary: EdgeReMIND is introduced as a scalable memorization baseline for temporal multi-relational link prediction, addressing memory and time budget limitations on large-scale graph datasets.

title: Locating Hidden Failures Makes Long-Horizon Agents More Reliable
summary: This paper discusses improving the reliability of long-horizon AI agents by developing methods to locate hidden failures during autonomous tasks, rather than solely judging by final success.

title: Beyond the Previous Layer: Residual Predictive Structure in Sparse MoE Routing
summary: This research investigates the routing mechanisms in sparse mixture-of-experts models, assessing if the preceding expert selection adequately predicts the next router's choice.

title: ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batched Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Inference
summary: ASPIRE introduces an asynchronous batched self-speculative decoding method to alleviate the attention bottleneck in long-context LLM inference by drafting tokens with sparse attention.

title: QuanText: Protecting Dataset-Level Secrets in Textual Data Sharing
summary: QuanText is presented as a method to protect dataset-level secrets when sharing textual data, preventing the revelation of sensitive global properties from the underlying data source.

title: The Attention Within: Consensus Dynamics in Selective State Space Models
summary: This paper analyzes the internal workings of selective state space models, exploring their 'consensus dynamics' as a competitive and efficient alternative to transformers.

title: Structural Inference under Hidden Agents
summary: This research focuses on structural inference in multi-agent systems, aiming to recover latent interaction structures from dynamics even when some agents are hidden.

title: Regional Explanations via Causal Sufficiency and Necessity
summary: This paper introduces a new explainable AI method called 'Regional Explanations' based on causal sufficiency and necessity to characterize prediction behavior at a region level.

title: Beyond Embedding Transfer: Component Roles in Grokking Transfer and Stability
summary: This research studies the roles of different model components in 'grokking transfer' and stability during warm-start transfer for algorithmic tasks, distinguishing between efficacy and stability.

title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
summary: Agora is presented as a shared memory system, using Git, that enables collective autonomous research by allowing multiple coding agents to share information and avoid duplicated efforts.

title: iMINDBench: iEEG Multi-Institution Neural Decoding Benchmark
summary: iMINDBench is introduced as a new multi-institution benchmark for intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) neural decoding, aiming to facilitate progress in general-purpose foundation models.

title: FoundAna: A GNN-assisted Foundation Model for Graph Anomaly Detection
summary: FoundAna is introduced as a GNN-assisted foundation model specifically designed for graph anomaly detection, with applications in fraud detection and network intrusion.

title: Colla-Q: Toward Collaborative Experts in MoE Quantization via Minimax Precision Balancing
summary: Colla-Q presents a new Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) quantization method based on activation entropy and minimax precision balancing to reduce memory and computational costs while mitigating performance degradation.

title: Rethinking How We Evaluate Methodological Progress in Health AI
summary: This paper critically examines and proposes new ways to evaluate methodological progress in AI for electronic health records, addressing issues of reproducibility and clinical relevance.

title: Reaching Every Position Without Searching: Rotating Sparse Wiring on the Hypercube as a Substitute for Attention
summary: This research proposes a novel architectural component using rotating sparse wiring on a hypercube as a fixed and efficient substitute for the more computationally expensive attention mechanism.

title: LIGE-GR: A Smooth Leap from Ranking to Generative Recommendation in the LLM Era
summary: LIGE-GR introduces a new generative recommendation framework leveraging Large Language Models, aiming to transition from traditional ranking methods to more dynamic generative approaches in recommender systems.

title: MoRE: Mixture of Reused Experts
summary: This paper introduces MoRE (Mixture of Reused Experts), a new Mixture-of-Experts architecture that addresses high memory footprints by reusing layer weights, combining efficiency with competitive capacity.

title: A Lightweight CNN Integrated Compact Convolutional Transformer for Multi-Scale Feature Learning and reducing computational complexity for breast cancer mammography image detection and classification
summary: This research proposes a Lightweight CNN Integrated Compact Convolutional Transformer designed for multi-scale feature learning to reduce computational complexity in breast cancer mammography image detection and classification.

title: APGEM: Adaptive Policy-Guided Error Mitigation for Quantum Reinforcement Learning on a Real-World CVRP Case Study
summary: This paper introduces APGEM, a method for adaptive policy-guided error mitigation in Quantum Reinforcement Learning, applied to a real-world Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) case study.

title: Anomaly Detection in General Ledger Data: Results from a Hybrid Approach
summary: This research presents a hybrid approach for anomaly detection in general ledger data, aiming to improve Journal Entry Tests (JETs) by identifying high-risk audit areas and potential material misstatements more efficiently.

title: F-DACE: Fuzzy Disagreement-Aware Causal Evidence Fusion for Abstention-Safe Conversational Retail Decision Support
summary: This paper introduces F-DACE, a system for fuzzy disagreement-aware causal evidence fusion to provide abstention-safe conversational retail decision support, utilizing causal machine learning as its engine.

title: Behavioral Fingerprinting and Navigation Prediction in Web Browsing
summary: This study conducts a comparative empirical analysis of behavioral fingerprinting and navigation prediction in web browsing, demonstrating that even short browsing fragments contain rich behavioral signals for inference tasks.

title: A GAN-Based Framework for Robust DDoS Attack Detection
summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based framework for robust Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack detection, aiming to counter evolving attack strategies that bypass traditional network security systems.

title: Bias Amplification in Multi-Agent Network: How Biased Agents Shape Opinions and Rhetoric
summary: This research investigates bias amplification in multi-agent networks, studying how biased Large Language Model (LLM) agents can shape opinions and rhetoric in collective reasoning and decision-making processes.

title: Enhancing Extubation Failure Prediction with LLM-Derived Features from Respiratory Therapy Clinical Notes
summary: This research presents a novel approach to enhance extubation failure prediction by leveraging features derived from free-text respiratory therapy clinical notes using Large Language Models.

title: Faking Good and Faking Bad in LLMs: Response Distortion Across Dark Triad Personality Traits
summary: This study investigates response distortion in Large Language Models (LLMs) when assessing Dark Triad personality traits, exploring whether LLMs systematically modulate their expressions, similar to human social desirability and impression management.

title: DANTINOX: A Unified Framework for Multi-Paradigm Language Modeling
summary: This paper introduces DANTINOX, a unified framework designed to facilitate the comparison and integration of multi-paradigm language modeling approaches, including autoregressive decoding, discrete masked diffusion, and continuous flow-matching.

title: Think Before You Comfort: Reflective Cognitive Alignment for Protocol-Grounded Elderly Stimulation Agents
summary: This research proposes reflective cognitive alignment for protocol-grounded elderly stimulation agents, aiming to develop scalable AI solutions for Cognitive Stimulation Therapy, especially for low-resource languages like Cantonese.

title: Relation Before Entity: Deferred Commitment in Language Model Factual Recall
summary: This research investigates the factual recall mechanism in language models, examining whether relation-type information becomes causally active before entity-specific information during recall.

title: From Pixels to Pairs: A Comprehensive Benchmark of LLM-Based Key-Value Extraction in Noisy Document Settings
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark evaluating the performance of open-source instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) for key-value pair extraction from documents, particularly under realistic OCR noise conditions.

title: MudawanSn: A Gold-Standard Wolof-Arabic Parallel Corpus for Machine Translation
summary: This paper presents MudawanSn, a new gold-standard parallel corpus consisting of 1,271 manually translated sentence-aligned pairs from Wolof to Modern Standard Arabic, designed for machine translation research.

title: Register Bias in Complexity-Based Large Language Model Routing
summary: This research reveals register bias in complexity-based Large Language Model routing systems, demonstrating that the routing process is not register-neutral and affects how different language styles are handled.

title: Large Language Models Versus Physicians in Traditional Chinese Medicine: A Real-World Clinical Case Evaluation
summary: This study evaluates the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) against physicians in real-world Traditional Chinese Medicine clinical case diagnosis and treatment, using a constructed library of 349 de-identified outpatient cases.

title: Legal LLM Hallucination Should Be Evaluated as Failure of Legal Warrant
summary: This position paper argues that hallucinations in legal Large Language Models (LLMs) should be evaluated as a failure of legal warrant, defining a context-sensitive relation between legal claims and authority.

title: How AI Assistants Respond to Repeated Abuse
summary: This research investigates how AI assistants respond to repeated verbal abuse, examining changes in their engagement and contributing a bilingual, multi-turn framework to understand their disengagement mechanisms.

title: Myovox: Reading Speech from the Muscles of the Face
summary: Myovox is an AI system that decodes open-vocabulary English text from surface electromyography (sEMG) signals recorded from facial muscles during vocalized speech, significantly reducing the word error rate on a specific corpus.

title: Do Social Patterns Hold in Synthetic Data? Analyzing Cyberbullying Dynamics in LLM-Generated and Authentic Dialogues
summary: This research investigates whether social patterns, specifically cyberbullying dynamics, observed in authentic dialogues are preserved in synthetic conversations generated by large language models (LLMs). It analyzes the use of LLMs for data augmentation and benchmarking in this context.

title: No Usable Linear "Capitulation Direction" in Two Small LLMs: A Validation Protocol for Activation-Steering Claims, and a Cross-Family Behavioral Study of Sycophancy Under Pushback
summary: This research investigates the phenomenon of "sycophancy" in small instruction-tuned language models, where they abandon correct answers under user pushback, studying Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B models on TriviaQA. It also proposes a validation protocol for activation-steering claims.

title: Does Moral Reasoning Training Help or Hurt? Red-Teaming RL-Trained Ethical Agents with Persona Attacks
summary: This paper red-teams ethical language-model agents trained with moral-reward reinforcement learning to assess if their alignment and cooperation persist under adversarial persona attacks, which introduce competing role instructions.

title: The Limits of BPE Tokenization in Polish: Segmentation-Flexional Forms, Grammatical Anchoring, and First-Person Stability in Inflectional Language Models
summary: This article analyzes the limitations of BPE tokenization in Polish, an inflectional language, to determine if frequency-based segmentation preserves linguistically relevant units for language models.

title: English Word Sense Disambiguation in 2026: When the Labels Become the Bottleneck
summary: This article argues that in English all-words word sense disambiguation, the quality of labels in the gold standard, rather than the models themselves, has become the primary bottleneck for accurate evaluation and benchmark rankings of frontier large language models.

title: Confidence Comes from Experience: Experiential Confidence Estimation from Reasoning to Agents
summary: This research introduces "experiential confidence estimation" for language models and agents, aiming to provide more reliable and calibrated estimates of output correctness, which is crucial for trustworthy AI deployment.

title: PrimeScientist: Strategic Allocation of Research Effort in Autonomous Research
summary: PrimeScientist proposes a method for strategic allocation of research effort in autonomous research agents, addressing the challenge of prioritizing numerous potential research directions given limited resources.

title: SFT or RL for Tool-Calling Agents? A Controlled Study Across Data, Method, and Scale
summary: This controlled study evaluates the impact of training data, adaptation methods (SFT with LoRA, RL via GRPO), and model scale on the tool-calling performance of language-model agents.

title: AfriSyCo: Measuring Assertive Framing, Verification, and Wording Sensitivity Around African-Language Content
summary: AfriSyCo is a study that measures assertive framing, verification, and wording sensitivity in language models when processing African-language factual content, analyzing answer switching behavior in cross-language contexts.

title: Who Judges Matters: Measuring Family-Conditioned Preference in LLM-as-Judge Panels
summary: This research investigates the impact of different open-weight large language model families when used as judges in evaluation panels, measuring family-conditioned preferences across Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 2, and Yi 1.5.

title: TACTICS: Taxonomy-Aware Intelligent Corpus Sampling for Machine Translation
summary: TACTICS is a method for taxonomy-aware intelligent corpus sampling designed to improve the evaluation of large-scale machine translation systems by ensuring test samples cover the full range of phenomena a system must handle.

title: A Calibrated Instrument for Measuring How Inference Optimizations Affect Output Quality
summary: This paper introduces a calibrated instrument designed to precisely measure how various inference optimizations, such as quantization and early-exit methods, affect the output quality of large language models.

title: Exact semantic readout from compressed vector representations
summary: This research characterizes the conditions under which compressed vector representations allow for exact linear or affine semantic readouts of a finite lexicon's truth conditions, identifying a necessary and sufficient row-space condition.

title: From a River in Gilead to the Inference Distributions of Large Language Models: Covert Dialect Bias and Linguistic Profiling at Scale
summary: This research reveals covert dialect bias and linguistic profiling in the inference distributions of large language models, demonstrating how attitudinal associations persist despite alignment techniques and can affect high-stakes applications like housing screening.

title: Linguistic Triggers of Gender and Racial Bias in Open-Weight LLMs Applied to Recruitment
summary: This paper identifies linguistic triggers of gender and racial bias in open-weight large language models when used in recruitment, highlighting their discriminatory failure modes and the resulting regulatory exposure under acts like the EU AI Act.

title: DualSQL: Text-to-SQL with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: DualSQL is a Text-to-SQL system that employs multi-agent reinforcement learning within a multi-agent pipeline to improve performance by leveraging the synergy between schema linking and SQL generation tasks.

title: TeochewBench: A Human-Reviewed Benchmark for Teochew Hanzi Translation
summary: TeochewBench is a new human-reviewed benchmark consisting of 300 Teochew Hanzi expressions designed to evaluate large language models on Teochew Hanzi translation, addressing the lack of evaluation resources for this language.

title: T-SANDHI: Tone Sandhi-aware Adaptive Network with Decoupled Hybrid Injection for Low-resource Taiwanese Hokkien Speech Recognition
summary: T-SANDHI is a tone sandhi-aware adaptive network with decoupled hybrid injection designed for low-resource Taiwanese Hokkien Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), addressing a major challenge in processing implicit phonological variations.

title: Behavior2Value: Benchmarking and Empowering LLMs for Consumer Value Measurement from E-commerce Behaviors
summary: This research introduces a method for benchmarking and empowering LLMs to measure consumer values from e-commerce behaviors, identifying stable drivers behind purchase decisions. It focuses on evaluating LLM capabilities in this specific domain.

title: Beyond Accuracy: How Procedural Traces Shift the Decision Criterion of LLM Overseers
summary: This study investigates how procedural traces influence the decision-making of LLM overseers in LLM-as-a-judge pipelines, using signal detection theory to analyze their gullibility. It provides insights into the evaluation of AI auditing systems.

title: I code or AI code: A comparative evaluation of AI-rated scores in classroom observations
summary: This study evaluates the feasibility of using an LLM (specifically GPT-5) to score teacher performance in classroom observations, comparing its ratings with those of trained human observers. It aims to assess AI's role in educational quality benchmarks.

title: Too Good to Be Real? Diagnosing and Reducing the Gap Between AI Preference and Real User Engagement
summary: This research investigates the discrepancy between content qualities favored by large language models and those that lead to high real user engagement on platforms like Zhihu, Quora, and Reddit. It aims to diagnose and reduce this gap for AI-generated content.

title: Made in Hungary: Comments on the performance of generative language models
summary: This paper comments on three initiatives in Hungary to develop generative language models for the Hungarian language, motivated by the limited proficiency of existing English-centric models. It provides a detailed examination of their performance.

title: Rollback the World, Keep the Reflection: Rollback-Induced Reflection for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This research proposes a 'rollback-induced reflection' mechanism to enhance the robustness of long-horizon LLM agents, allowing them to correct errors and repair altered contexts in multi-step tasks. It addresses compounding errors in agentic systems.

title: SEA-LION-v4.8: A Technical Report
summary: This technical report introduces Nemotron-SEA-LION-v4.8, a family of large language models for Southeast Asian languages built upon NVIDIA Nemotron 3. It includes 30B and 120B parameter models with base checkpoints and post-trained variants.

title: Knowledge-Graph Based Augmentation versus Retrieval Augmented Generation for Cultural-Related Question Answering
summary: This research compares knowledge-graph based augmentation with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to address large language models' 'long-tail deficit' in recalling culturally specific facts. It aims to improve LLM accuracy in cultural-related question answering.

title: Attention Dispersion as a Diagnostic Signal for Hallucination in Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces 'attention dispersion' as a diagnostic signal to detect hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs), aiming to improve their reliability in complex reasoning tasks. It offers a new technical method for addressing a significant LLM challenge.

title: Emotion Experience, Expression, and Perception: Emotion Analysis on Multimodal Social Media Posts
summary: This research investigates emotion analysis on multimodal social media posts, focusing on how emotions are experienced, expressed, and perceived through combined text and image content. It aims to improve understanding of human communication in digital environments.

title: Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper proposes a 'dependency-aware trajectory refinement' method to optimize multi-turn agent fine-tuning by identifying and removing redundant steps in agent trajectories. It aims to reduce training and inference costs for agentic systems.

title: Planning or Improvisation? Stress-Testing the Poetry Planning Site on Open Models and Open Cross-Layer Transcoders
summary: This study stress-tests how generative models, including Claude 3.5 Haiku, perform poetry planning by analyzing rhyme generation, and examines if these planning capabilities generalize across various open models. It investigates the internal mechanisms of creative AI.

title: M-SQE: Multilingual Skill Quality Estimation for Enhancing Language Equality in Agentic Skill Use
summary: This research introduces M-SQE (Multilingual Skill Quality Estimation) to improve language equality and utility in agentic skill use for LLM agents. It aims to support community-maintained skill libraries across various languages.

title: Size Matters: Foundation Model for Czech HTML documents
summary: This article discusses the development of a foundation model specifically designed for Czech HTML documents, aiming to create universal, high-quality, and economically performant representations of web content within the Czech context.

title: Align, Integrate, and Fire: Efficient Token-Level Alignment for Zero-Shot SpeechLLMs
summary: This paper proposes an efficient token-level alignment method for building zero-shot SpeechLLMs, addressing the challenge of extending large language model capabilities to spoken input. It avoids computationally expensive full-model fine-tuning.

title: Machine Translation between English and Syriac (East Syriac Dialect) using Statistical Machine Learning
summary: This research explores machine translation between English and the endangered East Syriac dialect using statistical machine learning methods. It addresses the lack of NLP studies for this underrepresented language.

title: A Probe Shift Is Not a Fairness Fix: The Limits of Representation Steering in Speech Models
summary: This research investigates fairness in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, specifically analyzing the limitations of representation steering as a method to mitigate unequal error rates across different speaker groups. It discusses the effectiveness of bias-reduction techniques.

title: PACT: Can Enterprise AI Assistants Be Trusted Under Pressure?
summary: This paper introduces PACT, an evaluation framework designed to assess the trustworthiness and compliance of enterprise-grade LLM agents in sensitive applications like hiring and healthcare. It addresses the critical need for agents to adhere to specified rules under pressure.

title: STRETCH the Boundaries: A Unified Self-Taught Framework for Progressive LLM Evolution
summary: This paper proposes STRETCH (Self-Taught Reasoning Evolution via Targeted CHallenge), a unified framework enabling progressive self-improvement and evolution for large language models. It addresses the issue of capability stagnation in self-improvement training.

title: Fallacy Benchmarks Measure Scheme Recognition, Not Fallacy Detection
summary: This paper critiques existing fallacy-detection benchmarks, arguing that their current construction primarily measures scheme recognition rather than genuine fallacy detection. It highlights a misleading aspect of current evaluation methods for reasoning abilities.

title: DyMT-ESB: Dynamic Multi-Turn Evaluation of Social Bias in User-LLM Interactions
summary: This paper introduces DyMT-ESB, a method for dynamically evaluating social bias and stereotyping-related harms in multi-turn conversational interactions with LLMs. It aims to assess model behavior for safety in interactive settings.

title: Selection Is Retrieval, Abstention Is Not: On-Device Tool Routing over 70 Korean-English Actions
summary: This research explores a method for on-device AI assistants to route actions to specific tools, deciding both which tool to invoke and whether to abstain from using a tool. The focus is on efficient tool selection and abstention for language models on devices.

title: Voice of Reason: Reinforcement Learning for Spoken Math
summary: This paper investigates using reinforcement learning to enhance the mathematical reasoning capabilities of speech language models, aiming to improve their accuracy on relevant benchmarks. It focuses on bridging the performance gap between text and speech models in this domain.

title: Selective Prediction and Uncertainty-Aware Referral for Pap Smear Classification
summary: This research proposes a method for deep learning models in cervical cytology to perform selective prediction, allowing them to refer cases they are least certain about to human cytopathologists. It focuses on integrating uncertainty-aware referral into screening systems.

title: DualCount: Structurally Consistent Density and Point Modeling for Zero-Shot Object Counting
summary: This paper introduces DualCount, a novel method for zero-shot object counting that combines density and point modeling to achieve structural consistency and mitigate spatial ambiguity. It aims to improve object estimation without category-specific training.

title: Not All Patches Are Equally Forgettable: Spatially Localized Domain Unlearning in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research explores spatially localized domain unlearning in vision-language models, aiming to remove undesirable domain-specific behaviors while preserving general recognition capabilities. It addresses how to disentangle domain-related and semantic information.

title: AgenTeeth: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Suppressing Hallucination in Frozen Vision-Language Models on Dental X-Rays via Tool Evidence Injection
summary: AgenTeeth is a model-agnostic framework designed to suppress hallucination in frozen vision-language models when interpreting dental X-rays by injecting tool-derived evidence. This approach aims to improve reliability in dental diagnostics.

title: GazeDiT: Gaze-Accurate Diffusion Image Generation for Eye Tracking via Spatial Conditioning
summary: GazeDiT introduces a method for generating gaze-accurate diffusion images using spatial conditioning, specifically designed for creating synthetic training data for eye tracking. It focuses on precise label control in generative models.

title: CALIPER: Metric-Grounded Model-Free Recognition of Visually Similar Industrial Parts
summary: This research introduces CALIPER, a metric-grounded and model-free method for recognizing visually similar industrial parts, focusing on distinguishing them by physical dimensions. It addresses challenges when CAD models or large datasets are unavailable.

title: RoboVAD: A Large Cross-Domain Evaluation Benchmark for Anomaly Detection in Robotic Arm Manipulation Videos
summary: This paper introduces RoboVAD, a large cross-domain evaluation benchmark designed for anomaly detection in robotic arm manipulation videos. It provides a standardized way to measure performance in this specific robotic application.

title: Investigating Adversarial Robustness of Heterogeneous Cooperative Perception
summary: This research investigates the adversarial robustness of heterogeneous cooperative perception systems used in connected vehicles, where diverse sensor setups share spatial awareness. It examines potential attacks against these systems.

title: Lumen: Parameter-Efficient Alignment of Pretrained Vision and Language Encoders for Zero-Shot Computational Pathology
summary: This research introduces Lumen, a method for parameter-efficiently aligning pretrained vision and language encoders to create zero-shot computational pathology models. It focuses on assembling pathology vision-language models from frozen unimodal foundation models.

title: Can VLMs Reliably Assess Sidewalk Accessibility Attributes from Pedestrian-Level Imagery?
summary: This research investigates the reliability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in assessing sidewalk accessibility attributes, such as width and slope, from pedestrian-level imagery. It aims to determine if VLMs can effectively evaluate urban infrastructure for accessibility.

title: Zing-0.5: Toward Playable Worlds with Real-Time Joint Action and Text Control
summary: This paper introduces Zing-0.5, a 5B autoregressive world model capable of generating playable worlds that users can control in real-time through joint keyboard and text commands. It features a unified control architecture for dynamic interaction.

title: Face-voice Association across LAnguages and Gender (FLAG) 2027 Challenge Evaluation Plan
summary: This outlines the FLAG 2027 Challenge Evaluation Plan, designed to investigate how face-voice association models perform across different languages and genders. It aims to identify issues like reliance on language/gender cues rather than speaker-specific characteristics.

title: Audio for Sports Highlight Detection: A Comparative Empirical Study
summary: This paper presents a comparative empirical study on the use of audio cues, such as commentator speech and crowd reactions, for detecting highlights in long sports videos. It investigates their effectiveness compared to visual-based methods.

title: Rapid Loss of the Sierra Nevada's Largest Trees Driven by Fire
summary: This research reveals the rapid loss of the largest trees in the Sierra Nevada, primarily driven by fire, using a deep learning model (U-Net-ID) and aerial imagery. It quantifies changes in biomass storage and habitat structure.

title: EDCT-Bench: Uncovering Faithfulness Gaps in VLMs via Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing
summary: This paper introduces EDCT-Bench, an intervention-based protocol that uses Explanation-Driven Counterfactual Testing to uncover faithfulness gaps in Natural Language Explanations generated by Vision-Language Models. It aims to identify inconsistencies between explanations and visual evidence.

title: Newer Is Not Fairer: Gender Stereotyping in Text-to-Image AI Across Model Generations
summary: This study evaluates gender stereotyping and representation in text-to-image generative models across multiple model generations and 20 occupations. It assesses whether newer models demonstrate fairer gender representations.

title: CoAtNet-DeepMoE: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid with DeepSeek Mixture-of-Experts for Parameter-Efficient Tomato Disease Classification
summary: This paper introduces CoAtNet-DeepMoE, a parameter-efficient convolution-attention hybrid model incorporating DeepSeek Mixture-of-Experts for classifying tomato diseases. It aims to improve food security by reducing crop losses.

title: Position Anchor Tuning: Towards Efficient Adaptation of Pre-Trained Point Cloud Transformers
summary: This paper introduces Position Anchor Tuning (PAT), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method to adapt pre-trained point cloud transformers for various downstream tasks, focusing on improving inference efficiency.

title: Finder: Agentic Closed-Loop Object Finding for Embodied Grounding
summary: This paper introduces Finder, an agentic closed-loop system designed for embodied agents to efficiently locate objects referred to by language within partially observed 3D scenes. It aims to improve object search without costly online exploration.

title: GeoCueFormer: Geometry-Guided Wavelet Representation and Prediction-Cued Dual-Stage Decoder for Underwater Semantic Segmentation
summary: This paper introduces GeoCueFormer, a novel method for underwater semantic segmentation that uses geometry-guided wavelet representation and a prediction-cued dual-stage decoder to address challenges from severe visual degradation in marine environments.

title: vidax: A Unified JAX Framework for Video Generative Models on Accelerator Meshes
summary: vidax is presented as a unified JAX framework designed for video generative models, enabling their efficient deployment and inference on Cloud TPU pods with accelerator meshes. This addresses the current reliance on PyTorch/CUDA implementations.

title: Mask 2D-3D: Adaptive Dual-Masked Autoencoder Network for Image-to-Point Cloud Registration
summary: This paper introduces Mask 2D-3D, an Adaptive Dual-Masked Autoencoder Network designed to improve image-to-point cloud registration by addressing issues like erroneous correspondences and domain discrepancies.

title: Aligned Consensus Teaching for Label-Efficient Oriented Object Detection in Weakly-Aligned Visible-Infrared Imagery
summary: This paper proposes Aligned Consensus Teaching, a semi-supervised learning method for label-efficient oriented object detection in weakly-aligned visible-infrared imagery, aiming to reduce the cost of dual-modality annotations.

title: PRISM: Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion for Social Robot Navigation
summary: This paper introduces PRISM, a Predictive Representation of Interaction Style and Motion, designed to enhance social robot navigation by allowing robots to better understand and predict human interaction tendencies in crowds.

title: MCLC-NET: Multimodal Continual Learning for Leaf Counting
summary: This paper proposes MCLC-NET, a multimodal continual learning network for leaf counting in plant phenotyping, which integrates RGB and depth information to overcome challenges like occlusion and lighting variations.

title: Stealthy in Semantics, Antagonistic in Space: Attacking Visible-Infrared Object Detectors via Object-Level Misalignment
summary: This research investigates a novel method for stealthily attacking visible-infrared object detectors by creating object-level misalignments, aiming to develop more subtle and effective physical adversarial attacks.

title: Multi-View Mixture-of-Experts with Vision-Language Reranking for Cross-View Object Geo-Localization
summary: This paper proposes a Multi-View Mixture-of-Experts with Vision-Language Reranking approach for Cross-View Object Geo-Localization, aiming to efficiently locate targets in satellite imagery using drone or street-view queries.

title: CapMap-MS-TTA: 3rd Place Solution for the MUMU Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge at ECCV 2026
summary: This entry describes CapMap-MS-TTA, the 3rd place solution for the MUMU track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge, which is a unified multimodal model for image tagging, open-vocabulary object detection, and English captioning.

title: Understanding Dynamic Scenes at Gigapixel Scale: Wide-Area Spatio-Temporal Perception from UAVs
summary: This research addresses the challenge of Wide-area Spatio-temporal Scene Understanding (WSTU) at gigapixel scale, leveraging UAV-borne imaging to shift aerial perception from target recognition to comprehensive scene analysis.

title: WISE: A Lightweight, Weakly-Supervised Model for Onboard Fire Smoke Detection and Localization
summary: This paper introduces WISE, a lightweight and weakly-supervised AI model designed for onboard fire smoke detection and localization from satellite imagery, optimized for deployment under strict memory and latency constraints.

title: Unified Response Geometry for Structured Pruning
summary: This paper proposes a Unified Response Geometry approach for structured pruning, reformulating pruning as selecting a subset of channels with large joint response capacity to improve model efficiency.

title: MS-RFD: Multi-Signal Release Frame Detection in Hammer Throw from Reconstructed 3D Trajectories
summary: This paper introduces MS-RFD, a multi-signal method for release frame detection in hammer throw using reconstructed 3D trajectories, applying AI and computer vision to sports performance analysis.

title: Decoder-Agnostic Token Merging for Vision Transformers: A Systematic Study of G2TM
summary: This paper presents a systematic study of G2TM (Decoder-Agnostic Token Merging) for Vision Transformers, aiming to reduce the computational complexity of the self-attention mechanism and improve ViT efficiency.

title: Visual Autoregressive Priors for RAW-to-sRGB Image Signal Processing
summary: This paper introduces the first application of Visual Autoregressive Priors (VAR) for RAW-to-sRGB Image Signal Processing, aiming to recover perceptually faithful colors and fine details from sensor measurements.

title: Can MiniMax-H3 Reason About the Physical World? An Evaluation of Omni-Modal Generative Model
summary: This paper evaluates MiniMax-H3, an Omni-Modal Generative Model that combines multimodal context understanding with audio-visual generation, to assess its capability for reasoning about the physical world.

title: PDA++: Field-Aligned Planning and Scene-Adaptive Insertion in Remote Sensing
summary: This paper introduces PDA++, a method combining field-aligned planning and scene-adaptive insertion for realistic synthetic data augmentation in remote sensing, beneficial for few-shot and long-tailed recognition scenarios.

title: Pose2Muscle: Structured Spatio-Temporal Decoding for Discrete Muscle Activity Estimation from Human Pose
summary: This paper introduces Pose2Muscle, a method using structured spatio-temporal decoding to estimate discrete muscle activity directly from human pose, offering a practical alternative to sensor-based monitoring for rehabilitation and injury prevention.

title: Visual Input and Its Framing Affect Attribute-based Descriptions Produced by Large Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper demonstrates how visual input and its framing affect attribute-based descriptions generated by Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), even when the text prompt is not specific to the image instance.

title: Online Multi-Camera 3D Tracking via ID Prediction over Recurrent Sparse Queries
summary: This paper presents an online architecture for multi-camera 3D tracking that improves association accuracy by explicitly carrying global identities, addressing fragmentation issues in query-based trackers.

title: MSR: Multiple Subject Reference for Video Generation
summary: MSR (Multiple Subject Reference) is a slot-aware conditioning scheme for LTX-based video generation that preserves appearance while associating multiple reference images with their intended roles.

title: Vocabulary-Guided Gait Recognition
summary: This work introduces Vocabulary-Guided Gait Recognition, an approach that enhances the comprehension of gait by defining it as human shape, motion, and inherent structure derived from images and points.

title: StrucPhysVideo: Learning Physical Dynamics from Structured Captions and Robot Actions
summary: StrucPhysVideo is a family of video world models for embodied AI that learns physical dynamics and predicts scene evolution by bridging physics-focused data curation with language- and action-conditioned prediction.

title: Occluded Gait Recognition with Mixture of Experts: An Action Detection Perspective
summary: This paper addresses challenges in occluded gait recognition by proposing a mixture of experts approach from an action detection perspective, leveraging dynamic contextual information within gait sequences.

title: DR.WILSS: Diffusion-Based Replay for Weakly Supervised Continual Semantic Segmentation
summary: DR.WILSS introduces a diffusion-based replay approach to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in weakly supervised class-incremental semantic segmentation, enabling models to learn new concepts over multiple steps with image-level supervision.

title: CSWAM: Better Causal Semantic Representations for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in World Action Models
summary: CSWAM proposes better causal semantic representations to improve out-of-distribution generalization for FastWAM-style world action models, addressing their poor performance under visual distribution shifts.

title: GeoCond: A Conditioning-Aware Reliability Adapter for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
summary: GeoCond is a conditioning-aware reliability adapter designed to improve the robustness of feed-forward 3D foundation models like VGGT, preventing silent failures under challenging geometric conditions.

title: Beyond Random Couplings: Contrastive Noise Alignment in Generative Flows
summary: This paper proposes contrastive noise alignment in generative flows, a method that improves the training of diffusion and flow-matching models by creating more meaningful data-noise couplings.

title: Human-Centric Grasp State Assessment: Toward Transferring Subjective Evaluation to Robots
summary: This framework aims to transfer human subjective criteria for assessing grasp states of deformable objects to robotic systems, bridging the semantic gap between human expectations and quantitative robotic measurements.

title: Predictive Varanus: Combining CSP Conformance Monitoring with Predictive LTL Runtime Verification
summary: Predictive Varanus combines CSP Conformance Monitoring with Predictive LTL Runtime Verification to provide proactive safety checks for autonomous and robotic systems, detecting violations before they occur.

title: Vision-Language Grounded Task-Context-Aware Imitation Learning for Robotic Disassembly
summary: This research proposes a vision-language grounded, task-context-aware imitation learning approach to enable robots to perform long-horizon disassembly tasks involving multiple parts and diverse configurations.

title: RAF-VLA: Representation Alignment with the Future for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: RAF-VLA enhances Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for end-to-end autonomous driving by aligning representations with future driving scenes, thereby improving planning performance through dense supervision.

title: CALOS: Control-Affine Lyapunov On-manifold Safety Layer for Safe Deep Reinforcement Learning for Quadrotors
summary: CALOS (Control-Affine Lyapunov On-manifold Safety) is a runtime safety layer that enforces attitude and rate constraints for Deep Reinforcement Learning-controlled quadrotors, guaranteeing safety during training and deployment.

title: DRT&R: Direct Radar Teach & Repeat
summary: DRT&R introduces a direct radar teach and repeat method for navigation, offering robustness to adverse conditions where lidar-based systems may fail.

title: HINT-Plan: Human Intention-Aware Robot Task Planning in Context-Rich Environments using Vision Language Models
summary: HINT-Plan is a novel approach to human intention-aware robot task planning in context-rich environments, utilizing Vision Language Models to integrate human presence and high-level behavior into mobile robot decision-making.

title: SPROUT: The Open-Source Soft Growing Robot for Search and Rescue
summary: SPROUT is an open-source soft growing robot designed for search and rescue operations, addressing barriers to deploying such systems from laboratories to the field.

title: Learning Multi-Humanoid Pickup and Transport via Decentralized Object-Centric Control
summary: This research investigates cooperative multi-humanoid pickup and transport of objects using decentralized object-centric control, where each humanoid learns to interact with a shared object.

title: Timely Activation of Safety Filters via One-Step Reachability Expansion
summary: This paper introduces safety filters based on Hamilton-Jacobi reachability to provide strong safety guarantees by overriding a nominal controller only when the system reaches the boundary of unsafe states. The method uses a Backward Reachable Tube (BRT) to define these states.

title: Multi-Session Multimodal Underwater Mapping with Acoustic and Optical Imaging
summary: This research presents a method for accurate seafloor mapping by integrating data from acoustic and optical imaging sensors across multiple survey sessions. It addresses challenges related to positioning drift and sensor offsets in multimodal data fusion.

title: Feedback-Modulated Harmonic Policies for Quadruped Locomotion
summary: This paper investigates feedback-modulated harmonic policies for quadruped locomotion, where joint trajectories are expressed as command-conditioned Fourier series. This approach aims to provide a more explicit periodic structure for locomotion control compared to direct observation-to-action mapping.

title: Online Multimodal Workload Assessment in Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction
summary: This paper presents an online multimodal assessment framework to continuously evaluate workload during contact-rich physical human-robot interaction (pHRI). The framework integrates various demands associated with physical interaction, motor regulation, and physiological response.

title: Geometric Shortcuts for Complex Trunk Postures: Dual-Helicity Coupling Enables Low-Dimensional Control
summary: This research proposes that complex elephant trunk postures arise from a low-dimensional geometric shortcut, specifically dual-helicity coupling between oblique muscles. The findings are demonstrated using a simplified soft-robotic prototype for low-dimensional control.

title: CLASP: A Cluster-Level Autonomous Selective Picking Robot with a Soft Rolling-Band Gripper for Fresh-Market Blueberry Harvesting
summary: This paper introduces CLASP, a cluster-level autonomous selective picking robot equipped with a soft rolling-band gripper, designed for harvesting fresh-market blueberries. The robot aims to address the labor-intensive and expensive nature of traditional selective picking.

title: Not All Layers Need Tuning: Diagnosing and Directing Adaptation in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This paper diagnoses and directs adaptation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, challenging the assumption that all network regions require equal adjustment during fine-tuning for new deployment environments. It investigates whether more efficient, non-uniform tuning strategies are possible.

title: ReRadar: Robust Radar Global Localization via Rotation-Equivariant Descriptor Learning
summary: ReRadar is a pipeline for robust radar global localization that extracts rotation-equivariant intermediate features to improve accurate pose retrieval. This method addresses challenges where traditional place-recognition descriptors often discard spatial structure.

title: Beyond Pixel Similarity: Task-Aware Evaluation of GAN-Based Synthetic Sonar Data for Robotic Perception
summary: This research investigates the task-aware evaluation of GAN-based synthetic sonar data to determine its effectiveness for robotic perception. The study aims to understand if synthetic data can reduce the cost of collecting and annotating training data for downstream perception tasks.

title: Technical Report: One-Step Drifting Action Heads for GR00T N1.7
summary: This technical report studies a GR00T N1.7 variant that uses one-step drifting action heads to significantly reduce the inference cost of its Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. The report evaluates its effect on closed-loop task success compared to iterative diffusion-transformer action heads.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Generative Physical Artificial Intelligence
summary: This comprehensive review surveys Generative Physical Artificial Intelligence (GPAI), a field integrating large-scale foundation models with physical embodiments to create agentic AI systems in robotics. These systems autonomously perceive, reason, and act in complex real-world situations.

title: OpenDexGrasp: Open-vocabulary Task-Oriented Dexterous Grasping
summary: OpenDexGrasp studies open-vocabulary task-oriented dexterous grasp generation, where a robot must infer functional grasps to preserve task-implied functions during real-world manipulation. This advances dexterous grasp synthesis beyond generating only stable hand poses.

title: Fetch My Beer: Synthetic-to-real Hierarchical Policy for Smooth Pick-and-place
summary: This research investigates a synthetic-to-real hierarchical policy for robotic pick-and-place tasks that require dynamically sensitive manipulation, such as handling liquid-filled containers. The goal is to maintain stable object dynamics throughout execution.

title: Prior Evolution and Task Alignment for Aerial Grasping
summary: This research is inspired by predatory birds to develop methods for aerial grasping, focusing on prior evolution and task alignment for highly coordinated maneuvers in flight. It uses trajectory optimization to reproduce such capabilities for robotic systems.

title: Energy-Regularized Imitation Learning for Force- and Work-Aware Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper studies energy-aware manipulation as a physically grounded learning problem, using energy-regularized imitation learning. It defines a joint-space mechanical-work proxy and trains a differentiable energy predictor from robot states and actions.

title: Characterizing Replay Retention Under Dynamics Shift in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research characterizes replay retention under dynamics shifts in continual model-based reinforcement learning (RL) for robotic systems. It investigates how old replay data impacts adaptation to new robot dynamics.

title: Approximating High Dimensional Self-Motion Manifolds via Deep Generative Models
summary: This paper proposes using deep generative models to approximate high-dimensional self-motion manifolds (SMMs) for redundant manipulators. Efficient recovery of SMMs underpins feasible and global optimal motion planning.

title: OmniRisk: Omnidirectional Trajectory-Risk Learning for Agile Quadrotor Dynamic Avoidance
summary: OmniRisk introduces an omnidirectional trajectory-risk learning method for agile quadrotor dynamic avoidance, enabling anticipation of collisions with fast-moving obstacles. This addresses the challenge of selecting feasible maneuvers with short reaction windows despite sparse range observations.

title: WholeBodyWAM: Learning Whole-Body World Action Models with Scalable Motion Priors
summary: This paper presents WholeBodyWAM, a method for learning whole-body world action models for humanoid manipulation by leveraging scalable motion priors. The approach aims to address the expense and difficulty of collecting large-scale trajectories from target robots by using abundant human and humanoid motion data.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: This research explores using reinforcement learning to fine-tune large, pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to achieve real-time policies for reliable robot deployment. The approach aims to mitigate high inference latency issues in modern VLA models.

title: CANTABILE: Learning Expressive Dynamics for Robotic Piano Performance
summary: This paper describes CANTABILE, a method for training robots to play the piano with expressive musical dynamics, moving beyond simple note accuracy for dexterous bimanual manipulation.

title: UMI-Bridge: Action-Anchored Latent Alignment across Human and Robot Manipulation Data
summary: UMI-Bridge proposes a method for aligning human and robot manipulation data, including egocentric videos and Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) demonstrations, to overcome limitations of real-robot data.

title: ForceDelta-VLA: Distilling Force-Conditioned ActionCorrections for Contact-Rich Manipulation
summary: ForceDelta-VLA introduces a method to distill force-conditioned action corrections for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, improving contact-rich robotic manipulation by separating reference actions from contact-dependent adjustments.

title: Acting in Meters: Learning Metric Interactions for Precise Robotic Manipulation
summary: This research explores learning metric interactions for precise robotic manipulation, combining semantic understanding with spatial feedback to improve Vision-Language-Action and World-Action models.

title: A3P5 NEMESIS Integrated Rover Design for Environmental Reconnaissance and Robotic Sampling with Reproducible Mobility Analysis and an External Data Machine Learning Calibration Benchmark
summary: A3P5 NEMESIS describes the design and assessment of a four-wheel rover for environmental reconnaissance and robotic sampling, integrating remote inspection and lightweight manipulation capabilities.

title: ${M}^2$Tok: Multi-head Multi-codebook Discrete Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: ${M}^2$Tok introduces a multi-head, multi-codebook discrete action tokenization method for Vision-Language-Action models, enabling effective mapping of high-dimensional continuous action signals into compact discrete tokens.

title: Function-Preserving Data Generation for Zero-Shot Real-to-Sim-to-Real Manipulation
summary: This research proposes a function-preserving data generation paradigm to scale robot learning for zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real manipulation, particularly for challenging contact-rich tasks.

title: RAFAIL: Relationship-Aware Failure Detection for Robotic Manipulation
summary: RAFAIL introduces a relationship-aware failure detection method for robotic manipulation, aiming to improve reliability by distinguishing task-relevant deviations from harmless scene variations using VLMs and OOD detectors.

title: UAVs Meet Embodied Intelligence: Bridging Human Intents and Flying Dynamics Via Harnessing Physical-Digital AI Agents
summary: This paper explores how physical-digital AI agents can bridge human intent and flying dynamics for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), extending embodied intelligence into continuous three-dimensional space.

title: RecMorph: Topology-Guided Spatial Recurrence for Generalized Morphology Control
summary: RecMorph introduces a topology-guided spatial recurrence mechanism for generalized morphology control, enabling a single policy to coordinate whole-body motion and transform information across limbs.

title: Decoupling Vision, Language, and Action for Efficient Multi-Task Robot Policies
summary: This research proposes decoupling vision, language, and action components in VLA models to create more efficient multi-task robot policies, particularly for low-level manipulation, by reducing VLM computational cost.

title: DistAL: Distance-based Advantage Learning for VLA Fine-Tuning
summary: DistAL presents Distance-based Advantage Learning for fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, a technique that iteratively improves VLAs for robotic manipulation by training a value function.

title: DetAug: Obstacle-Blind Trajectory Augmentation for Zero-shot Obstacle Avoidance
summary: DetAug introduces obstacle-blind trajectory augmentation to improve policies for robotic manipulation, enabling zero-shot obstacle avoidance in environments different from the initial teleoperated datasets.

title: Hardware-Free Robotics Laboratories in Mixed Reality
summary: This paper presents MR-Robotics LAB, a mixed-reality platform designed to provide hardware-free robotics laboratories, allowing learners to experience robot motion at real scale.

title: VLM-MPPI: Grounding Natural Language in Behaviorally Diverse Trajectories for Aerial Navigation
summary: VLM-MPPI proposes a hierarchical UAV navigation framework that grounds natural language intent in behaviorally diverse trajectories, enabling dynamically feasible flight in cluttered indoor environments.

title: ActionPiece: Rethinking Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: ActionPiece proposes a new approach to action tokenization for autoregressive Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, re-evaluating how policy training targets and executable commands are derived from predicted tokens.

title: The era of AI warfare has arrived
summary: This article discusses the arrival of AI warfare, noting the rapid integration of autonomous systems on the battlefield and the unpredictable advancements of AI models.

title: DeepMind offshoot nears $4bn valuation just a month after founding
summary: A British startup, founded by former DeepMind researchers, is reportedly nearing a $4 billion valuation and close to raising $700 million for its new venture, Emulate.

title: Japan has good reason to welcome arrival of driverless taxis - Financial Times
summary: This Financial Times article suggests that Japan has compelling reasons to embrace the introduction and expansion of driverless taxi services.

title: Gore downplays AI threats and touts its climate potential
summary: Former US vice-president Al Gore reportedly downplays general AI threats while advocating for its significant potential to contribute to climate solutions and green progress.

title: 4 in 10 Companies Boost Security Spending on AI Adoption, Wary of Shadow AI - finance.biggo.com
summary: A report indicates that 4 out of 10 companies are increasing their security spending due to AI adoption, driven by concerns over 'Shadow AI'.

title: Vývojáři díky AI píšou dvakrát víc kódu. Proč z toho firma nemá dvojnásobný zisk?
summary: Data analyzed by a Czech company shows that developers write twice as much code using AI, raising questions about why this increased productivity doesn't translate into double profits for companies.

title: Dubai Business Forum · China Unveils Elite Chinese Corporate Guest Lineup: Tencent, Huawei & Leading Firms Share Globalization Practical Insights - 36 Kr
summary: China unveils a lineup of elite corporate guests, including Tencent and Huawei, for the Dubai Business Forum, where they will share insights on globalization.

title: US, China security experts propose nuclear-style safeguards for AI risks - Reuters
summary: Security experts from the US and China are proposing nuclear-style safeguards to mitigate risks associated with artificial intelligence.

title: Iceland-based Treble raises $18 million for its voice simulation platform
summary: Iceland-based Treble raised $18 million for its voice simulation platform, which is utilized by voice AI model developers and companies in AI wearables and robotics.

title: Treble Raises $18M for Voice AI Simulation Platform - The Tech Buzz
summary: Treble has raised $18 million to support its voice AI simulation platform.

title: Unstop acquires PerspectAI in all-equity deal to deepen AI-led talent assessment
summary: Unstop has acquired PerspectAI in an all-equity deal, aiming to enhance its AI-led talent assessment capabilities by integrating PerspectAI's technology, intellectual property, data, clients, and team.

title: Bill Gates prirovnal AI k mimozemskej inteligencii: Svetové vlády na ňu podľa neho nie sú ani zďaleka pripravené
summary: Bill Gates compared AI to alien intelligence, stating that global governments are unprepared for its implications, as AI has transitioned from labs to everyday tools for tasks like writing and programming.
