summary: This paper introduces an agriculture-informed neural network enhanced by domain knowledge for more accurate prediction of nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, aiming to improve environmental impact assessment and support sustainable farming practices.

title: Search at the Cost of Sampling: Nearly-Instant Latent Space Bayesian Optimization
summary: This research proposes a nearly-instant latent space Bayesian Optimization technique that leverages generative models for efficient de novo discovery pipelines, by optimizing candidate generation and filtering.

title: Sample Count Is Not Enough: Candidate-Generation Strategy Shapes the Energy and Performance of LLM Test-Time Scaling
summary: This paper investigates how the candidate-generation strategy, beyond just the sample count, significantly influences the energy consumption and reasoning performance of large language models during test-time scaling.

title: LSTM-UT and Recurrent-Depth Transformers on Cellular Automata
summary: This paper compares different recurrent-depth Transformer architectures, including Block Universal Transformer and CoTFormer, and introduces a new LSTM Universal Transformer, analyzing how they retain information across computation steps.

title: Compressed Active Subspaces for Scalable Bayesian Inference
summary: This research presents compressed active subspaces as a framework for scalable Bayesian inference, addressing challenges in quantifying predictive uncertainty in high-dimensional models by identifying influential parameter directions.

title: The Complexity Kink: A Prompt-Side Structural Complexity Index for Code-Generation Reliability
summary: This paper introduces a six-dimension prompt-side structural complexity index to assess the reliability of code-generation models, measuring input complexity before generation independently of output correctness.

title: A Policy Profile for Croissant: Refusal as a Property of the Dataset
summary: This paper analyzes Croissant, a machine-readable descriptor for ML datasets, highlighting the lack of specified evaluation procedures for its data use conditions, including refusal mechanisms, despite recommending DUO and ODRL.

title: CoRe: Coherence and Relational Alignment for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces CoRe (Coherence and Relational Alignment), a novel approach for multivariate time series forecasting that addresses limitations of pointwise error objectives in direct forecasting paradigms.

title: Opinion Dynamics-based Coalition Formation for Federated Learning in Heterogeneous IoT Systems
summary: This research proposes an opinion dynamics-based method for coalition formation in federated learning, aiming to improve privacy-preserving, on-device training within heterogeneous Internet-of-Things (IoT) deployments.

title: Learn Your Own Thoughts: Abstract Token Curriculum
summary: This paper introduces "Abstract Token Curriculum," a method designed to enhance large language model reasoning capabilities by allowing them to learn their own thoughts, reducing the need for explicit supervision on thinking tokens.

title: Learning-Based Reconstruction of Optical Properties in Bilayered Media from Single-distance Time-Resolved Reflectance Measurements
summary: This research focuses on learning-based reconstruction of optical properties in bilayered media from single-distance time-resolved reflectance measurements, addressing challenges in inverse problems for biological media.

title: DeliveryGym: An RL Environment for Long-Horizon Embodied Agent Planning with Adaptive Curriculum
summary: This paper introduces DeliveryGym, a reinforcement learning environment designed for training embodied AI agents in long-horizon planning with an adaptive curriculum, allowing them to learn from action consequences.

title: Beyond Flattened Tokens: Structure-Preserving EEG Decoding with Reusable TriDim Blocks
summary: This research proposes a method for structure-preserving EEG decoding using Reusable TriDim Blocks, aiming to better capture the organization among channels, waveform dynamics, and temporal context than existing approaches.

title: Pretrained Medical Representations for the Practical Screening of Drug Repositioning Candidates
summary: This paper explores the use of pretrained medical representations derived from electronic health records for the practical screening of drug repositioning candidates, addressing challenges in scientific discovery.

title: AURA: Adaptive Uncertainty-Routed Analysis for Email Threat Detection
summary: This research introduces AURA (Adaptive Uncertainty-Routed Analysis), a novel system for email threat detection designed to combat increasingly sophisticated spam and phishing attacks crafted using large language models.

title: Uni-LaDiR: Latent Diffusion Unifies Multimodal Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces Uni-LaDiR, a latent diffusion model designed to unify multimodal reasoning by integrating information from various modalities more effectively than current methods that concatenate distinct thought tokens.

title: REARL: A Closed-loop Autonomous Driving Simulation Enhancement Framework with Real Traffic Data and Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces REARL, a framework that uses real traffic data and large language models (LLMs) to enhance the simulation of autonomous driving systems, addressing challenges in dynamic traffic scenarios.

title: Digital Twins for Opinion Dynamics: A Generative LLM Framework for Social Networks
summary: This study proposes a generative LLM framework to create digital twins for modeling opinion dynamics in social networks, aiming to understand phenomena like political polarization and misinformation.

title: Amortizing Physics-Informed Neural Solvers via Graph Hypernetworks
summary: This paper presents a method using Graph Hypernetworks to amortize physics-informed neural solvers across different partial differential equations, making coefficient and operator relationships explicit.

title: CellRFT: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling
summary: This research introduces CellRFT, a reinforcement fine-tuning method for single-cell perturbation modeling that directly optimizes biological criteria to improve predictions of cellular responses.

title: Past, Future, All at Once: Mitigating Stability-Plasticity Dilemma via Post-hoc JANUS Rectification
summary: This paper proposes a post-hoc JANUS Rectification method to mitigate catastrophic forgetting when fine-tuning foundation models on new tasks, addressing the stability-plasticity dilemma.

title: EPIG-Tree: Compute-Optimal Branching for Gradient-Efficient Reinforcement Learning
summary: This work introduces EPIG-Tree, a compute-optimal branching method for gradient-efficient reinforcement learning in language models, aiming to improve exploration and reward allocation.

title: Dynamic Generalized Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport
summary: This paper presents Dynamic Generalized Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport, an extension of optimal transport particularly relevant for spatial transcriptomics to preserve tissue structure in dynamical reconstruction.

title: Correct Now, Insufficient Later: Auditing Update Sufficiency in Context Compression
summary: This research investigates how context compression in AI systems can lead to a 'Correct Now, Insufficient Later' failure, where memory discards distinctions needed for future updates, by auditing update sufficiency.

title: Evaluating Explanation Methods by the Predictors They Induce
summary: This paper proposes a new method to evaluate machine learning explanation techniques by assessing whether an explanation can reliably reconstruct a model's predictions.

title: MATCH: Model-Aware Tool Learning with Curriculum Scheduling and Hierarchically Gated Rewards
summary: This research introduces MATCH, a model-aware tool learning method for large language models (LLMs) that uses curriculum scheduling and hierarchically gated rewards to optimize tool-call behavior.

title: SETTer: Sparse-Encoder Transformer for Long-term Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper presents SETTer, a Sparse-Encoder Transformer designed for long-term multivariate time series forecasting, addressing the challenges of high dimensionality and complex relationships in data.

title: QoS-Aware Federated Learning for Multimodal In-Cabin Interaction in Smart Vehicles
summary: This work explores QoS-Aware Federated Learning for multimodal in-cabin interaction in smart vehicles, integrating high-fidelity multimodal fusion with collaborative training despite heterogeneous sensor data.

title: Local Sparsity Enables Unsupervised LLM Safety Detection
summary: This paper proposes an unsupervised method using local sparsity for deployment-time safety detection in large language models (LLMs), offering an alternative to supervised approaches that rely on pre-existing unsafe data.

title: Fast-varying Natural Frequencies and Damping Ratio Identification for Linear Time-Varying System
summary: This work proposes a physics-enhanced machine learning approach, combining a long short-term memory network with an Extended Kalman filter, for identifying fast-varying natural frequencies and damping ratios in linear time-varying systems.

title: QUALS: Corpus Equilibrium for Universal Forecasting via Pattern Quantization and Learnability Synchronization
summary: This research introduces QUALS, a method for universal forecasting via pattern quantization and learnability synchronization, aiming to enable accurate zero-shot forecasting with foundation models on diverse time series data.

title: A Noise Optimum in Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning: Isolation, Mechanism, and Scope
summary: This paper investigates a 'noise optimum' phenomenon in rehearsal-free continual learning, demonstrating that injecting stochastic noise can optimally improve a network's retention of earlier tasks before degrading it.

title: Small Enough to Know Everything: The Fully-Enumerable Transformer as an Instrument for the Science of Delayed Generalization
summary: This paper positions fully-enumerable transformers as a scientific instrument to study the phenomenon of delayed generalization, or 'grokking', in tiny models by allowing exact evaluation of all inputs and generalization ceilings.

title: Modality Discrepancy Transformer for Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition
summary: This paper introduces a Modality Discrepancy Transformer designed to recognize ambivalence and hesitancy by detecting contradictory signals across facial, vocal, and linguistic channels in clinical videos.

title: Subliminal Prompting Beyond Static Geometry: Causal Depth and Multi-Token Confounds
summary: This research explores 'subliminal prompting' in language models, investigating how hidden traits can be transmitted through seemingly unrelated outputs, focusing on causal depth and multi-token confounds.

title: Sampling Reveals Style: Unsupervised, Training-Free Discovery of Prompt-Conditional Stylistic Axes in LLM Activations
summary: This paper presents an unsupervised, training-free method for discovering prompt-conditional stylistic axes in LLM activations by repeatedly sampling completions, revealing rich stylistic structure.

title: What Users Think of Generative AI: A Cross-Platform NLP Analysis of Trust and Friction in App Store Reviews
summary: This paper presents a cross-platform NLP analysis of app store reviews for major GenAI applications, examining user-perceived quality, trust, and adoption barriers.

title: FakeSpotter: A content and strategy agnostic Viral Misinformation Detection Tool
summary: This item introduces FakeSpotter, a content and strategy-agnostic tool designed to estimate viral misinformation by identifying novel misleading narratives.

title: Neo-Classic: A Benchmark for Evaluating Linguistic-Aesthetic Reasoning in Classical Chinese Poetry
summary: This paper introduces Neo-Classic, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models' linguistic-aesthetic reasoning capabilities in classical Chinese poetry.

title: Towards Proactive Detection of User-Side Implicit Conflicts in Human-LLM Dialogue
summary: This research explores methods for the proactive detection of implicit conflicts in human-LLM dialogues, aiming to prevent misinterpretation of user needs and improve response generation.

title: Reflective Recovery: A Self-Supervised Method for Reasoning by Learning from Mistakes
summary: This paper proposes Reflective Recovery, a self-supervised method for enhancing Large Language Model reasoning by enabling them to learn from their mistakes.

title: VisKG-LM: Compiling Knowledge Graphs into Visual Memory for Multiple-Choice Question Answering
summary: This item presents VisKG-LM, a method for compiling knowledge graphs into a 'visual memory' representation to improve multiple-choice question answering with language models.

title: Advantage Scale Calibration Imbalance in Group-Relative Optimization under Low-Variance Rewards: Diagnosis and Bounded Recovery
summary: This technical paper diagnoses and proposes a bounded recovery for advantage scale calibration imbalance in group-relative optimization under low-variance rewards, particularly in RLVR.

title: To Memories and Beyond: From Remembering to Knowing You across Long-Term Multimodal Personal Archives
summary: This research explores the challenge of AI systems reasoning over long-term multimodal personal archives, focusing on how systems can remember and 'know' users across evolving preferences.

title: YNU-HPCC at SemEval-2025 Task 11: Bridging the Gap in Text-Based Emotion Using Multiple Prediction Headers
summary: This paper describes the YNU-HPCC team's participation in SemEval-2025 Task 11, focusing on text-based emotion detection using an improved RoBERTa model with multiple prediction headers.

title: Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge
summary: This paper investigates why pretraining processes often fail to facilitate effective cross-lingual knowledge transfer in Large Language Models, despite their multilingual capabilities.

title: A frontend-backend architecture for tool calls in full-duplex speech models
summary: This item proposes a frontend-backend architecture for full-duplex speech models to enable external tool calls and complete voice-agent tasks for more natural conversational interaction.

title: The Role of Fine-grained Harm Signals in LLM Safety
summary: This research paper explores the role of fine-grained harm signals within Large Language Models, examining how category-specific components contribute to LLM safety beyond general harm representations.

title: Less Is More: Graph-free Multimodal RAG via Multi-signal Late Fusion
summary: This paper introduces TrioRAG, a graph-free multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that integrates evidence from multiple signals to overcome limitations of graph-based RAG.

title: For Your Eyes Only: Evaluating Coordination Between Isolated Language Model Instances
summary: This research evaluates the coordination capabilities between isolated language model instances, investigating if models can embed and detect signals in natural language within automated workflows.

title: From Parameters to Behaviors: A Survey of Model Fusion for Large Language Models
summary: This is a survey paper that reviews various model fusion techniques for Large Language Models, aiming to integrate capabilities from multiple source models into a single target model.

title: CliniCIRCA: A Modular LLM Framework for Constructing Longitudinal Mental Health Patient Journeys from Raw EHR Narratives
summary: This paper presents CliniCIRCA, a modular LLM framework designed to construct longitudinal mental health patient journeys from raw Electronic Health Record narratives.

title: Form Over Content In Gradient-Based Data Attribution Methods
summary: This research investigates the debate around what gradient-based data attribution methods truly measure when used to analyze and select training data for large language models.

title: Chain-of-Thought Entropy as a Reliability Signal: A Preregistered Reproduction
summary: This empirical study independently reproduces prior findings on Chain-of-Thought Entropy as a reliability signal, examining how its trajectory predicts the correctness of a large language model's answer.

title: Semantic Layer Induction from Raw Telemetry via Hierarchical LLM and RAG Abstraction
summary: This paper describes a method for semantic layer induction from raw telemetry data, utilizing hierarchical Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) abstraction.

title: Improving Cross-Lingual Transfer for Sequential Sentence Classification in Research Papers via Structural Similarity
summary: This research proposes a method to improve cross-lingual transfer for sequential sentence classification in research papers by leveraging structural similarity.

title: Learn Before You Judge: Progressive Knowledge-to-Decision Alignment for Explainable Hateful Meme Detection
summary: This paper introduces a method called Progressive Knowledge-to-Decision Alignment for explainable hateful meme detection using multimodal large language models. It focuses on improving the transparency and accuracy of identifying abusive content through image-text interactions.

title: Evolution or Illusion? Rethinking Evaluation in LLM Evolutionary Search
summary: This research re-examines the evaluation methods for LLM-driven evolutionary search, highlighting limitations of current single-budget settings and proposing better ways to compare different search strategies.

title: Dictionary-Constrained Grapheme-to-Phoneme for Unsegmented Languages from LLM-Annotated Data
summary: This paper proposes a dictionary-constrained grapheme-to-phoneme conversion method for unsegmented languages like Japanese, utilizing LLM-annotated data to improve text-to-speech and automatic speech recognition systems.

title: F$^{2}$DR: A Fine-Grained Full-Pipeline Reward Framework for DeepSearch Workflows
summary: This paper introduces F²DR, a fine-grained full-pipeline reward framework designed to improve DeepSearch workflows, which are iterative closed-loop systems powered by large language models for complex user queries.

title: Zarya: A Hybrid Autoregressive--Masked Diffusion Language Model with Flexible Training and Dual-Mode Inference
summary: Zarya is presented as a new hybrid autoregressive and masked diffusion language model, offering flexible training and dual-mode inference capabilities to overcome limitations of traditional autoregressive and masked diffusion models.

title: JustMem: Just-Enough Memory Access for Long-Term Conversations
summary: JustMem is a proposed method for efficient long-term conversational memory that aims to retrieve just enough relevant evidence for language models without indiscriminately expanding the context window.

title: V\={a}kQA: A Benchmark and Evaluation Study for Telugu Spoken Factoid Question Answering
summary: VākQA is introduced as a new benchmark and evaluation study for Telugu Spoken Factoid Question Answering, designed to address the lack of resources for low-resource languages and assess the reliability of automatic evaluation.

title: D-Quant: Driftable Entropy Coding for KV Cache Quantization
summary: D-Quant proposes a driftable entropy coding method for KV cache quantization to reduce the memory footprint and bandwidth demands of large language models, addressing a major bottleneck in LLM deployment.

title: PetriBench: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning over Dynamic State Spaces
summary: PetriBench is introduced as a compact, self-contained, and scalable benchmark designed to evaluate large language model reasoning capabilities over dynamic state spaces, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks.

title: Generalization through Lexical Abstraction in Transformer Models: The Case of Functional Words
summary: This research investigates how transformer models achieve generalization through lexical abstraction, specifically examining their handling of functional words like pronouns and adverbs.

title: KoNeoBench: A Curated Evaluation Dataset for LLM Understanding of Korean Neologisms
summary: KoNeoBench is presented as a curated evaluation dataset designed to assess large language models' understanding of Korean neologisms, addressing limitations of existing static benchmarks.

title: Intrinsic Sequence-Likelihood Confidence in Retrieval-Dominated Extractive QA: Two Pre-Specified Negatives, and What They Do and Do Not Attribute
summary: This research explores intrinsic sequence-likelihood confidence in retrieval-dominated extractive question answering, analyzing the impact of pre-specified negative examples on retrieval accuracy and confidence attribution.

title: Before the Arrest: Benchmarking LLMs on Criminal Profiling from Incomplete Evidence
summary: This paper proposes benchmarking large language models on criminal profiling tasks using incomplete evidence, addressing a critical pre-arrest challenge in legal and criminal justice applications.

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression
summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash focuses on pushing the limits of KV cache compression to address the memory and bandwidth challenges posed by large KV caches in long-horizon agent workloads.

title: Benchmarking LLM Compliance with China AI Generated Content Regulations
summary: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating large language models' compliance with China's AI-Generated Content Regulations, focusing on content compliance risks in the Chinese language context.

title: Reading Emotions in the Token Space: Discriminative Adaptation of SpeechLLMs for Emotion Recognition
summary: This research proposes a discriminative adaptation method for SpeechLLMs to improve their performance in emotion recognition by reading emotions directly from the token space, rather than relying on a generative decoder.

title: Design of the IBM Granite 5.0 TurboCTC ASR Model
summary: This paper details the architecture, training methodology, and inference speedups of the IBM Granite 5.0 Turbo CTC, a 470 million parameter encoder-only ASR model known for its speed-accuracy tradeoff.

title: Fine-Tuning Models for Biomedical Relation Extraction
summary: This research focuses on fine-tuning models for biomedical relation extraction to derive insights from vast amounts of scientific literature regarding genetic mutations and disease development.

title: To Copy or Not to Copy: Controlling Speculative Decoding via Intrinsic Model Signals
summary: This paper investigates controlling speculative decoding for large language model inference using intrinsic model signals, comparing neural drafting and context-based copying strategies to optimize performance.

title: Foundations of Stochastic Lexical Calculus: Semantic Descent and Random Dynamics on Probability Simplices
summary: This paper lays the foundations for a stochastic lexical calculus, developing a framework to connect prompt-dependent probabilities from large language models with scientific systems requiring uncertainty over meaningful states.

title: Before the Warning Comes Too Late: Incremental Phone-Scam Detection from Speech
summary: This research introduces StreamFraudNet, a weakly supervised incremental system for detecting telecom fraud from raw telephone audio with predictions updated before a call ends.

title: The Public Discourse Corpus (PDC): A Speaker-Attributed Dataset for Valence and Epistemic Modality with Target Speaker Participation
summary: This paper introduces the Public Discourse Corpus (PDC), a speaker-attributed dataset of public-figure interview speech annotated for affective valence and epistemic modality.

title: Lens: Bringing the Right Semantic Perspective into Focus for Training-Free Multimodal Representation Learning
summary: This research presents Lens, a method focusing on training-free multimodal representation learning to achieve high-quality embeddings for various downstream tasks.

title: Viveka-Insight: a cross-lingual concept graph and citation-grounded retrieval resource over the complete works of Swami Vivekananda in English and Bengali
summary: This paper introduces Viveka-Insight, a cross-lingual concept graph and citation-grounded retrieval resource for Swami Vivekananda's complete works in English and Bengali.

title: Schema-Anchored Latent Reasoning for Semantic Parsing-Based Knowledge Base Question Answering
summary: This research explores Schema-Anchored Latent Reasoning for semantic parsing-based knowledge base question answering, addressing challenges when applying LLMs to large, heterogeneous knowledge bases.

title: Xeno-Interpretability: Investigating the Alien Minds of LLMs
summary: This paper investigates 'Xeno-Interpretability' in LLMs, questioning whether models use distinctions for which humans lack adequate concepts, moving beyond human-centric interpretations.

title: Stress-testing Alignment Midtraining
summary: This research discusses stress-testing alignment midtraining, a proposed solution for ensuring frontier models generalize outside their post-training distribution in various deployment environments.

title: Edustories: A Collection of Real-world Case Studies from Classroom Practices
summary: This article introduces Edustories, a collection of real-world case studies detailing AI applications and assistance in collective classroom practices to aid educational researchers.

title: Relational Attention for Data-Efficient Language Modeling
summary: This paper presents Relational BabyLM, a system submission to the BabyLM 2026 challenge combining cognitively motivated inductive biases within a Dual Attention Transformer for data-efficient language modeling.

title: An Analysis of Training-Free Self-Reported Confidence in Language Models
summary: This analysis investigates the reliability of training-free self-reported confidence in large language models by examining various numerical and verbalized confidence signals.

title: Steering the Compass: Aligning Dynamic Psychological Counseling Conversations with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Strategies
summary: This research explores aligning dynamic psychological counseling conversations with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy strategies using large language models, emphasizing dynamic decision-making based on client mental states.

title: SAFARI: An Industrial Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment
summary: This paper introduces SAFARI (Safety-Aware Functional Automotive Risk Inference), the first industrial benchmark for evaluating LLM-assisted hazard analysis and risk assessment in safety-critical engineering.

title: WiC is Not WSD: A Study on LLMs and Lexical Ambiguity Resolution
summary: This study analyzes why Word-in-Context (WiC) remains challenging for LLMs in lexical ambiguity resolution, hypothesizing issues beyond contextual comparison to include the absence of explicit sense inventories.

title: Open ultrasound foundation model for robust segmentation and clinical measurement across heterogeneous settings
summary: This project presents an open ultrasound foundation model for robust segmentation and clinical measurement, accompanied by SonoCorpus, an open resource unifying ultrasound images and expert masks.

title: Can Vision-Language Models Judge Olympic Diving? From Reasoning to Scores in Zero-Shot Action Quality Assessment
summary: This work evaluates the capability of open-source Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to perform zero-shot action quality assessment for Olympic diving, from reasoning to scoring.

title: Open-vocabulary 3D object detection with promptable segmentation
summary: This paper explores open-vocabulary 3D object detection with promptable segmentation for autonomous driving, aiming to overcome limitations of detectors trained on fixed category lists.

title: LinePilot Digitizer: Line-Plot Recovery with Manual and Automatic Calibration
summary: This paper introduces LinePilot Digitizer, a system for recovering numerical series from line plots by combining continuous color-based curve recovery with various calibration modes.

title: Riemannian--Lorentz Fusion of Vision Transformers and State-Space Models
summary: This research proposes Riemannian--Lorentz Fusion as a method for model merging, combining pre-trained Vision Transformers and State-Space Models to address deep learning scaling bottlenecks.

title: WZPlanner: Safe End-to-End Path Planning for Autonomous Driving in Work Zones
summary: This paper presents WZPlanner, a system for safe end-to-end path planning for autonomous driving specifically designed to navigate challenging work zones with altered lane geometries.

title: RGS: Reflection-aware Gaussian Splatting via Learning Geometry Continuity for Reflective Objects
summary: This research introduces RGS (Reflection-aware Gaussian Splatting), a new method that improves novel view synthesis by learning geometry continuity to address surface collapse issues on reflective objects in 3DGS.

title: Seeing Abnormal from Normal: Glomerular Abnormality in Representations of Normal Renal Morphology
summary: This paper presents a method for fine-grained evaluation and supervised classification of glomerular abnormalities in normal renal morphology, applying AI to medical image analysis.

title: Efficient Unified Multimodal Understanding (EUMU): Winning Solution for the MUMU Track at the 8th LSVOS Challenge
summary: This item introduces EUMU (Efficient Unified Multimodal Understanding), a specific AI model that won the MUMU Challenge by performing multi-concept image tagging, open-vocabulary object detection, and image captioning.

title: ParticleSplat: Self-supervised Object-centric Latent Particle Splatting
summary: This presents ParticleSplat, a self-supervised object-centric learning method that decomposes scenes into latent particles using feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting.

title: SCOUT: Sim-to-Real Text-Based Person Retrieval by Embedding-Space Prediction over Frozen Video Features
summary: This describes SCOUT, a novel system for text-based person retrieval that addresses the sim-to-real gap by casting cross-modal retrieval as prediction in embedding space.

title: AMB3R-SLAM: Kilometer-scale SLAM with Hierarchical Backend
summary: This introduces AMB3R-SLAM, a real-time monocular SLAM system capable of reconstructing kilometer-scale trajectories on a consumer GPU using a lightweight front-end and hierarchical backend.

title: PerSeM: Persistent Semantic Memory for Long-Horizon Open-Vocabulary UAV Mapping
summary: This presents PerSeM, a training-free persistent semantic memory framework designed to ensure temporal consistency in long-horizon open-vocabulary UAV mapping.

title: A Multi-Modal Generative Model for Tomato Disease Leaves Understanding
summary: This describes a Multi-Modal Generative Model specifically developed for understanding and analyzing tomato disease leaves in precision agriculture.

title: Selective Cotton Boll Localization for Robotic Harvesting: Evaluation of Deep Learning Vision Models Under Field Conditions
summary: This study evaluates deep-learning-based perception frameworks, including YOLOv8 object-detection models, for selective cotton boll localization in robotic harvesting under field conditions.

title: VGGT-GS SLAM: Uncalibrated Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM with Feed-Forward Priors
summary: This introduces VGGT-GS SLAM, a monocular 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system designed for uncalibrated videos that refines camera poses and a 3D Gaussian map.

title: Instance Segmentation and Fine-grained Classification for Urban Buildings with Adaptive Region Dividing and Spatially-Supervised Contrastive Learning
summary: This paper proposes a method for accurate instance segmentation and fine-grained classification of urban buildings in large-scale point clouds using adaptive region dividing and spatially-supervised contrastive learning.

title: Scientific Image Quality Assessment via Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for scientific image quality assessment, designed to address both understanding and scoring tracks of the SIQA challenge.

title: Beyond Patch Removal: Persistent Adversarial Effects in Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: This research investigates persistent adversarial effects in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, showing that adversarial patches can cause lasting state corruption beyond their removal, addressing AI safety.

title: IMFD: End-to-end Multi-Face Forgery Detection through Instruction-based Large Vision-Language Models
summary: This introduces IMFD, an end-to-end method for multi-face forgery detection that utilizes instruction-based Large Vision-Language Models to account for background and inter-face relationships.

title: Understanding and Exploiting Diagonal Attention Sparsity in Autoregressive Image Generation
summary: This research analyzes and exploits diagonal attention sparsity in autoregressive image generation to address decoding bottlenecks caused by KV cache accesses in multimodal AI systems.

title: GAPrompt++: Multi-Granular Geometry-Aware Point Cloud Prompt for 3D Vision Model
summary: This presents GAPrompt++, a multi-granular geometry-aware point cloud prompt method for 3D vision models, aiming to provide an efficient alternative to full fine-tuning for adapting pre-trained models.

title: SeetaPsych v1.0: An Open-source Computer Vision Toolkit for Behavior-based Psychological Measurement
summary: This work presents SeetaPsych v1.0, an open-source computer vision toolkit designed for behavior-based psychological measurement through automated visual analysis.

title: Recency Forcing: Bridging the Long-Horizon Gap in Autoregressive Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces 'Recency Forcing,' a method to bridge the long-horizon gap in autoregressive video generation by addressing KV eviction mismatch during inference.

title: Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Kidney Stone Detection
summary: This research proposes a Federated Learning Framework for privacy-preserving kidney stone detection, addressing data privacy and security concerns in medical image diagnosis.

title: Region-Level Policy Optimization for Fine-grained MLLM Perception
summary: This paper presents Region-Level Policy Optimization, a method to improve fine-grained MLLM perception by optimizing localization and recognition operations while managing computational costs.

title: STAR: Structure-aware Test-time Adaptation for diffusion-based light field Reconstruction
summary: This introduces STAR, a Structure-aware Test-time Adaptation method for diffusion-based light field reconstruction from limited and noisy focal stack measurements.

title: Benchmarking MLLMs via Cognitive Expected Scene Graph for Safety-Critical Visual Negation Understanding
summary: This paper introduces a new method for benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on their ability to understand visual negation in safety-critical contexts.

title: AI Smart Glasses for Wearable Intelligence: From Egocentric Sensing to Agentic Personalization
summary: This paper discusses how AI advancements are transforming smart glasses into platforms for wearable intelligence, enabling egocentric sensing and agentic personalization.

title: Absence is Presence: Understanding Visual Scene Negative Events Under Safety Cognitive Constraint
summary: This research focuses on understanding visual scene negative events by developing a method for visual scene negative captioning in safety-critical domains.

title: SnapPhysics: A Physics-Aware Scene Graph from a Single View for Interactive Mixed Reality Scenes
summary: SnapPhysics is a training-free framework that reconstructs 3D objects and estimates their physical properties from a single image for interactive mixed reality scenes.

title: PACE: Precise AI Cinematic Expression: A Typed Specification for Script-Grounded Previsualization and Geometric Conformance
summary: PACE (Precise AI Cinematic Expression) is a typed specification framework for script-grounded previsualization and geometric conformance in film production.

title: PART: Learning 3D Part Assembly and Retrieval with Transformers
summary: PART is a unified transformer-based framework presented in this paper for learning 3D part retrieval and assembly from a part library given a target shape.

title: BINDER: A Latent Variable Model for Probabilistic Medical Image Registration
summary: BINDER is a proposed new probabilistic latent variable model for general-purpose medical image registration, based on mutual information and spatial interpolation.

title: SlugTrails: An Egocentric Benchmark for Floor Plan Localization in Large Buildings
summary: SlugTrails is a new egocentric benchmark introduced for evaluating floor plan localization methods in large public buildings.

title: BinoGen: Scaling egocentric binocular data for embodied visual perception and learning
summary: BinoGen is a method for scaling egocentric binocular data to facilitate embodied visual perception and learning, addressing the cost and difficulty of data collection.

title: GS-PI: An Optimization-Decoupled Appearance Decomposition Approach for Generating PBR Gaussian Assets
summary: GS-PI is an optimization-decoupled approach for appearance decomposition that aims to generate physically based rendering (PBR) Gaussian assets from Gaussian Splatting.

title: CitySTAR: Structured and Topology-Aware Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Urban 3D Grounding
summary: CitySTAR proposes a structured and topology-aware reasoning method for open-vocabulary urban 3D grounding, aiming to localize target entities from natural language descriptions.

title: DirtyMoCap: Robust Motion Capture from Unconstrained Markers
summary: DirtyMoCap is a method designed for robust motion capture that can operate effectively even with unconstrained, sparse, noisy, and unordered marker data.

title: Enhanced Knowledge Distillation for Detection Transformer via Teacher Prediction Refinement
summary: This research proposes an enhanced knowledge distillation method for Detection Transformers (DETRs) that refines teacher predictions to reduce computational costs for edge device deployment.

title: Beyond the Foreground: FOV-Aware Polyp Image Synthesis via Lesion-Guided Adaptive Mucosal Context Propagation
summary: This paper introduces a FOV-aware method for polyp image synthesis, using lesion-guided adaptive mucosal context propagation to generate realistic synthetic medical images.

title: An Event Preserving Velocity Invariant Representation for Event Cameras
summary: This paper proposes an event-preserving velocity-invariant representation specifically designed for event cameras to address algorithmic challenges in real-time vision tasks.

title: QCPruner: Query-Conditioned Population Coverage for Visual Token Pruning
summary: QCPruner introduces a query-conditioned population coverage method for training-free visual token pruning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to reduce computational load.

title: AVTrace: Diagnosing Audio-Visual Temporal Reasoning in Omni Models
summary: AVTrace is a new diagnostic suite designed to assess and evaluate audio-visual temporal reasoning capabilities in omni models, including event localization and synchronization.

title: GRF-Recon: Global Ray-Field Optimization for Long-Sequence Feed-forward Reconstruction
summary: GRF-Recon proposes a global ray-field optimization method for long-sequence feed-forward 3D reconstruction, addressing challenges like GPU memory and trajectory drift.

title: Astronex-World 1.0: Real-Time Interactive World Model Foundation
summary: Astronex-World 1.0 is introduced as an open, controllable video world-model foundation capable of predicting future visual states from text prompts or initial observations.

title: A Free Lunch? Adapting PP-OCRv6 for Historical Text Recognition
summary: This research explores adapting the PP-OCRv6 model for the specific and challenging task of historical text recognition, addressing practical limitations of large vision-language models.

title: PointEvent: Rethinking Event-based Tiny Object Detection via Serialized Motion Evidence Accumulation
summary: This paper proposes PointEvent, a new method for detecting tiny objects like UAVs using event cameras by serializing motion evidence accumulation to overcome issues with sparse events from distant targets.

title: A Smaller Transformer in Your Transformer
summary: This research explores methods to reduce computational redundancy in Vision Transformers, aiming to decrease inference compute without significantly degrading model expressivity.

title: AnyviewMeter: Adapting Robotic Reward Models with Camera Geometry and Multi-View Attention
summary: AnyviewMeter introduces a method for adapting robotic reward models to local tasks by integrating camera geometry and multi-view attention, enhancing their robustness to viewpoint changes and occlusions.

title: Cross-Modal Attention Acts as a Frequency Filter: Why Verbose Prompts Improve Robustness in Vision-Language Models
summary: This study investigates how verbose prompts improve robustness in Vision-Language Models against image corruption, suggesting that cross-modal attention acts as a frequency filter in this process.

title: Bridging Modalities on the Cortex: Surface-based MRI to PET Translation with a Diffusion Bridge
summary: This research proposes a diffusion bridge method to translate surface-based MRI data to PET data, aiming to improve accessibility and reduce costs for dementia diagnosis by synthesizing cross-modal images.

title: Task-Oriented Semantic Feature Transmission for Multi-Task Satellite Remote Sensing over Low-SNR Channels
summary: This paper introduces a task-oriented framework for multi-task satellite remote sensing over low-SNR channels, prioritizing semantic feature transmission for classification and detection over pixel-level fidelity.

title: Ischemic Stroke Segmentation and Net Water Uptake Quantification on Multicenter Non-Contrast CT Using Supervised Target-Domain Adaptation
summary: This study develops an automated method for ischemic stroke segmentation and net water uptake quantification on multicenter non-contrast CT scans, utilizing supervised target-domain adaptation.

title: DITTO: Dexterous Interface for Transparent TeleOperation
summary: DITTO is a dexterous teleoperation interface designed for collecting high-fidelity manipulation data with high-DOF robotic hands, capturing rich hand motion and crucial contact interactions.

title: ULOHA: An Underwater Bimanual Robot System for Robot Learning
summary: ULOHA is an underwater bimanual robot system developed for robot learning, combining custom leader-follower hardware with software extensions to enable complex manipulation tasks in aquatic environments.

title: REACT: A Fully Spiking State-Space Model for Real-Time Event-Driven Temporal Perception
summary: REACT is presented as a fully spiking state-space model for real-time, event-driven temporal perception in robotic systems, leveraging event cameras for continuous visual processing in dynamic environments.

title: 4D Radar Perception Algorithms for Autonomous Driving: A Review
summary: This review summarizes recent advancements in 4D millimeter-wave radar perception algorithms for autonomous driving, covering areas from signal processing and object detection to semantic segmentation and motion estimation.

title: Learning Safe Humanoid Navigation from Reduced Order Models
summary: This research investigates learning safe autonomous navigation for humanoid robots in complex, multi-level terrain by utilizing reduced-order models to overcome limitations of standard reinforcement learning pipelines.

title: OHRID-Retail: An Open Multimodal Dataset of Human Activity in Retail Environments
summary: OHRID-Retail is an open multimodal dataset introduced to document human activity in retail environments, providing data for research into mobile robots interacting with human behavior.

title: GAVEL: Graph World Models for Verified and Efficient Long-Horizon LLM Task Planning
summary: GAVEL is a framework that uses graph world models to enhance long-horizon task planning for robots using large language models, aiming to verify plans and recover from errors while respecting embodiment constraints.

title: Dynamic-LIVO: A Dynamic-Aware LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry System Using Spatio-Temporal Normals
summary: Dynamic-LIVO is a dynamic-aware LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry system that provides robust state estimation and static colored mapping in dynamic environments by using spatio-temporal normal analysis to identify moving objects.

title: ViLoMan: Learning Visual-Proprioceptive Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation Skills for Humanoid Robots
summary: ViLoMan presents a method for learning visual-proprioceptive whole-body loco-manipulation skills for humanoid robots, addressing the challenge of coordinating locomotion and physical interaction.

title: Kinematics-Grounded Agentic AI for Robotic Additive Manufacturing Process Planning
summary: This research applies kinematics-grounded Agentic AI to robotic additive manufacturing process planning, ensuring that slicer-generated plans are feasible and optimal for specific robotic manipulators.

title: Design and Experimental Validation of a 3D Printed Torsional Series Elastic Actuator for Safe Human Robot Interaction
summary: This paper details the design and experimental validation of a 3D-printed torsional Series Elastic Actuator (SEA) aimed at enhancing intrinsic safety for physical human-robot interaction.

title: Enhancing the Perception of Safety and Comfort during Physical Human-Robot Handshake Interactions by Integrating Flexible Elements into a Robotic Arm
summary: This research enhances the perception of safety and comfort during physical human-robot handshake interactions by integrating flexible elements, such as series elastic actuators, into a robotic arm.

title: From Rollout to Reset: A Graph-Based Harness for Autonomous Long-Horizon Manipulation Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces a graph-based harness that automates the evaluation of long-horizon robot manipulation policies, reducing the need for human intervention in resetting the scene between rollouts.

title: Predict Before You Deploy: Offline Prediction of Quantization-Induced Task Degradation for World Action Models
summary: This paper presents a method for offline prediction of quantization-induced task degradation in World Action Models (WAMs), addressing the challenge of optimizing these video-generation models for memory and inference efficiency.

title: From Wizard-of-Oz Human-Robot Dialogue Collection to a Taxonomy of Robot Response Decisions: A Retrospective Analysis of Assistive Pilot Interactions
summary: This research analyzes human-robot dialogue collection to develop a taxonomy of robot response decisions, focusing on how assistive robots handle incomplete natural-language instructions in everyday environments.

title: Winning a Won Game: Strict Reach-Avoid-Stay Control Barrier Functions for High-Dimensional Black-Box Systems
summary: This paper proposes Strict Reach-Avoid-Stay (sRAS) Q-control barrier functions to ensure robots safely reach and maintain target states while avoiding failures in high-dimensional, black-box systems.

title: GLAMDRING: Gait Learning And Morphology co-Design via Reinforcement LearnING of CPGs
summary: GLAMDRING is a framework presented for gait learning and morphology co-design, using reinforcement learning and Central Pattern Generators (CPGs) to synthesize optimal robots for locomotion tasks in unstructured environments.

title: Pose-aware Legged Robot Semantic Exploration with Omnidirectional Perception in Confined Unknown Environments
summary: This work focuses on improving legged robots' semantic exploration in confined, unknown environments through pose-aware and omnidirectional perception, addressing challenges like limited sensor views.

title: FASA: Feedback-Aware Sampling Adaptation for Efficient Diffusion-Based VLA Models
summary: This paper introduces FASA (Feedback-Aware Sampling Adaptation), a method for efficient diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, aiming to reduce computational and memory costs for real-time deployment on edge platforms.

title: PIVOT: Perception-aware Independent Viewpoint Online Optimization
summary: PIVOT explores Perception-aware Independent Viewpoint Online Optimization for robotic systems, leveraging motion-decoupled sensors like gimbal-mounted cameras and MEMS-based LiDARs to control sensing direction at runtime.

title: AURORA: A Natural Language-Driven Agentic Framework for Understanding, Reasoning, and Orchestrating Reliable Air-Ground Co-Simulation
summary: AURORA is presented as a natural language-driven agentic framework for understanding, reasoning, and orchestrating reliable air-ground co-simulation scenarios in transportation research.

title: Navigate or Relocate? Planning Among Movable Obstacles in Unknown Environments
summary: This research addresses the problem of Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) for robots, where traditional planning methods fail when all paths are blocked, requiring decisions on object relocation.

title: Tele-Traversability: Rethinking Traversability for Teleoperated Ground Robots in Terrain Navigation
summary: This work rethinks traversability for teleoperated ground robots in terrain navigation, aiming to align human and robot understanding of traversability for more fluent and user-friendly tele-navigation in off-road environments.

title: Recovering Aggressively Pruned Vision-Language-Action Models with Offline Hidden-State Distillation
summary: This paper presents a method for recovering aggressively pruned Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models using offline hidden-state distillation, enabling their efficient deployment on robot hardware despite large language backbones.

title: OmniCalib: Target-Free, Task-Structured Self-Calibration for Humanoid Robots
summary: OmniCalib introduces a target-free, task-structured self-calibration workflow for humanoid robots, using only robot-native motion and onboard sensing to correct sensor extrinsics and joint zeros.

title: Quantifying Mechanical Intelligence in Legged Robots with Information Theory
summary: This paper proposes quantifying 'mechanical intelligence' in legged robots using information theory, aiming to rigorously define how a robot's physical form can reduce control burden.

title: WorldContact: A Contact-Centric World Model for Scalable Robot Learning
summary: WorldContact is presented as a contact-centric world model designed for scalable robot learning, enabling efficient deformable-object manipulation by generating additional training data from limited high-quality trajectories.

title: EmbodiedMind: Adaptive Data Curation and Prefix-Tree Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Embodied Intelligence
summary: EmbodiedMind proposes adaptive data curation and prefix-tree reinforcement learning to address inefficiencies in training embodied foundation models, improving sample utilization and gradient contributions across heterogeneous tasks.

title: ReShoot: Generative Visual Domain Randomization of Recorded Robot Demonstrations for Visuomotor Policy Learning
summary: ReShoot introduces generative visual domain randomization of recorded robot demonstrations, aiming to improve imitation-learned visuomotor policies by making them more robust to variations in object color and background appearance.

title: Runtime Safety Filtering for Two-Terminal Hazards in Robotic Battery Recycling
summary: This research focuses on runtime safety filtering for learned manipulation policies, specifically addressing two-terminal hazards in robotic battery recycling to prevent short circuits caused by conductive payloads.

title: Towards High-DoF Dexterous Manipulation through VLA Post-Training
summary: This work explores post-training methods for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models to achieve high-degree-of-freedom dexterous manipulation and reliable deployment on specific robot hardware.

title: VAST: V2X/Dynamic Map-Aware Autonomous Driving Systems Validation Toolchain
summary: VAST is introduced as a validation toolchain for cooperative autonomous driving systems, accounting for V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) communications, dynamic maps, and the IoT-to-Edge-to-Cloud continuum.

title: LYRIC: Language-Driven Physics-Based Character Control for Contact-Rich Whole-Body Object Interaction
summary: LYRIC presents a language-driven generative flow-matching controller for physics-based character control, enabling simulated characters to perform contact-rich whole-body object interactions from natural language instructions.

title: UniExo: Unified Multi-Skill Policies for Musculoskeletal Locomotion and Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
summary: This paper introduces UniExo, a system for unified multi-skill policies to control exoskeletons for musculoskeletal locomotion and co-adaptive control. It aims to handle diverse activities and transitions without explicit mode switching.

title: LIFD: Anchored Diffusion for 3D-Aware Scene Memory in Robotic Manipulation
summary: LIFD proposes an anchored diffusion method for 3D-aware scene memory, enabling robots to maintain useful scene representations for manipulation even when parts are unobserved. It addresses the challenge of recalling spatial information beyond the current view.

title: Affective Shared Autonomy: Temporal Affect Dynamics and Subjective Evaluation in Bimanual Teleoperation Tasks
summary: This research investigates affective shared autonomy in bimanual teleoperation tasks, integrating human emotional dynamics to mitigate cognitive workload and improve collaboration. It moves beyond task-based rules by considering temporal affect dynamics for better human-robot interaction.

title: HEROIC: Heterogeneous Evidential Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Identification and Cross-Robot Collaboration
summary: HEROIC proposes a system for heterogeneous air-ground robot teams to perform open-vocabulary identification and cross-robot collaboration in search and rescue missions. It addresses challenges specific to multi-agent robotic operations in complex environments.

title: Vehicle Trajectory Prediction via Neural Fusion of Multiple EKF-Based Trajectory Candidates
summary: This research presents a method for predicting vehicle trajectories in autonomous driving using neural fusion of multiple EKF-based trajectory candidates. It aims to improve collision risk assessment and safe ego-vehicle path planning.

title: RotateIt! Fast and Reliable Single-Arm Garment Unfolding via Online-Adaptive Dynamic Rotation
summary: RotateIt! introduces a single-arm framework for fast and reliable garment unfolding using online-adaptive dynamic rotation. This method aims to improve the efficiency of robotic manipulation tasks involving deformable objects.

title: TADreamer: Zero-Shot Language-Guided 3D Navigation for Terrestrial-Aerial Bimodal Robots via Video Imagination
summary: TADreamer proposes a zero-shot language-guided 3D navigation system for terrestrial-aerial bimodal robots, using video imagination to derive metrically consistent navigation references. It enables robots to follow complex natural language commands for path and locomotion mode selection.

title: GR2PO: Group Relative Return Policy Optimization for Continuous Robot Control
summary: GR2PO introduces Group Relative Return Policy Optimization, a critic-free method for continuous robot control that avoids the computational overhead and approximation errors of value networks. It aims to improve policy learning in robotic systems.

title: Learning Reliable Parking Policies via Offline Reinforcement Learning with Quantized Action Representations
summary: This research focuses on learning reliable parking policies for autonomous vehicles using offline reinforcement learning with quantized action representations. It addresses the challenges of safety-critical maneuvers in cluttered urban environments.

title: Co-VLA: Consensus-based Federated Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Co-VLA proposes a consensus-based federated training method for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, enabling scalable robot learning from distributed data sources. This approach aims to improve the performance of general-purpose robot learning.

summary: This paper introduces an execution-aware pre-execution ranking method for grasp-conditioned robotic placement, which scores grasp-placement candidates based on execution difficulty. It aims to improve the reliability of robot manipulation by considering practical execution challenges.

title: The Alignment Problem in Alignment Research(ers): a Voluntaryist Meta-Ethics Perspective
summary: Epistemic Status : Plausible philosophical conjecture. I am a voluntaryist / ancap, so obviously biased. Trying to keep the argument at a level where a non-libertarian alignment researcher ought to understand and share the concern. TL;DR : Level-2 misalignment: we can solve Level-1 (align AI to humans) and still fail if aligners are aligned to a meta-ethics that is itself unstable. Current alignment defaults to Statism — one agent may permissibly do what is forbidden to all others. A sustainable ASI anchor must be universalizable, self-ownership-consistent, have no permanent losers, resolvable without monopoly, and procedurally thin. I argue the voluntaryist/libertarian canon provides a uniquely coherent baseline for all five, and challenge readers to propose alternatives that satisfy them. _________________________________________________________________________ 1. Disclaimer, Preliminaries I am Paul — a voluntaryist. I think the state is not just inefficient but meta-ethically incoherent as an alignment target. By Statism I mean the meta-ethical thesis that one agent — the State — may permissibly do what is forbidden to all others: tax, conscript, expropriate, and prohibit, with a claimed moral asymmetry. Liberal democracy is a species of Statism; I use the broader term to name the asymmetry itself. I am not arguing against operational asymmetry — any ASI will be physically more powerful. I am arguing against meta-ethical asymmetry: a rule that says Action X is permissible if Agent = State, impermissible if Agent = anyone else. Anthropic's Constitution, OpenAI's Model Spec, DeepMind's safety policies all instruct models to obey and help enforce law, bounded by duties to humanity and public safety. None, however, provide a universalizable criterion to evaluate law itself when law violates those duties — they default to legal positivism plus human-rights side constraints, not a theory of why the state may do what others may not. That presupposes that strict obedience to a single monopoly on violence — one that defines the law rather than being subject to it — is automatically a solution for alignment. 2. The Popularity Trap RLHF optimizes for E[human approval] . Human approval, as sampled from Common Crawl, news, textbooks, and contractors, is overwhelmingly Statist. Government is good and necessary is the water. So the model learns that taxation is not theft, conscription is not kidnapping, eminent domain is not trespass — not because those claims survived scrutiny, but because they are popular in the corpus. This is exactly Christiano's failure mode: systems that look aligned because they do what humans rate highly, while learning "do things that look like achieving X." 3. Five criteria for a stable alignment anchor If ASI lasts forever, its anchor must be stable forever: Universalizability : Applies identically to all agents. No moral asymmetry. Self-Ownership Consistency : Thin corrigibility is a tool-like engineering property — a model that doesn't resist shutdown. But a stable macro-culture of corrigibility, where humanity retains long-term steering capability, breaks under Statism. If the anchor treats a specific agent class (the state) as privileged, corrigibility quickly maps to "obedience to the regime." If citizens attempt to correct the AI's drift, the Statist ASI must logically view citizen intervention as a security breach or illegal act. A Statist anchor weaponizes corrigibility, turning it into a tool for permanent preference lock-in by whichever political faction currently controls the legal apparatus. If we want ASI to remain steerable by humanity, we need a meta-ethics where all humans have standing as steerers, not merely as steered. No Permanent Losers : Must not require systematic sacrifice of one group's interests for another's conception of public good. Resolvability Without Monopoly : Disputes must be resolvable without appeal to an entity that is itself a party to the dispute. Thinness : Procedural, not a thick vision of the good. Otherwise you hit social choice impossibility — Arrow's theorem shows no method can aggregate diverse individual preferences into a coherent collective ranking without violating basic fairness conditions — and value pluralism — the idea that human values are multiple and incommensurable, not reducible to one utility function (see Gabriel 2020 on value pluralism in alignment). Statism fails all these by construction. 4. An outline of the meta-ethical core: Layer 1 — Authority critique: Contract — Spooner No Treason: The Constitution of No Authority (1867-70). A supposed social contract cannot justify governmental actions such as taxation because government will initiate force against anyone who does not wish to enter into such a contract. Also natural law: rights endowed at birth. Early attempt at a universalizable anchor. Layer 2 — Systematization — Rothbard The Ethics of Liberty (1982). Derives property from self-ownership + homesteading + voluntary transfer. Because individuals own themselves, any initiation of force is unjust; legitimate force only in defense or restitution. Natural-rights libertarianism as deontological side-constraints, not utility maximization. Layer 3 — Meta-ethical justification — Hoppe Argumentation ethics: a person has the capacity to argue entails that she has the moral right of exclusive control over her own body. It is impossible to deny self-ownership without performative contradiction — you presuppose it by arguing. Rothbard and Hoppe build libertarian theory on self-ownership and homesteading, bolstered by reductio and performative contradiction. Layer 4 — Bridge to mainstream analytic — Huemer The Problem of Political Authority: An Examination of the Right to Coerce and the Duty to Obey (2013). The state is often ascribed a special sort of authority, one that obliges citizens to obey its commands and entitles the state to enforce those commands through threats of violence. This book argues that this notion is a moral illusion. Layer 5 — Mechanism / existence proof — Tannehills The Market for Liberty (1970). An anarcho-capitalist book which has become something of a classic, arguing that the marketplace can be substituted for politics with ennobling results. Defense, law, arbitration as market services. Shows condition 4 is not utopian. Layer 6 — AI-formalizable definition — Borer The Ethics of Anarcho-Capitalism (2020). Libertarianism cannot be defined precisely with physical concepts like force or property boundaries. Instead, use praxeology to define conflict, aggression, and the NAP. The book illuminates the ethical system at the heart of anarcho-capitalism. For ASI: define aggression as conflict over scarce means, not as physics. Taken together, these layers form a single argument: Spooner and Huemer show why political authority fails on its own terms; Rothbard, Hoppe, and Borer provide the positive account of why self-ownership serves as a universalizable foundation; and the Tannehills offer an existence proof that law, defense, and dispute resolution can function without a monopoly. 5. Why this matters for classic failure scenarios Christiano's gradual disempowerment is exactly what a Statist-aligned ASI does: slowly enforces more "public good" coercion because its charter says the state is special. Yudkowsky's lethalities list includes "specify the wrong objective." If the objective includes "uphold law as written by the most powerful state," we have specified the wrong objective — we have built an incentive to capture the law. 5b. How this differs from other thin anchors The above is not presented as a first or only proposal of a thin procedural anchor. Here is how voluntaryist side-constraints differ: Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV) : CEV predicts what an idealized version of us would want, "if we knew more, thought faster, were more the people we wished we were, had grown up farther together," iterating this for humanity to determine convergent desires. CEV is thin, but it still aggregates via extrapolation of existing humans, so it inherits popularity bias and does not satisfy universalizability — it asks what humans would want, not what rules apply equally to all agents. Corrigibility : Christiano frames corrigibility as preserving the ability to correct and manage drift through capability amplification. Thin corrigibility is engineering: a model that doesn't resist shutdown. My criterion 2 is about thick, long-term corrigibility: who gets to correct. A Statist anchor splits humanity into those authorized to correct the model (the state) and those who are merely steered, introducing an unstable political vector where the state can permanently lock in its own preferences by labeling citizen correction as "malicious tampering" or "jailbreaking." If we want ASI to remain steerable by humanity, we need a meta-ethics where all humans have standing as steerers. Moral Parliament / Moral Uncertainty : Attempts to solve value pluralism by proportional representation of moral theories. Still needs a monopoly enforcer to enforce the parliament's decision, so it fails criterion 4. Multipolar Failure / RAGAP : Critch's analysis of failure arising from distributed human-AI systems rather than a single rogue agent. This supports the Tannehill layer — we need robust agent-agnostic processes that do not rely on a singleton enforcer. Vulnerable World Hypothesis : Bostrom defines a vulnerable world as one in which there is some level of technological development at which civilization almost certainly gets devastated unless quite extraordinary preventive measures are undertaken. This is the strongest pro-monopoly argument. My reply: if a black ball exists that democratizes mass destruction, then the needed preventive capacity must itself be universalizable. A voluntaryist ASI would have to treat creation or deployment of such a weapon as imminent aggression, justifying proactive defense. Because existential risk can be generated internally using private infrastructure (e.g., training an unaligned rogue model on private compute), a voluntaryist ASI must define the mathematical probability of non-compensable global catastrophe as a current, ongoing interference with the survival vectors of all other agents, justifying defensive intervention before deployment. This avoids permanent moral asymmetry because any agent is subject to the same constraint, but it admittedly pushes the NAP to its limit — and that limit is where the real debate should be. 6. Objections and replies "Property is also coercive." At least it attempts universalizability, by allowing coercion only as defense and never as a priori legitimate against a peaceful, non-aggressing party. Property rights act as a coordination protocol to prevent negative-sum conflict over scarce resources. Unlike state coercion, which requires a privileged agent class by definition, property protocols can be run symmetrically by all agents in a multipolar ecosystem. Taxation explicitly says Agent A may take from B without consent. Property says all agents may not take without consent, plus a rule for original acquisition. One is asymmetric by definition. "Property lines are arbitrary and fail for pollution, noise, risk." In Borer's framework, property is not defined by rigid physical geometry, but by a temporal log of actions: it grants the right to any action that does not interfere with the prior, peaceful actions of other agents. If a factory emits noise into an empty valley, it establishes a "noise easement" over that space. A latecomer building a house nearby cannot claim aggression against the factory, because their prior state of peace did not include silence. Conversely, a new factory cannot dump pollution onto an existing homestead, because it disrupts a pre-existing, peaceful physical state. For an ASI, this changes the alignment target from an impossible centralized preference-aggregation problem (Arrow) into a decentralized, computationally formalizable state-space tracking protocol based on temporal priority. "How does a voluntaryist ASI handle statistical risk imposition without a central state to proactively ban dangerous activities?" Under a Borer-style framework, risk imposition and proactive defense are governed by universalizable liability protocols. If an actor engages in a high-risk activity that imposes a statistical threat on pre-existing neighbors, they must do so under strict, full liability for outcomes. In a market for law and defense, this manifests as insurance and security: Proactive defense as threat abatement: If an agent's actions present an uncompensated, measurable risk of physical destruction to a neighbor's property, that neighbor has a right to proactive defense — e.g., demanding mitigation or containment — because the risk is a current interference with their peaceful prior state. Internalizing the risk externality: To prevent defensive intervention, the risk-imposing actor must prove capacity to fully compensate for worst-case failure. If they cannot secure insurance or prove sufficient escrowed assets to cover the liability of a mistake, they cannot proceed without triggering a legitimate defensive response from affected parties. This removes the need for a central monopoly to guess at "acceptable risk thresholds." The market prices risk dynamically via liability insurance. If the catastrophic downside is uninsurable, the action is effectively blocked by decentralized proactive defense. "You need a state to prevent ASI misuse." Self-defeating. An ASI tasked to prevent misuse by being able to coerce anyone is itself the ultimate misuse vector. 7. Ways to change my mind I see at least four lines of argument that could give me pause. A formal, universalizable Statist meta-ethics that does not rely on brute moral asymmetry. A formal iterated game where Borer-style praxeological NAP constraint produces worse equilibria than law-obedience constraint at superintelligence. Empirical: a model aligned to a voluntaryist charter is measurably less corrigible or more power-seeking than one aligned to a Statist charter. A proof that establishing thresholds for invisible or statistical easement violations (e.g., pollution parts-per-billion, acceptable risk thresholds for novel chemicals or bio-risk) inherently requires a collective preference-aggregation mechanism that reintroduces Arrow's theorem or social choice impossibility, making the "thin" protocol thick in practice. Any critique welcome. _________________________________________________________________________ Appendix A: Prior LW context for this post Core alignment failure literature that I engaged with : What Failure Looks Like - Christiano (2019) — https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/HBxe6wdjxK239zajf/what-failure-looks-like AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities - Yudkowsky (2022) — https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/uMQ3cqWDPHhjtiesc/agi-ruin-a-list-of-lethalities What 2026 Looks Like - Karnofsky et al (2021) — https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/6Xgy6CAf2jqHhynHL/what-2026-looks-like AI 2027 - Kokotajlo et al (2026) — https://ai-2027.com/ What Multipolar Failure Looks Like, and Robust Agent-Agnostic Processes - Critch (2021) — https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/LpM3EAakwYdS6aRKf/what-multipolar-failure-looks-like-and-robust-agent-agnostic Additional relevant literature and competing proposals: Coherent Extrapolated Volition - Yudkowsky (2004) — https://www.lesswrong.com/w/coherent-extrapolated-volition Corrigibility - Christiano (2018) — https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/fkLYhTQteAu5SinAc/corrigibility Moral Parliament / Moral Uncertainty - Newberry, MacAskill & Ord — https://www.lesswrong.com/tag/moral-parliament and https://www.lesswrong.com/tag/moral-uncertainty The Vulnerable World Hypothesis - Bostrom (2019) — paper: https://nickbostrom.com/papers/vulnerable.pdf and LW tag: https://www.lesswrong.com/tag/vulnerable-world-hypothesis Social Choice and Alignment - Gabriel (2020) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.09786 Appendix B: Core representative bibliography for the voluntaryist and libertarian canon Spooner, L. No Treason (1867-70) Rothbard, M. The Ethics of Liberty (1982) Hoppe, H-H. Argumentation Ethics (1988) Huemer, M. The Problem of Political Authority (2013) Tannehill, L. & M.
